title: A.B.Café
label: Coffee Shop / Café
text: Situated in the trendy and style-conscious suburb of Midsommarkransen, A.B.Café is something of a trip to the 1950s era Stockholm. The café is located just a stone's throw from Konstfack University College and is a popular spot for up-and-coming designers and artists to get a relaxed cup o' joe and a fresh snack.

title: Prinsen
label: Restaurant
text: Stockholm’s cultural elite has been dining well at Prinsen since 1897. The walls are decorated with the portraits of famous habitués. Prinsen is an excellent spot for the diner who wants to try well-prepared Swedish classic dishes in a cozy and pleasant atmosphere. Their version of Biff Rydberg is renowned, and the service is professional and personal. Guests are met by Prinsen’s own coat check staff.

title: B.A.R.
label: Restaurant
text: The Blasieholmen area has recently undergone a renaissance, with numerous exciting new establishments opening their doors. One of them is B.A.R.– a seafood grill where customers choose fish and shellfish directly from the fish tank.

title: Beijing8
label: Restaurant
text: Smart and stylish Asian fast-food restaurants that serve top quality dumplings at very good prices. The dumplings come in a variety of taste combinations and are served with Chinese teas. Quick service in a relaxed environment. Beijing8 has one restaurant in Östermalm, one in Täby, and another one at Arlanda Airport. Their dumplings are also sold in the city center at the food court K25.

title: Nationalmuseum
label: Museum
text: After five years of renovations and modernizations, Nationalmuseum - Sweden's premier museum of art and design - opened up its doors again in 2018. The new space is tailored, quite literally, to highlight the museum's enormous collection of classic art.

title: Tolv Stockholm
label: Activity
text: Below 3Arena, this entertainment complex is spread over 12,000 square meters. Bring your family or squad and challenge each other in different arcade games, sing karaoke, or try disco bowling.When you’ve had enough of activities, have a seat in one of Northern Europe’s biggest sports bars with a 200-inch LED screen surrounded by a spectator terrace fitted with VIP seats from the 3Arena.

title: Moderna Museet
label: Museum
text: Experience one of Europe's foremost collections of art from the twentieth century to today, featuring works by artists including Picasso, Dali, Derkert, and Matisse. Moderna Museet is located on Skeppsholmen island, a setting of natural beauty. The building was designed by Spanish architect Rafael Moneo.

title: Birka
label: Attraction
text: One of Sweden’s first real towns. During Viking times, Birka on the island of Björkö in Lake Mälaren was the central hub and the most important marketplace in the entire Mälar Valley. It was established in the mid-eighth century, attracting travelers from near and afar. Birka of today has a wealth of ancient remains that have been excavated and studied since the 19th century. It was designated a world heritage site by UNESCO in 1993. Birka is only open during the summer season, May-September, but can be easily reached by taking a tour with Strömma's Birka-boat from central Stockholm. The trip takes roughly 2 hours.

title: Drottningholm Palace
label: Attraction
text: Take a day trip to Drottningholm and experience a historic milieu of the highest standard. Drottningholm Palace is Sweden's best-preserved royal palace constructed in the seventeenth century, the permanent residence of the royal family, and one of Stockholm's three World Heritage Sites.The palace was constructed according to a French prototype by the architect Nicodemus Tessin the Elder, by the commission of Queen Hedvig Eleonora. Many royal personages have left their mark on the palace since then. The palace features magnificent salons from the seventeenth, eighteenth, and nineteenth centuries, a beautiful park, a unique palace theater, and a Chinese Pavilion. The imposing Baroque garden was laid out at the beginning of 1681 according to drawings by Nicodemus Tessin the Younger. The palace and the park are mostly open to visitors year-round.Drottningholms Slottsteater (the Drottningholm Palace Theater) is the best-preserved eighteenth-century theater in Europe and the only one in the world that still uses the original stage machinery on a regular basis. The theater has guided tours and performances during the summer.The palace has been the permanent residence of the present royal family since 1981. The rooms in the southern part of the palace are reserved for members of the royal family. In 1991 Drottningholm was the first Swedish attraction put on UNESCO’s list of World Heritage Sites. The easiest way to get to Drottningholm is by taking a bus from Brommaplan.

contact_text.text: Drottningholm is closed the 7-19 september on the occasion of HM the King´s 50th anniversary.

title: World Heritage Skogskyrkogården
label: Attraction
text: A place of sublime beauty and poetry. Created over a period of a quarter-century (1915-1940) on about 250 acres of pine-covered boulder ridge under the direction of the famous modernist architects Gunnar Asplund and Sigurd Lewerentz.Considered one of the most important works of the modernists, it evokes a Nordic philosophy on nature, life, and death. There are also a number of beautiful chapels and a visitor center (open May-September and October weekends). Skogskyrkogården is a UNESCO World Heritage site since 1994.

contact_text.text: Guided tours on Sundays, June - September.

title: Comics Heaven
label: Shop
text: Located in Gamla Stan, Comics Heaven is a treasure trove for comic book lovers. European adventure and sci-fi comics, Marvel and DC superheroes, manga, American indie comics, and Swedish stalwarts like Fantomen and Agent X-9. You’ll find something exciting to read in English or Swedish.

title: Ugglan Boule & Bar
label: Bar
text: Ugglan is not your typical bar, but more of an activity center for adults with a plethora of games and activities to choose from. Because sometimes a nice drink or beer is not enough. Sometimes you simply need arcade games, pinball, board games, foosball, dart, shuffleboard, boule or air hockey to go with that drink.

title: Stockholms Science Fiction Antikvariat
label: Shop
text: Travel to the faraway planets and exotic worlds of yesteryear at Stockholm Science Fiction Antikvariat. The small bookshop on Södermalm specializes in vintage editions of science fiction, fantasy and horror literature. You’ll find both great bargains as well as out-of-print rarities.

title: Pet Sounds
label: Shop
text: One of Quentin Tarantino’s favorite places in Stockholm, Pet Sounds has been serving up essential listening since 1979. The crates are full of both classics and hidden gems, from the latest indie sensations to seminal records from Kraftwerk and Dylan. Regardless of musical preferences, you’re guaranteed to find something to cater to your taste.

title: Bio Rio
label: Activity
text: Arthouse cinema Bio Rio is currently one of Stockholm's few remaining single-screen theaters from the 1940s, and the setting is uniquely preserved. Indio is a vital part of Hornstull's cultural life, with a wide offering of movies and cultural programs for all ages, including premieres, independent films, live operas, children's movies, and Sweden's first cinema bar. There is also a restaurant, that serves lunch, and dinner.

title: Zita
label: Activity
text: Vinterpalatset, Gyllene Göken, Rita, Nya Rita, and finally Zita. The movie theater on Birger Jarlsgatan 37 has been known by many names. First opened in 1913, Zita is Stockholm's oldest movie theater still in operation. During the course of its history, it's been a silent movie theater, a part of the once-mighty RI-movie empire, and an adult movie theater. Today it primarily offers a program of independent and world cinema, and once every year it screens Swedish classics with English subtitles. Zita also houses Bongo Bar, where you can grab a drink or meal before or after your movie.

title: Bio Capitol
label: Activity
text: Bio Capitol is Stockholm's newest independent cinema. Inspired by institutions like the Alamo Drafthouse in Austin, the ambition is to give moviegoers a film experience they won't get at multiplexes with a repertoire of classics, international cinema, and off-beat movies. The two screen-cinema also runs a bistro and bar, and moviegoers are welcome to order food and drinks from a small bar menu to bring into the auditorium.

title: Hey STHLM!
label: Activity
text: Ready player one! The backroom of the pool-hall RoQ is lit by the bright lights and screens of 30+ arcade machines, ready to gobble up your coins. Here, at Hey Stockholm!, you’ll find both well-known arcade classics and hard-to-find Japanese games. Test your reflexes with Ikaruga, challenge a friend in Pop’n Music, or cruise along the cloudy highland in Outrun 2.

title: Biocafé Tellus
label: Activity
text: At its peak in 1946, Stockholm had around 110 movie theaters in the city and several more in the surrounding suburbs. Today those numbers have dwindled down to around 20 in the whole Stockholm-area, mostly multiplexes. There are a few single-screen theaters left though, one of them being Tellus in Midsommarkransen. Run by a local culture society, Tellus has shown movies on a regular basis since 1920. You can still catch a movie Wednesday, Thursday or Sunday. Or if you're not in the mood, maybe just grab a coffee and a fika at the café.

title: Nåttarö
label: Excursion
text: Stora Sand on Nåttarö is the archipelago’s largest sandy beach and one of the best places to swim. The island also has a cave called Drottninggrottan. The story is that it was a hiding place for Queen Maria Eleonora in the early 1600s when she fled the court and government after the death of her husband, King Gustav II Adolf. There is a large vacation village open in the summer along with campsites and bike and rowboat rentals.

title: Grinda
label: Excursion
text: A charming island, just over an hour away by the fastest boat, via Vaxholm. A blissful archipelago setting, in a nature reserve. Good swimming in summer. Grinda Wärdshus is an inn, built-in art nouveau style, open from April to early November. Grinda has hotels, cabins, a youth hostel, and campground, plus a range of activities including kayaking.

title: Sandhamn
label: Excursion
text: An island where you can experience the remarkable maritime terrain of the outer archipelago. Sandhamn is the key meeting place for sailors and yachters, with a vibrant party scene during summer. The idyllic village, a historical sea pilot station, has an inn, hotels, the classic Royal Swedish Yacht Club, and numerous restaurants and bars. There are also many activities on the island like kayak paddling and bicycle renting. Sandhamn is also worth a visit off-season when the archipelago has returned to its peaceful natural state. Fans of Nordic Noir might recognize Sandhamn as the island where Mikael Blomkvist takes refuge in the Millenium series and as the primary setting of Viveca Sten's The Sandhamn Murders book series.

title: Utö
label: Excursion
text: A popular year-round island in the outer southern archipelago known for its beaches. Utö has Sweden’s oldest iron mines with old, preserved miner’s dwellings and a mining museum. The island also boasts the well-known Utö Wärdshus with a hotel, hostel, and restaurant, and nearby is good swimming from the rocks in Rävstavik Bay. Try renting a bike and going to Ålö Island just south of Utö. Enjoy the white sandy beach and eat delicious Swedish seafood and fish at Båtshaket. Be sure to buy a loaf of the renowned Utö bread from the bakery before the trip home.

title: Finnhamn
label: Excursion
text: Popular archipelago island to visit year round. It lies near the outer archipelago and you can get there in about 2.5 hours. A wooded island with many small bays with rocks for swimming from and perfect for hiking. There is a café, tavern, hostel, campground, and bike and boat rentals. It also has a farm shop where visitors can buy vegetables and homemade delicacies.

title: Möja
label: Excursion
text: Möja is a traditional, idyllic archipelago island lined with small villages and well-preserved harbors. There is still fishing and farming practiced here, and a small supermarket and hostel operate all year round in the main village, Berg. Don’t miss visiting the popular tavern Wikströms Fisk in the village of Ramsmora, which is run by the archipelago’s only professional fisherman. Möja is perfect for hiking and biking, but not for swimming. There are hostels, B&Bs, and several cottages for rent.

title: Gustavsberg and Värmdö
label: Excursion
text: On Värmdö you will find a rich history and a varied island landscape with well-known islands such as Grinda, Möja, and Sandhamn. The municipality is made up entirely of islands, yet you can still reach the main town of Gustavsberg in just 20 minutes. In Gustavsberg you can visit the porcelain factory, with its shop, a fantastic gallery and exhibition of glass, glassworks, and pleasant shops and cafés.

title: Fjäderholmarna
label: Excursion
text: Where the archipelago begins, only a 20-minute boat trip from downtown Stockholm. The excellent restaurant Fjäderholmarnas krog is open during the summer season, and for the julbord Christmas buffet. The popular Rökeriet restaurant and café is located by the guest harbor. Many artists have studios and stores in the center of the island. Fjäderholmarna provides a nice taste of the archipelago for people who don't have time to explore further. Boats depart from Strandvägen and Slussen during the summer.

title: Vaxholm
label: Excursion
text: Idyllic archipelago town with many well-preserved wooden houses from the turn of the last century painted in the archipelago’s typical delicate pastel tones. Vaxholm has numerous charming restaurants, cafés, and shops. And more adventurous travelers have a range of exciting activities to chose from like SUP and kayak paddling or fishing. Waxholm Hotel, with its great views of the fortress and harbor, is a classic choice for lunch or dinner, or, why not a Christmas Buffet. Vaxholm is easily accessible year-round, by Waxholmsbolagets boat traffic or by bus. If you take the bus, the trip is covered by Stockholm's public transport service.

title: Björnö nature reserve
label: Activity
text: Located on the tip of Ingarö, Björnö is a beloved nature reserve in the Stockholm archipelago. With its mix of open sea and green islands, it's popular with both hikers and swimmers. You'll find farmland, beaches, pine forests, and wetland. The nature reserve has a lovely forest trail for hikers, as well as an underwater snorkel trail and kayak-rentals.

title: Landsort
label: Excursion
text: Landsort is the name of the lighthouse and small village on the island of Öja; the Stockholm archipelago's most southern point. Öja is a long, narrow island, about 5 km (2.5 miles) long and 500 meters (1/3 mile) wide, with nice walking paths from north to south. The island’s hostel is open year-round, and it is just as exciting to visit Landsort in the fall or winter as it is during the summer. You'll get a sample of the many facets of life in the archipelago; beautiful nature, fascinating history, and a calm and soothing atmosphere.

title: Ambar vinbar
label: Bar
text: Sherry, rum, cognac, beer and orange wine. The duo behind Ambar has a passion for amber colored liquids. Primarily a bar where you can experience carefully selected nature wines and lager beer, Ambar also has a small menu of simple Japanese snacks to complement your drinks.

title: Tyge & Sessil
label: Bar
text: Tyge & Sessil, celebrity chef Niklas Ekstedt's wine café, is all about the underdogs. The wine list consists of natural wines from independent small-scale producers, mainly from areas beyond the famous regions, and made from lesser-known grapes. Don't worry if you're hungry though; there’s also a small menu of simple, fresh dishes and snacks to go with your drink of choice.

title: Katrina Ölkafé
label: Bar
text: Located on Katarina Bangata is this snug beer pub that has succeeded in the art of being both personal and trendy. The beer comes from ultralocal microbreweries, and the snacks come in great flavors. Especially the pastrami sandwiches are much talked about. In the summer there is a small sidewalk cafe.

title: Filmhuset
label: Attraction
text: The aptly named Filmhuset (quite literally Swedish for "The House of Film") is home to the Swedish Film Institute. Built in the late ’60s, the building’s brutalist architecture mirrors the daily film-related activities going on inside. Windows resembling perforations on a strip of film, elevator doors looking like make-up mirrors. In fact, the building as a whole is shaped like a camera, and – from above – it almost looks like a roll of film.In addition to being the center of the Swedish film industry, you’ll also find Sweden’s largest library with books and magazines on film. Filmhuset is also the main venue for Cinemateket; a movie club showcasing a wide program of auteur masterpieces, cult rarities, world cinema, and beloved classics.

title: Gamla Filmstaden
label: Attraction
text: When inaugurated in 1920, Råsunda Filmstaden (today called Gamla Filmstaden) was the world’s most modern movie factory. It had workshops, dressing rooms, office space, a film laboratory, film storage, a directors’ pavilion, a restaurant – and most importantly – two large soundstages. This is where legendary director Ingmar Bergman used to work, and where actresses Ingrid Bergman and Greta Garbo made their debut.Even though movies are no longer made here, the walls are still steeped in cinematic history.In total, 30 of Ingmar Bergman's movies were filmed here, including his award-winning movie debut Torment (1944). You can still see the grove behind Backstugan where Monika ran with the stolen roast in Summer With Monika (1953), and the site of the witch-burning in The Seventh Seal (1957).Today, Gamla Filmstaden is an obvious destination for film buffs and movie lovers. Guided tours, audio guides, and a café await visitors, as well as a modern multi-screen cinema.

title: Artipelag
label: Museum
text: Artipelag is a venue for art, culture, design, and delicious food, located among the pine trees of Värmdö in the Stockholm archipelago. The museum takes admission for the exhibitions but the surrounding park and nature path are free of charge. You can also enjoy a breathtaking view of the archipelago from the museum's restaurant or café.

contact_text.text: For those who like to take the scenic route, Strömma operates ferries that take passengers from Stockholm city to the museum during the summer months.

title: Huvudskär
label: Excursion
text: The group of islands named Huvudskär was a fishing hamlet, as far back as the middle ages. Situated at the southern reaches of the Archipelago, with nothing but open sea lying ahead, its inhabitants were mostly fishermen needing a simple cottage to sleep during the fishing season. After being burnt down by the Russian army in the 18th century the cottages were rebuilt, with the addition of a lighthouse and a toll station. Travel to Huvudskär might be cumbersome, seeing as it’s quite remote. But the area’s nature reserve, with beautiful and picturesque surroundings, is definitely worth a night or two at the main island's hostel.

title: Roslagsleden
label: Activity
text: Roslagsleden offers hiking trails through deep forests and coastal landscapes, with several cultural sights sprinkled along the way. The 190-kilometer-long trail starts in Danderyd just north of Stockholm city and passes by places like Domarudden, Norrtälje, and Roslagsbro before ending in Grisslehamn.The hiking trail is divided into 11 sections with plenty of swimming opportunities. The overnight stay options are many: choose between shelters, campsites, cabins, or hotels.Three places not to miss along the way are Angarnssjöängen (Section 2) which is one of the county’s finest locations for birdwatching, the idyllic red cottages at the historical environment Wira Bruk (Sections 5 and 6), and the artist and author Albert Engström’s studio (Section 11), overlooking the Sea of Åland.

contact_text.text: Roslagsleden is part of the European hiking trail no. 6, which starts in Greece and ends in northern Finland.More information in English about hiking along Roslagsleden can be found here.

title: Savant Bar
label: Bar
text: A wine bar that leads a double life as a coffeeshop during the daytime. Either drop in for a cup of craft coffee and a tasty sandwich during lunch or wait until the afternoon when Savant opens up its bar. The focus is primarily natural wines, but you’ll also find Swedish craft beer and seasonal dishes on the menu.

title: Rökeriet Fjäderholmarna
label: Restaurant
text: Located on Fjäderholmarna, Stockholm's closest Archipelago island, Rökeriet serves Swedish classics and seafood staples. It's a great place to escape and get a small sample taste of the archipelago, with just a 25-minute boat ride from central Stockholm.
mass_info: Some restaurants and cafés in the Stockholm archipelago are closed during fall and winter. Be sure to check their webpage if you're planning a visit outside of the spring and summer season!

title: Grand Hotel Saltsjöbaden
label: Restaurant
text: Built in 1893, Grand Hotel Saltsjöbaden is an imposing landmark located in the affluent suburb of Saltsjöbaden. The hotel was built by financial tycoon K.A. Wallenberg, with inspiration from luxurious French hotels like the Hotel de Paris in Monte Carlo. Obviously, it's first and foremost a hotel. But you don't have to be an overnight guest to enjoy a great dinner in the hotel's classic dining room, Franska Matsalen, with it a beautiful view of the Stockholm Archipelago.

title: Batteri Arholma
label: Museum
text: The coastal battery at Arholma was built at the height of the Cold War. Strategically placed in the northern archipelago, to protect Swedish sovereignty against soviet attacks, the installation was in use well into the 2000s, before it was dismantled. These days, the formerly top-secret military facility is a museum open to the public.

title: Pythagoras Industrimuseum
label: Museum
text: Verkstads AB Pythagoras was founded in 1898 as a factory making mechanical calculators (hence the name). When the prototype for the calculator turned out to be a dud, the company pivoted to locks, candelabras, and electric light fittings instead, and eventually developed a hot bulb engine of their own which became the main export. Gaining some moderate international success, Pythagoras was an important employer in the small town of Norrtälje, until it’s closing in 1979.These days Pythagoras functions as a museum instead, with its well-preserved factory floor, interior, and various machines giving a unique insight into the industrialization of Sweden in the 20th-century.

title: Ostmakeriet
label: Coffee Shop / Café
text: Taste artisan cheese, made in the Stockholm Archipelago. Ostmakeriet is a small dairy on Rindö, producing cheese on milk from nearby farms and artisanal ice cream from local ingredients. Either enjoy a grilled sandwich or pie in their café or pick your selection of delicious dairy products to bring home.

contact_text.text: During the summer (June to August), Ostmakeriet is open 12-17 every day. September-December, and March to May, only on Fridays and Saturdays.

mass_info: Some restaurants and cafés in the Stockholm archipelago are closed during fall and winter. Be sure to check their webpage if you're planning a visit outside of the spring and summer season!

title: Stockholm Outdoor
label: Activity
text: Stockholm Outdoor specializes in island hopping for anyone with a more adventurous side. During the summer they offer kayak, canoe, and sailing tours in the Stockholm Archipelago, either in a one-day excursion or a two-day adventure. During winter the focus is instead on hiking trips either by foot or with the help of snowshoes and cross-country skis.

title: Skärgårdens Kanotcenter
label: Activity
text: At Skärgårdens Kanotcenter you can rent a kayak to explore the archipelago on your own, or in the company of a guide! The award-winning tour operator also offers tours during the winter, and even have a hot sauna to relax in after the icy tour.

title: IBC Stockholmscharter
label: Activity
text: The best way to experience the Stockholm Archipelago is by sea. With IBC Stockholmscharter you can rent your own ship with an experienced crew and refreshments onboard, for a scenic tour at your own pace through the archipelago. Both modern and classic boats are available, for small as well as large groups.

title: Sailing Stockholm Archipelago
label: Activity
text: How do you best explore the Stockholm Archipelago with its over 30 000 islands? By boat of course. The Green Trails offers either a 1-, 2-, or 3-day sailing trip together with an experienced skipper. No previous knowledge of sailing is needed as you take to the sea and you'll get the chance to see some of the Archipelago's stunning islands, take a swim in the sea and relax on sun-warmed granite rocks.

title: Roslagen
label: Excursion
text: Roslagen is the name of the coastal areas north of Stockholm, which also constitute the northern part of the Stockholm Archipelago. Small picturesque island villages, historical sites, and untouched nature are waiting to be discovered in Roslagen. The largest communities are Norrtälje, Grisslehamn, Österåker, Öregrund, and Östhammar.Try an island tour and sail with a historical ship or paddle in a kayak. Travel down interesting footpaths in the national park, and see white-tailed eagles and seals in the outer archipelago. You can also experience Swedish history at the one-of-a-kind Walloon ironworks, Vaxholm’s fortress, the holy Birgitta’s “Finsta,” and the many Middle Age churches and museums.

title: Gålö
label: Excursion
text: The Gålö peninsula is located in Southern Stockholm and can be reached either by car or with one of several buses from Haninge station. Almost the entire island is a nature reserve with beautiful nature, forest paths, and vistas to experience. Although a great destination for a day trip to the Stockholm Archipelago, there are campings and hostels for anyone who’s planning on staying a night or two.

title: The National Museum of Science and Technology
label: Museum
text: From the very start 100 years ago in 1924, the museum has looked to the future! The premises of 10,000 square meters are filled with exhibitions and experiences about the history and the future and are open from morning to late evening. The experience arena Wisdome Stockholm with its spectacular wooden architecture takes visitors on breathtaking adventures in immersive 3D - further into space, into the fantastic worlds of computer games and the smallest components of the Universe.

title: N3rds Bar
label: Bar
text: Aside from game-themed drinks and tasty beer, N3rds Bar has a whole library of video games to keep both diehard gamers and casual nerds occupied. From timeless classics like Street Fighter 2 and Super Mario Bros., to the latest and greatest on current-gen consoles. In other words, you no longer have to choose between a night out on the town and a gaming evening at home.

title: Snickars Records
label: Shop
text: A visit to Snickars is mandatory for serious crate diggers. The vinyl record store deals mainly in House, Techno, Disco, Soul, Funk, Hip Hop. They carry new releases and deal in second-hand trading. There’s also an assortment of DJ equipment and Snickars regularly hosts in-store releases and gigs.

title: Science Fiction Bokhandeln
label: Shop
text: What do dragons, starships, vampires, and ninjas have in common? You’ll find them all at Science Fiction Bokhandeln. Since its inception, back in 1984, the bookstore has grown quite a bit, and today it stocks more than just books. Boardgames, role-playing games, comic books, movies, manga, plush toys, collectible card games and more. If you consider yourself a sci-fi, fantasy, or horror aficionado, Science Fiction Bokhandeln is definitely worth a visit.

title: Café Nizza
label: Restaurant
text: Café Nizza is a local restaurant on Södermalm, with a relaxed atmosphere and a kitchen where French cooking meets Swedish flavors. Compose your own menu for a fixed price or choose any of the dishes from the à la carte menu.

title: Local boat transport
label: Travel info
text: Traveling by local ferries is a fantastic way to experience a city built on islands. Ferries are used by both commuters and tourists wanting to take a better look around. There are ample ferry departures from Nybroviken and Slussen out to the leafy island of Djurgården and Hammarby Sjöstad. An SL Card includes the ferries from Slussen and you can also buy single tickets on the quay.

contact_text.text: More infoWaxholmsbolagetStockholm sightseeingRessel Rederi

title: V Italiano Moderno
label: Restaurant
text: V Italiano Moderno in MOOD Stockholm serves artisan pizza, pasta, and Italian small plates in the heart of the city. The menu combines classic flavors with more modern combinations, making the restaurant a popular spot for lunch, dinner, or after-work drinks.

title: 450 Gradi
label: Restaurant
text: Treat yourself to a thick Neapolitan pizza made with typical Italian 00 flour at 450 Gradi. The seaside pizzeria is located on the Lidingö, overlooking lake Mälaren, and is a great spot for meal after a day spent exploring the island.

title: Adam/Albin
label: Restaurant
text: Adam/Albin is the most ambitious restaurant project to date from chefs Adam Dahlberg and Albin Wessman. Located on Regeringsgatan overlooking the Royal Palace, the Royal Swedish Opera, and Parliament, the restaurant offers a fine dining experience centered around seasonal ingredients, precision, and warm hospitality. Spanning three floors, it combines thoughtful design with a welcoming atmosphere.

contact_text.text: Adam/Albin received its first Michelin star in 2022.

title: Agnes
label: Restaurant
text: At the cozy and quality-conscious bistro Agnes, guests quickly feel a sense of community. Come for a beer in the bar or a family dinner, or spend an evening at the restaurant. The interior decor, menu and wine list encourage flexibility when it comes to options for combining small and large plates – have a seat at a community table or choose a calmer alternative in the bar. The menu spans a broad spectrum of offerings: choose from small plates like oysters, charcuterie, and cheese, or enjoy the main course shared among friends.

title: Ai Ramen
label: Restaurant
text: One of Stockholm's best ramen bars, Ai Ramen has served mouth-watering noodle bowls, donburi, and saké since 2015. And in that time it has become one of Södermalm's most popular hang-out spots, either to grab a lunch, dinner or an evening drink. In 2019 Ai Ramen opened a second location in the center of Stockholm on Gamla Brogatan 27.

title: AIRA
label: Restaurant
text: In March 2020, Tommy Myllymäki opened AIRA, a fine dining restaurant on the island of Djurgården. The acclaimed chef wants the restaurant to be worth a detour – a clear hint to those who know their Guide Michelin. The kitchen focuses on seasonal Nordic ingredients, traditional cooking, and flavors from all around the world. Choose between à la carte or a tasting menu, depending on how much time and money you are willing to spend. In June 2023, AIRA received its second star from Guide Michelin.

title: Arc
label: Restaurant
text: Arc, a restaurant and bar on the top floor of the Blique by Nobis-hotel, was named of the best rooftop bars in the world by Forbes magazine. The menu focuses on a Korean Ssäm-style sharing menu, and the terrace offers great drinks with a stunning view over northern Stockholm. For busy parents, they also offer a nanny service to take care of your kids – free of charge.

title: Artilleriet
label: Restaurant
text: Inside the massive walls surrounding the Army Museum, you'll find this hidden gem restaurant. Open for lunch and dinner, with live jazz on Tuesdays and DJs on Fridays. Don't miss the quirky cocktail menu – or the affordable cava. Dogs are welcome too!

title: Asplund
label: Restaurant
text: Asplund takes its name from the legendary architect Gunnar Asplund who has designed the listed 1930’s building which houses the restaurant. The kitchen mixes flavors from all around the world – Asia, Europe, and the Americas – but made from fresh and locally produced ingredients. So, not only will you get the chance to try Asplund’s popular pizzas, but also get a glimpse of classic Swedish architecture.

title: At Kungsholmen
label: Restaurant
text: Neighborhood restaurant by the trio behind Petit France, inspired by New York brasseries. The Friday dinners are accompanied by live music. The restaurant also has a deli with lunches to go, sweets, and sauces.

title: Babas Burgers Högdalen
label: Restaurant
text: Why can’t the suburbs have good restaurants with reasonable prices? That’s the question the gang behind Babas Burgers and Bites asked themselves and that led them to open up their first restaurant in Rågsved. Today Babas has relocated to Högdalen, but still serves the same hamburgers that have made them a haven for burger enthusiasts from all over town.

contact_text.text: Babas has several restaurants in Stockholm: Nacka, Heron City, Kista, Sundbyberg, Fruängen and Tyresö. Visit their webpage for more info.

title: Babette
label: Restaurant
text: Babette is a restaurant that delivers pizza in the front room. The wine menu is constantly changing and carefully selected to match the outstanding pizza and à la carte options. Babette is located in the area of Sibirien in Vasastan.

title: Bar Agrikultur
label: Restaurant
text: Bar Agrikultur is the new sister restaurant of popular Agrikultur. Like its older sibling, Bar Agrikultur focuses on a fixed menu of organic, seasonal and local ingredients served in an inviting and cozy setting.

title: Bar Central
label: Restaurant
text: Bar Central is a vibrant restaurant, bistro, and bar in Södermalm, serving hearty Central European classics such as schnitzel, goulash, and apfelstrudel in a relaxed setting. Popular with both locals and visitors, it’s a natural stop for traditional comfort food with roots in Germany, Austria, and Hungary.

title: Barobao
label: Restaurant
text: Taiwanese bao, steamed buns served with various fillings, are one of the latest trends on Stockholm’s restaurant scene. Söder is home to Barobao, an innovative, trendy and affordable Asian restaurant offering fast food with an organic sensibility. A seasonal side-dish menu complements the delicious, fluffy buns. This popular hole in the wall does not take reservations.

title: Barrels Burgers & Beer
label: Restaurant
text: Hungry after a day at the The Royal Palace or Royal Armory? Why not grab a juicy burger at Barrels Burgers & Beers, just a short walk from all of Old Town's great sights. Grab a meat or veggie burger and, as you've probably guessed by the name, Barrels also has a selection of great brews to go with your food.

title: Bastard Burgers
label: Restaurant
text: Bastard Burgers started off in the northern part of Sweden and uses 100 percent renewable energy from Swedish hydropower plants. The burgers are named after cities around the world and there is also a completely vegan menu. The branch in Vasastan was the first one to open in Stockholm, in February 2018. The restaurant's rapid expansion has led to over a dozen restaurants in Stockholm.

title: Bergamott
label: Restaurant
text: Bergamott on Kungsholmen is one of Stockholm's most beloved bistros. Traditional and simple French cuisine made from fresh and seasonal produce, with a large selection of French wines.

title: Berns Asiatiska
label: Restaurant
text: Contemporary cuisine with inspirations from all of Asia is served in a well-preserved setting from 1863, with a gilded ceiling and magnificent chandeliers.In addition to Asian food, a cocktail menu with many signature drinks is offered and a worldwide wine list. On weekends, DJs provide music that creates a lively vibe.

title: Bierhaus
label: Bar
text: Walk through the doors and enter a classic German beer hall, with wooden panels, communal tables, and brick walls. At the bar, you can order your favorite of the 18 German beers on tap, or ask advice from the friendly and able staff. The kitchen serves traditional German dishes like homemade sausages, sauerkraut, and pickles, all at very affordable prices.

title: Bistro & Grill Ruby
label: Restaurant
text: Texas or Paris? The sister restaurants Bistro Ruby and Grill Ruby sit side by side in Gamla Stan, each with its own signature style reflected in the menu and décor. Choose between grilled food in US Southern down-home style, or French home cooking accompanied by wine and white tablecloths.

title: Bistro Bananas
label: Restaurant
text: To the highest degree possible, family-owned and trendy Bistro Bananas lives by the motto “something for everyone.” The menu seizes upon urban food culture with precision – from incredible pizzas to three-course vegan meals. The wood oven and kitschy neon colors meet in an unpretentious setting. Outdoor seating lines the classic flatiron building on Skånegatan in the summertime.

title: Bistro Barbro
label: Restaurant
text: Barbro is a popular and cozy watering hole for Hornstull's locals. With a menu of medium-sized Asian fusion dishes, Barbro also serves refreshing drinks both in the restaurant and the downstairs bar Under Barbro.

title: Rival's Bistro and Bistrobar
label: Restaurant
text: At Rivals Bistro, the best seasonal ingredients are used. The popular classics are always in place as well as a "Plat du jour" as a complement to the regular menu.

title: Bistro Süd
label: Restaurant
text: Bistro Süd is a modern bistro with a friendly atmosphere located near Mariatorget at Södermalm. The menu is inspired by the French kitchen, combined with Swedish produce and cooking tradition.

title: Bitza
label: Restaurant
text: Bitza serves crispy Italian pizzas but with a Middle Eastern twist and ingredients typical in Palestinian, Syrian and Lebanese cooking. Tahini, hummus, shawarma, and Palestinian cheese and the zaatar spice blend to name a few.

title: Blå Porten
label: Restaurant
text: A classic destination for Stockholmers on a weekend walk or a visit to the museums of Djurgården island. Beautiful old interior, and relaxed bohemian garden. Tempting pastries and lunch dishes with a Mediterranean touch.

title: Bleck
label: Restaurant
text: The park Lilla Blecktornsparken is home to this hidden little gem, where hipster Södermalm meets families with children and couples on dates. Situated right by the park, the lush outdoor seating area becomes a glorious oasis in summer. Those who prefer to sit inside will be well-taken care of in the new, lush, glass room with a stove. The menu is focused on smaller dishes to share. Bleck also serves brunch on weekends.

title: Boqueria
label: Restaurant
text: Both restaurant and bar, Boqueria is the obvious meeting place in the popular shopping mall Mood for a lunch, brunch, dinner or evening drink. The busy Spanish restaurant main focus is tapas and pintxos but there’s also a selection of main courses available.

title: Brisket & Friends
label: Restaurant
text: Have a hearty BBQ-meal in rain or shine at Brisket & Friends. The smokehouse is serious about their cuts of meats with briskets, ribs and pork belly smoked and seasoned in Texas-fashion, with tasty sides and cold beer. You can either visit the original smokehouse, out in the suburb of Årsta, or the restaurant in Vasastan.

title: Broms
label: Restaurant
text: Broms, located in Östermalm, is a restaurant that delivers. The combination of a delicate menu and living room setting make Broms worth a visit. The breakfast buffet is also hard to beat with home-made marmalades, muesli, and sour-dough bread. If you prefer take-out, everything from the menu is ready to go and don't miss out on the treats in the deli and the bakery.

title: Bun Meat Bun Farsta Strand
label: Restaurant
text: Started by two burger enthusiasts in 2012, Bun Meat Bun originally opened in the southern Stockholm suburb of Farsta. The hamburger joint quickly proved to be a success and today you can taste their simple but meaty burgers at several locations in Stockholm, the most central being in the K25 and City Food Hall food courts.

title: Calle P
label: Bar
text: Calle P is beautifully situated in Berzelii Park, at walking distance from the venerable Berns Sallonger, Chinateatern, and The Royal Dramatic Theatre. In other words, a great spot to enjoy a small meal and drinks before a concert or performance. During summer the open-air area is perfect to cool off with a lovely drink and a view of Nybroviken.

title: Campfire
label: Restaurant
text: During the day, Campfire is a great breakfast spot in downtown Stockholm. And during the evening it morphs into a lively bar with great drinks, a great vibe AND a literal campfire over which guests can roast a marshmallow.

title: Cirkus Restaurang
label: Restaurant
text: Located in the lush island of Djurgården in central Stockholm, the historic stage Cirkus offers a fantastic spectra of theatre, musicals, concerts and shows. Their restaurant is a creative and playful bistro inspired by the festive history of Cirkus, where they serve a variety of dishes with French, Asian and American influences. Enjoy a cup of coffee, a cocktail or a great meal in the beautifully decorated dining hall, or enjoy the sun in their open-air bar and restaurant.

title: Coco & Carmen
label: Restaurant
text: The new owners of Coco & Carmen have really managed to put their mark on this classic lunch restaurant in Östermalm. In the evening, the à la carte is swopped out for a 9 course set menu with significant influences from their rebellious restaurant Punk Royal in Södermalm. It’s trendy, crowded, and priceworthy, even though it’s everything but cheap.

title: Copine
label: Restaurant
text: Stockholm’s Copine brings a modern take on Southern European dining to the central district of Östermalm, known for its mix of restaurants, cafés and boutiques. After a full refresh, the restaurant now features a new social food bar with views straight into the kitchen – a relaxed spot for lunch, dinner or a late evening stop. The menu mixes well-liked classics, including their popular cornbread, with new dishes that add range and personality. Copine also offers a chambre séparée for groups and a generous wine list to explore. Its location on Kommendörsgatan 23 puts you close to everything while still feeling tucked away.

title: Crispy Pizza Bistro
label: Restaurant
text: Delicious and luxurious pizzas in Vasastan made from local produce. The flatbread might be traditional Neapolitan, but the toppings are anything but. Smoked pork belly, butternut squash, Bulgogi, honey to name a few.

title: Järnet
label: Restaurant
text: Yet another addition to the exciting line-up of new restaurants and gastropubs in Gamla Stan. Järnet is a favorite haunt for people looking for a glass of wine and an appetizer after work, to enjoy a simple dinner, or linger through the evening with a drink in the bar. On the menu: Tapas with a Scandinavian twist and wines for people who care about wine.

title: Delikatessen Bistro Bar
label: Restaurant
text: A cozy restaurant with a bistro feel on Södermalm. Being located inside a fire station from the early 1900s gives the restaurant a special atmosphere, the beautiful red and whitewashed floor go well with the high ceilings and the arched doorways. The French-inspired menu is carefully crafted and the staff is both friendly and helpful.

title: Den Gyldene Freden
label: Restaurant
text: In a medieval basement in the Old Town, you’ll find this classic restaurant. Owned by the Swedish Academy, which selects the Nobel Prize for literature. Legend has it that many Nobel prizes have been decided at the Academy’s regular table here. The menu offers big names in classic Swedish cooking, nowadays with interesting contemporary touches.

title: DoMa
label: Restaurant
text: DoMa started as an at home-restaurant. But as word of mouth spread about the delicious dinners and brunches (and the growing family needed to reclaim their living area) the concept moved into new digs at Nybrogatan 48. The homey living room-feeling is intact, and much of what you eat is grown on the family’s Ingarö-orchard.

title: Dr. Mat
label: Restaurant
text: A fresh vegetarian alternative serving 100% organic, gluten-free and lactose-free seasonal dishes. Enjoy salads, green pasta, and nutritious smoothies with influences from all over the world. Dr. Mat also offers a large selection of raw desserts and snacks.

title: East
label: Restaurant
text: East bar and restaurant has had its own unique personality since its inception in 1989. Asian food is served in a contemporary setting modeled on high-tech Japanese culture. The East bar often plays host to live DJ’s, and during the summer season, there is a popular outdoor dining section.

title: Ecobaren Centralbadet
label: Restaurant
text: Ecobaren is a watering hole for people looking for a healthy and organic lunch in a relaxed atmosphere. The menu is crafted with love, natural ingredients, and raw foods, all served in a green environment. And why not combine the visit with a swim or a spa treatment at Centralbadet?

title: Ekstedt
label: Restaurant
text: Well-known chef Niklas Ekstedt has created a kitchen in which food is prepared using the original methods over an open flame. The superb quality and artisanal excellence are familiar from Ekstedt's other restaurants, along with awareness of the sources of the ingredients and elements of Scandinavian cuisine. The ambiance is warm, welcoming, and rustic, expressed in natural materials.

contact_text.text: Ekstedt was awarded its first star in the 2013 Guide Michelin.

title: Ellery Beach House
label: Activity
text: Elegant yet cozy. The Ellery Beach House is a hotel, spa, beach club (Stockholm's first, in fact), and a conference center, though all visitors are welcome for a drink at the Bally Bar or a meal at one of their restaurants. Palmer's offers Mediterranean-flavors with ingredients from the Greek archipelago and Lebanon, while The Coco Beach Club goes all-in on a Cali-style menu.

title: Eriks Bakficka
label: Shop
text: After 30 years in the neighborhood of Östermalm, Eriks Bakficka reopened last fall with a new kitchen. Not to worry, classic dishes like Biff Rydberg and Toast Skagen are still on the menu and the atmosphere is just as welcoming as before. Eriks Bakficka is a sister restaurant to Gondolen, and run by celebrity chef Erik Lallerstedt.

title: Etoile
label: Restaurant
text: Etoile means “star” in French, and the restaurant was indeed rewarded with a Michelin star in February 2020. Etoile offers a playful set menu of 20 courses. Open for dinner Tuesday-Saturday.

contact_text.text: In 2020, Etoile received it's first star in Guide Michelin.

title: Falafelbaren
label: Restaurant
text: Take your meal to go if you are not lucky enough to get a seat in this hole-in-the-wall-sized restaurant. Freshly fried falafel is, of course, the hero on the menu but you can also choose from traditional dishes like börek. The food is made to order and definitely worth the wait.

title: Farang
label: Restaurant
text: One of the best Asian restaurants in Stockholm can be found on Norrmalm. Farang will envelop you in its very own world on the ground floor of the old factory space, Stockholms Elektricitetsverk (Stockholm Electric Works). The industrial feel remains, but now features simultaneously rustic and modern design elements with soft lighting from enormous lamps. You will find a cocktail bar, a huge open kitchen and community tables. The food is served according to the southeast Asian mindset: everyone shares the dishes placed on the table. Beautiful ingredients and genuine craftsmanship unite here to form a cozy and unique culinary experience.

title: Flippin' Burgers
label: Restaurant
text: Before opening Flippin' Burgers, the owner traveled around the US in search of inspiration on how to make the perfect burger. After returning home, he crowdfunded the restaurant and got started on his burger-quest. Now, many connoisseurs agree that he excelled. Soon Flippin' turned out to be a success and to better accommodate the ever rising demand, Flippin' Burgers have now moved to a larger location but keep serving mouthwatering hamburgers and Ben & Jerry's milkshakes.

title: Folii
label: Bar
text: The wine bar Folii is the brainchild of sommeliers Béatrice Becher and Jonas Sandberg. Combining their many years of experience and expertise, the bar offers an ever-changing wine list depending on their new discoveries, and a menu to compliment their current favorites.

title: Frantzén
label: Restaurant
text: In 2016, renowned chef Björn Frantzén moved his luxurious restaurant from Gamla Stan to Klara Norra Kyrkogata in downtown Stockholm for a new and unique dining experience. The restaurant is located in a renovated 19th-century townhouse, where 23 guests change rooms and floors as they work their way through the fixed fine dining menu.

contact_text.text: In 2018, Frantzén became the first restaurant in Stockholm to gain three stars in Guide Michelin.

title: Gastrotek Zink
label: Restaurant
text: The classic restaurant Zink Grill has left Norrmalm for Östermalm and become Gastrotek Zink. Regulars don’t have to worry though: The head chef is the same and the grill still plays the leading role. Stockholmers come here for a quick breakfast before work, a bustling dinner, or one last drink at – you guessed it – the zinc bar counter.

title: Geronimos FGT
label: Nightclub
text: In the basement of the legendary Blues and Jazz club Stampen, you’ll find the considerably spicier Geronimos FGT. Besides being a rock club and concert venue, Geronimos FGT offers a menu of southern American classics and spicy Mexican food.

title: Giro
label: Restaurant
text: Giro is the result of a genuine collaboration based on like-minded values between Nobis and one of the world's oldest pizzerias Da Michele. With inspiration from classic pizzerias in Naples and ingredients selected with extra care, Giro creates pizzas to love.

title: Goma
label: Restaurant
text: Goma is Sweden's first Asian gastropub. It opened in October 2020, just around the corner from sister restaurant Miss Voon. Come for lunch (to stay or to go), an afternoon meeting, dinner, or a late drink. No reservations drop-in only.

title: Gondolen
label: Restaurant
text: Having been closed for renovation for several years Gondolen made a comeback, under new management, in October 2023. The new menu fuses exclusive and elegant ingredients with beloved comfort food like ratatouille and fish gratin. The view overlooking Gamla Stan, Djurgården, and the waters of Saltsjön, is still one of the best in any Stockholm restaurant.

title: Göteborg
label: Restaurant
text: Seasonal and fresh food served in a great setting at the waterfront of Hammarby Sjöstad. The menu at Göteborg (the restaurant, that is) is in constant flux, but with an affinity for delicious seafood. And just like the town of Göteborg, you can reach it either by boat or tram.

title: Greasy Spoon
label: Coffee Shop / Café
text: This is a great brunch spot from breakfast to dinner, offering a menu of British classics with a modern twist. At Greasy Spoon you can have your eggs benedict any time of the day, together with the sound of the jukebox or even a Bloody Mary.There are four Greasy Spoon venues: at Tjärhovsgatan 19 and Södermannagatan 53 on Södermalm, at Hagagatan 4 near Odenplan in the Vasastan district, and at the Playhouse Theatre, close to Stockholm Central Station.

title: Grill
label: Restaurant
text: A vast array of ingredients and a huge number of barbecue techniques, with inspiration from five continents. The interior is playful and imaginative, to say the least, with nine different styles, spanning from hunting lodge to Versailles.

title: Grodan
label: Restaurant
text: Originally named La Grenouille, Grodan bowed under the pressure of its regulars who had a hard time pronouncing its French name. Their influence didn’t stop there, which has made Grodans menu and interiors one of the most beloved and well-known in the Stockholm restaurant scene since Grodan opened its doors for the first times in 1985.

title: Restaurang Häktet
label: Restaurant
text: This old prison is a place to escape to, rather than from. Whether you're looking for a nice meal or to party like a prisoner, with three bars and an interesting Stockholm crowd, this is the place for a night out. Häktet is also one of few bars on Södermalm that closes at 3 am.

title: Hallwylska
label: Restaurant
text: Hallwylska restaurant and bar may be one of the most beautiful inner courtyards in Stockholm. This is the place for dinner and drinks or just some refreshments after a visit to the Hallwyl Museum – or even lunch with a palace view. Open during summer months only.

title: Hermans
label: Restaurant
text: Using organic ingredients, over 60 spices and inspiration from cuisines all over the world, Hermans sets out to prove that "vegan" doesn’t mean "boring". The buffet is completely vegan. In addition, the restaurant boasts a panoramic view of the entire inlet to Stockholm. In the summer there’s plenty of room in the shady garden.

title: Hillenberg
label: Restaurant
text: South European classics meet Swedish flavors and interior design at Hillenberg. The restaurant, located on Östermalm, is run by celebrity chef Niklas Ekstedt and has a close partnership with Ekstedt's wine café Tyge & Sessil. In other words: great food and great wine!

title: Hjärtat på Torget
label: Bar
text: Torget is the obvious meeting place for Stockholm’s gays. Many people stop here during the night because of its central location in Gamla Stan. At Torget, you can also get updates on the latest and tips on what there is to do in Stockholm.

title: Hornhuset
label: Restaurant
text: Hornhuset is a hip, trendy and popular venue with restaurants, bars and clubs on three floors, plus a rooftop patio that is open in summer. Each floor has its own theme and the atmosphere is usually exuberant in the popular premises in Hornstull, Södermalm. On weekends, be smart and arrive early to beat the lines.

title: Hötorgshallen
label: Shop
text: The first Hötorgshallen stood on this site in the 1880's. Today delicacies from all around the world share the space in Hötorgshallen. Go on a gastronomical journey, and browse through the market booths.

title: Husmor Lisa
label: Restaurant
text: At Husmor Lisa they want you to feel at home. The restaurant calls its menu Fine Home Dining - classic Swedish everyday dishes but with a luxurious twist, enjoyed in a setting that feels homey and cozy. Situated on the picturesque island of Resarö in the northern archipelago, Husmor Lisa uses seasonal ingredients either grown by local farmers or in the restaurant’s garden.

contact_text.text: Husmor Lisa is only open during the summer months.

title: Ichi
label: Restaurant
text: The sister restaurant of Barabao, Ichi, is a Japanese fusion restaurant that delights guests with a fixed menu with smaller dishes. The award-winning restaurant has become quite a hotspot for the residents of Södermalm so a booking well in advance is recommended.

title: Il Tempo
label: Restaurant
text: Il Tempo is one of Södermalm's most popular Italian restaurants, serving staples of the Apennine Peninsula like pizza, pasta, and classic chicken and fish dishes. And of course a large selection of wines and Italian spirits.

title: Josefina
label: Restaurant
text: A popular and well-attended summer club and restaurant on the green island of Djurgården, a stone's throw from the Nordic Museum. Josefina offers an exotic environment with palm trees, waterfront views, and a large sun deck. Here, you can enjoy a drink, have dinner or dance to the latest house music. Open May-September.

title: K25
label: Restaurant
text: A modern, urban food court a touch above the ordinary. You will find high-quality, inexpensive dishes from all over the world. A popular lunch place among office workers in central Stockholm. Sit down at one of the long tables and get to know the locals.

title: Kalf & Hansen
label: Restaurant
text: On Mariatorget Square on Södermalm, you’ll find lunch restaurant Kalf & Hansen, run by a father and son team. The menu consists of a fine offering of Nordic, organic fast food, centered on beef, fish, and vegetarian quenelles served with salad and tasty sauces. The interior design is simple and tasteful, just like the food. Kalf & Hansen also has a lunch restaurant at Bolinders plan 3, Kungsholmen.

title: Karamellan
label: Restaurant
text: Karamellan has been serving classic Swedish cuisine and fika since the 19th century. With its proximity to one of Stockholms three UNESCO World Heritage Sites, it’s the perfect place to cap off your visit to Drottningholm Palace and treat yourself to a delicious meal.

title: KB, Konstnärsbaren
label: Restaurant
text: The distinguished Konstnärsbaren ("Artists' bar") prepares Swedish traditional cuisine and delicacies with love and care. Beautiful bar, separate from the main restaurant, with murals. A classic meeting point.

title: K-Märkt
label: Restaurant
text: K-märkt is located inside the culturally historic Garnisonen building. It has its own bakery and is run by celebrity pastry chef Daniel Roos, beverage expert Jens Dolk and chef Hanna Normark. The restaurant aims to unify fine dining and large-scale production as a single concept. The menu changes constantly and is guided by the available ingredients, which are purchased the same night. The craftsmanship of the restaurant is utterly clear, and the enormous venue offers exciting architecture with a colorful industrial feel. Up to 1,000 guests can eat lunch or gather for an evening event here.

title: Kommendören
label: Restaurant
text: Relaxed, personal and cozy. Kommendören on Östermalm is a pleasant neighborhood restaurant with a bar that is equally lovely. The menu is based on the staff’s personal favorites and varies from month to month with flavors from the US, France, and Sweden. White tile and wooden interiors provide a sense of harmony without superfluous ornamentation. Enjoy a leisurely evening here; you will definitely be back again.

title: Lådan
label: Restaurant
text: Housed in a raw - almost industrial - setting with cement floors and plywood walls, Lådan (or The Box) is sister joint to the super popular Flippin' Burgers. Lådan is a large beer hall and slider restaurant with the same love for simple street food of the highest quality as its older sibling.

title: Landet
label: Restaurant
text: Classic, seasonal traditional dishes meet French cuisine and flirt with the rest of the world. Landet is a well-known spot at Telefonplan, 10 minutes from City. Popular, unpretentious, industrial and welcoming, this is a place to which people regularly return each weekend to eat, hang out in the bar or dance the night away at the club on the second floor. The interiors are designed by students from the University College of Arts, Crafts & Design, and the space used to be a post office.

title: Långa Raden – Hotel Skeppsholmen
label: Restaurant
text: The idyllic island of Skeppsholmen is situated just a stone's throw from the hustle and bustle of the city, but still in the heart of downtown. Classic Hotell Skeppsholmen and its restaurant Långa Raden are situated in a park-like area at the water's edge, in a setting that has been preserved since the 17th century. The dining room serves traditional Swedish flavors with style, and in the summertime, you are welcome to take a seat on the patio. Or why not combine a walk around the island with a stop for coffee?

title: Långbro Värdshus
label: Restaurant
text: Långbro Värdshus offers a quiet and relaxed setting for a delicious lunch, dinner or brunch away from Stockholm’s busy city center. The modern inn is located on the southwestern outskirts of town and also gives you a chance to explore typical Swedish 1960’s architecture in the surrounding suburb of Fruängen.

title: Långholmens Wärdshus
label: Restaurant
text: On leafy Långholmen, Långholmen's Wärdhus is housed in an old country estate from the 17th century. In the historical environment lie a restaurant, a hotel, a conference and a museum.In the restaurant, you can eat traditional Swedish food prepared with local ingredients for lunch and dinner. On weekends, brunch is also served, and in the bar Finkan you can order something nice to drink.Throughout the year, traditional Easter, Martinmas, and Christmas menus are served. When summer comes, the park opens for patrons wishing to eat and drink outside.

title: L'Avventura
label: Restaurant
text: L'Avventura's is located on the premises of a former movie theater which is hinted at both in its name (having a namesake in Michelangelo Antonioni's 1961 masterpiece) and in its stylish and grandiose main dining room. The menu consists of classic dishes covering the whole Apennine peninsula. The restaurant's ambition is simply to take Italian dining in Stockholm and bring it to a whole new level.

title: Le Rouge
label: Restaurant
text: Brunnsgränd 2-4 is an address that has been associated with food for centuries. It's gone from being a fish market hall during the Middle Ages to a potato storage house in the 18th century and wine house in the 19th century. Today it's the Moulin Rouge-inspired restaurant Le Rouge. The menu is both Swedish and international and the impressive wine cellar has something delicious to offer for every pallet.

title: Lilla Ego
label: Restaurant
text: Lilla Ego is a neighborhood restaurant in Vasastan, where the love for Swedish food shines through in every dish. The two owners are award-winning chefs who serve luxurious food, at a very reasonable price and in a cozy and informal environment.

title: Lily's Burger
label: Restaurant
text: Lily’s Burger doesn’t just serve you great hamburgers, shakes, and fries. Started by Swedish actors Mahmut Suvakci and Joel Kinnaman, the burger joint lets you enjoy a plate of Americana in a cozy 50’s dinner. Stalls with leather sofas, neon lights and of course a jukebox or two.

title: Lisa Elmqvist
label: Restaurant
text: Since 1926, Lisa Elmqvist has been a restaurant associated with first-class fish and seafood. Located in the beautiful Östermalmshallen food hall, the restaurant supplies patrons with well-prepared food made from delicacies from the sea. There is also a wine bar and a deli shop.

title: Loopen
label: Bar
text: A relaxed atmosphere and West Indies feel attracts both landlubbers and seafarers to this boat club. Take a seat in a lounge chair under one of the artificial palms and watch the boats dock. The restaurant serves light snacks as well as hearty meals. Lots of fish and shellfish but also American-style meat dishes. A Caribbean oasis at the foot of Liljeholm Bridge.

title: Lux Dag för Dag
label: Restaurant
text: A couple of years ago, reputed gourmet restaurant Lux on the island of Lilla Essingen re-opened with a more simplistic and affordable concept. Close to nature, Scandinavian flavors and local produce is however still the main focus. Cozy atmosphere and secluded location with Lake Mälaren nearby.

title: Luzette
label: Restaurant
text: In the middle of the bustling central station, you will find this light and spacious oasis, with a beautiful décor and pleasant atmosphere. Luzette serves brasserie-style cuisine of high class, but there are also plenty of seats if you just fancy a coffee. There is also a deli with ready meals, bread, and sweets.

title: Lydmar
label: Restaurant
text: Lydmar’s homey living room, with its unfailing sense of style, has won the hearts of Stockholmers. A broad spectrum of dishes is served in the restaurant, extending over all international borders, as if you were in the home of a good friend.

title: Magnolia
label: Restaurant
text: Magnolia is situated just a stone’s throw from Monteliusvägen, the popular viewpoint on Södermalm. Their specialty is bao, a Taiwanese bun steamed and stuffed with various delicious fillings. Pick one on offer from the menu, or compose one yourself. There is also a selection of dishes from East Asia with typical Japanese, Chinese and Thai flavors.

title: Mälarpaviljongen
label: Bar
text: A verdant oasis with a restaurant, bar, and alfresco section, located on the pier, waterfront and a barge at Norr Mälarstrand with a stunning view of the waters of Riddarfjärden. Atmospheric, cozy local restaurant and high-spirited bar with great music. Open during the summer season only.

title: Mäster Anders
label: Restaurant
text: Pleasant local eatery on Kungsholmen that dates from 1905 and has preserved the turn-of-the-century style in features including the beautiful tiled floor. The menu is Swedish and French-inspired and dominated by beautifully prepared meat dishes.

title: Matateljén
label: Restaurant
text: Beloved restaurant Matateljén has settled into Stockholm's up and coming area Slakthusområdet, where its creative approach to seasonal cooking continues to evolve. The vibrant space is centered around an open kitchen designed as several individual stations. The kitchen offers a four-course set menu with either seafood or meat as the guiding theme, while the à la carte options allow for a more flexible visit.

title: Matbaren
label: Restaurant
text: Matthias Dahlgren's Matbaren likes to keep it relaxed and informal. This bistro, housed in Grand Hôtel on Blasienholmen, uses the very best of fresh seasonal produce, to create a vibrant menu of medium-sized dishes and well-paired wine and beverages. Matbaren serves lunch Monday through Friday and dinner Monday through Saturday.

title: Meatballs for the People
label: Restaurant
text: Meatballs for the People is a restaurant, bar, and deli in Stockholm's vibrant Södermalm area, dedicated to the Swedish meatball. The menu features more than a dozen variations, from the classic with cream sauce to elk, wild boar, salmon, and vegetarian options. A lively, rustic setting where you can sit down for a meal or pick up meatballs to go.

title: Meno Male
label: Restaurant
text: Not only are Meno Males delicious Neapolitan pizzas made from typical tipo flour and traditional Italian ingredients like fior di late, prosciutto cotto and Portobello mushroom. The restaurant’s pizza oven itself was made by craftsmen in Napoli and later shipped to Sweden, to make sure every plate keeps the highest crispy pizza standards.Meno Male has several locations in Stockholm, including Mariatorget, Nytorget, Kungsholmen, Östermalm, and Vasastan. Outside the city center, you’ll also find Meno Male in Sundbyberg.

title: Misshumasshu
label: Restaurant
text: Misshumasshu is a lively restaurant, bar, and brasserie that now fills an entire neo-renaissance arcadein central Stockholm. Historic architectural details meet a modern dining space centered around a social bar. The menu draws inspiration from East Asia with clear Japanese influences, offering shareable dishes alongside familiar lunch options. Open from lunch until late in the evening.

title: Nalen Restaurang
label: Restaurant
text: Located in the renowned Nalen, a classic nightclub with roots dating back to the swingin' 20’s, Nalen Restaurang is a place to catch a delicious meal before the evening's concert. Fresh and seasonal ingredients on a classic Swedish menu that strives to serve you sustainable food. They also serve a Jazzbrunch on Saturdays during selected periods of the year, where you can enjoy food and jazz at the same time.

title: Nook
label: Restaurant
text: Nook serves its well-known mix of Nordic flavors and Asian influences in Stockholm's vibrant Södermalm district. The kitchen works with seasonal ingredients and keeps a thoughtful, sustainable approach at the center of what they do. The set three-course menus can be paired with a range of small snacks, and larger groups can enjoy a more private setting in the chambre separée "Glashuset".

title: Nya Carnegiebryggeriet
label: Bar
text: A modern artisan brewery and restaurant in a former lightbulb factory called Lumahuset, in Hammarby Sjöstad. From a collaboration between Brooklyn Brewery and Carlsberg come classical brews with a modern twist. Enjoy the gorgeous space, have a bite to eat, and try the house brews. The outdoor patio opens during summer.

title: Nybrogatan 38
label: Restaurant
text: Breakfast, lunch, dinner, or drinks - Nybrogatan 38 is open from morning till late. The menu combines Scandinavian classics with Mediterranean influences, served in a relaxed and lively setting. A social spot in Stockholm's Östermalm district where food, drinks, and music come together throughout the day.

title: Nytorget 6
label: Restaurant
text: Nytorget 6, which is in the trendy SoFo section of Södermalm, offers classic Swedish food with influences from Southern Europe. Here you can eat well morning, noon and night. Start the day with a croissant or a bowl of porridge, or finish off the evening with a planked steak or lobster omelet. The atmosphere is cozy with friendly staff. There are two cocktail bars above the restaurant section and a dance hall and small theater in the basement. The restaurant's owners operate several other restaurants in Stockholm including Meatballs for the People and Nybrogatan 38.

title: Nytorget Urban Deli
label: Restaurant
text: Urban Deli Nytorget is located in the heart of Sofo on Södermalm. Here you'll find everything from breakfast and lunch to coffee breaks or after-work drinks. In the deli and shop, you'll find not only cheese and charcuterie, but also ready-made dinner kits, single-portion meals, and freshly baked bagels. During summer, a large outdoor seating area opens up. You can also find Urban Deli in Sickla, on Sveavägen, or in Hagastaden.

title: Omaka
label: Restaurant
text: Omaka is a brewery, restaurant, bar, and beer garden created by Sweden's youngest brewmaster Hedda Spendrup. The restaurant has an open kitchen concept, where head chef Christian Siberg has composed a menu with modern dishes to pair with every beer brewed in the building. The spacious bar has large windows overlooking the brewery. Omaka's slogan for their beer is 'Taste before style' – but with the new place, we'd say they've got both.

title: Operakällaren
label: Restaurant
text: A classic. Sweden's most famous dining room, in the same building as the Royal Swedish Opera. A magnificent setting, with views of the water across the Royal Palace from the terrace bar. Dine on first-class international delicacies, presented with bold, contemporary flair. The legendary Nobis wine cellar is a wine lover's magic cave.

contact_text.text: Operakällaren has one star in Guide Michelin.

title: Operakällarens bakficka
label: Restaurant
text: Classic mini-bistro and food bar with well-made traditional Swedish dishes. Part of the Operakällaren’s food palace. Very popular for lunch. No reservations, so come early or late.

title: Östermalm Market Hall
label: Shop
text: Östermalm Market Hall has been an institution ever since it opened in the beautiful brick building on Östermalmstorg in 1888. Stroll around the counters packed with fresh fish, meat, sweets, and traditional delicacies or have a seat at one of the many restaurants or wine bars for some people watching. Östermalmshallen houses 18 traders, many of which have been here for generations.In March 2020, the market hall re-opened after several years of renovation. The original star-shaped floor plan has been reinstated, there are three easily accessible floors, and visitors can enjoy several new stores and restaurants.

title: Paradiso
label: Bar
text: Cozy bar with a menu of light vegetarian dishes on their menu. The bar, located close to Mariatorget, also has one of the finest collections of rum in town.

title: Pelikan
label: Restaurant
text: Pelikan provides a glimpse of Stockholm in the old days when there was a beer café on every corner. Classic Swedish home fare is served in a rustic beer hall with high ceilings, where the atmosphere is relaxed, the food is affordable and the crowd is a mix of people. Pelikan is a long-time favorite of many in the city’s culture crowd.

title: Phil's
label: Restaurant
text: The first Phil's Burger opened up in 2014, and since then new joints have popped up all over the city – Danderyd, Gärdet, and Fältöversten to name a few locations. Phil's hamburgers are made from carefully selected ingredients, with buns from their own bakery, and they offer both vegetarian and gluten-free options.

title: Pocket by Pontus
label: Restaurant
text: Simplicity and style define the concept at this French-Swedish bistro, located opposite Mall of Scandinavia. Pocket by Pontus offers fast quality lunch and take away, and is also open during events at Friends Arena.

title: Portal
label: Restaurant
text: Award-winning chef Klas Lindberg offers a food experience with loads of heart and culinary joy – Portal is a familiar and casual restaurant with high ambitions. The menu combines French and Nordic cuisines and features ingredients from all over Sweden. The pleasantly unpretentious light wood decor creates a cozy atmosphere.

title: Proviant
label: Restaurant
text: A little big-city restaurant or a big local eatery? Food is prepared with curiosity along the theme: classic dishes, modern tastes.

title: Råkoko
label: Restaurant
text: Råkoko, located at the beautiful 17th Åkeshofs Castle, lies just a short walk from Åkeshov metro station. The name is a play on words underscoring the manor's late baroque-interior, as well as the restaurant's, focus on healthy and fresh produce. Guests are treated to plant-based food – with fish and meat as an added option – made from locally produced ingredients.

title: Reggev Hummus
label: Restaurant
text: Reggev Hummus on Ringvägen is all about the delicious dip made from chickpeas and beans. Although having a few meat dishes, a large part of the Middle Eastern menu can be enjoyed by vegetarians and vegans alike.

contact_text.text: You'll also find Reggev at a second location on Döbelnsgatan 51 in central Stockholm.

title: Restaurang AG
label: Restaurant
text: AG is the chemical symbol for silver and the name stems from the fact that this trendy and popular industrial-chic restaurant on Kungsholmen is set in an old silver factory. Despite its somewhat off-beat location and the fierce competition, AG immediately became a meeting place that attracted ’everyone’ and a major topic of conversation when it opened its doors in 2011. Specialising in meat, which is tenderized on site in a large fridge that can be inspected as you take your seats.

title: Restaurang Hantverket
label: Restaurant
text: “Hantverk” literally means “craft” in Swedish, and Restaurang Hantverket emphasizes just that; the delicate craft of cooking. The best seasonal ingredients are chosen to highlight authentic Swedish and rustic flavors and the interior concept strives to be just as cozy and homey.

title: The Restaurant  - Fotografiska
label: Restaurant
text: Combine a visit to one of Stockholm's most popular museums, Fotografiska, with a dinner at its award-winning restaurant. The vegetarian menu at Restaurangen puts in-season and locally produced vegetables front-row-and-center with added flavors from the animal kingdom. All dishes on the menu are available without meat or fish, so be sure to let your waiter know if you're vegan or vegetarian. The restaurant works hard to be a zero-waste restaurant and received Guide Michelin's sustainability certificate in 2020.

title: Rolfs Kök
label: Restaurant
text: Rolfs Kök has become a modern restaurant classic. Its founder, Rolf, wanted an open kitchen in order to be in contact with the guests. He was one of the early people to bring in well-known Swedish architects to create the right environment. Jonas Bohlin and Thomas Sandell were given nearly a free hand, and the result was well thought out, timeless and contemporary. Rolfs Kök is a successful combination of warm personal service, outstanding wines and well-prepared food based on fine ingredients.

title: Rost
label: Restaurant
text: Rost is a charming place reminiscent of restaurants in The Village. Go here for the warm atmosphere, the organic food, tasty pizzas and live music on stage – or to fix up your motorcycle!

title: Sally Voltaire & Systrar
label: Restaurant
text: Calling themselves a food-spa, Voltaire serves modern vegetarian food complemented by fish and seafood. The restaurant is located in the Åhléns City department store and is a bright and relaxed oasis for busy shoppers. There is also a store selling everything from organic tea to soap and clever tools for the kitchen.

title: Scandwich
label: Restaurant
text: The people at Scandwich are serious about their bread. The restaurant serves up finger-licking-good sandwiches, both for meat-eaters and vegetarians, spilling over with fresh ingredients and delicious dressings.

title: Smak
label: Restaurant
text: The flavors are the stars here! The inventive restaurant concept is based on having guests select three, five or seven flavors, which correspond to appetizers of the same size. The food comes from all corners of the globe. The drinks work the same way – small glasses customized to each dish. Well-known DJ’s often take a guest turn at the bar, and the beverage list follows the same flavor scheme as the restaurant.

title: Snack Bar
label: Restaurant
text: Snack bar is a fast food restaurant created by renowned fine-dining chefs. Focus lies on kebab the French way, with fewer ingredients than regular döner and sauces based on mayonnaise, and with the Baguette Américain as their crown jewel.

title: Sollidens restaurang
label: Restaurant
text: This iconic restaurant at the open-air museum Skansen has a breathtaking panoramic view of Stockholm. For the 2026 season, renowned restaurant group Stureplansgruppen has been entrusted as the new restaurateur and creative partner of Restaurang Solliden.

title: Soyokaze
label: Restaurant
text: Batjargal Ochirbat’s Soyokaze has been the talk of the town since its opening in late 2016. The small 12 seat restaurant serves its exclusive sushi Omakase-style, roughly translated “I trust you”. In other words, the menu is up to the chef who makes and serves the exclusive sushi one at a time.

title: Spanjorskan
label: Restaurant
text: Spanjorskan is a lively Spanish restaurant in Stockholm, inspired by regional cooking from across Spain. The menu centers on shared plates, seafood, and classic flavors, suited for both casual drinks and tapas-style dinners. A social spot where food and conversation naturally come together.

title: Stadshuskällaren
label: Restaurant
text: Everyone who doesn’t have the advantage of being invited to the Nobel ceremonies can still sample the food at Stadshuskällaren, which offers all of the Nobel menus that have been served since 1901. The restaurant is located in Stockholm City Hall (where the annual Nobel banquet is served in the Blue Hall). The cellar vault provides a classic atmosphere.

title: Stallmästaregården
label: Restaurant
text: A stone's throw from the city in Haga Park on the shore of Brunnsviken lake is the eighteenth-century Stallmästaregården inn. Classic Swedish home fare is served here in a Gustavian setting.

title: Strandbryggan
label: Bar
