In winter, The Green Trails offers Nordic ice skating after dark with headlamps, a beginner-friendly cross-country skiing course, and a winter wildlife safari with a tipi tent, cooking over an open fire, and a short walk in the dark. The tours highlight Stockholm’s easy access to nature – from sailing and frozen lakes to forests, wildlife, and food cooked outdoors.

title: The Nest
label: Aktivitet
text: Situated in the middle of Stockholm, at the top-floor of the Downtown Camper hotel, The Nest is a wellness oasis in the heart of the city. Open to hotel guests and locals alike, The Nest features an outdoor rooftop pool, a sauna, yoga and other fitness activities, and a bar serving delicious mocktails and cocktails.

title: The Wooden Bike Tour
label: Activity
text: Experience Stockholm while using a quite unique kind of transportation: a hand-crafted wooden bicycle. The Wooden Bike Tour lasts two hours and takes you through the heart of Stockholm, to all the most important landmarks in the city.

title: True Nature Sweden
label: Activity
text: True Nature Sweden specializes in guided tours and soft adventures around Stockholm; kayaking, hiking, ice skating and more. Take anything from a five-hour mountain bike ride in the forests of Nacka to a week's worth of kayaking in the beautiful Stockholm Archipelago.

title: Tyresta nationalpark
label: Activity
text: Tyresta National Park, 40 minutes from the city center, is one of the largest untouched woodlands in Sweden outside the alpine areas. The area has a beautiful virgin forest and was made a national park in 1993.The park has a 30-kilometer perimeter and a wide variety of unique plants and animals. Pack a picnic and take a walk in the wild, magical forest. Stop to pick berries or swim in one of the lakes.There are a café and a farm shop in Tyresta By and buildings from the 18th and 19th centuries. Also worth seeing are the exhibits at Naturum (Nationalparkernas hus). The building is shaped like a map of Sweden and is characterized by its eco-friendliness and natural materials.

title: Ullna Golf Club
label: Activity
text: Ullna Golf Club was created by golf legend Jack Nicklaus and Swedish sports icon Sven Tumba. The golf course is often listed as one of the best in Sweden and is, above all, appreciated for its beautiful location by the lake Ullnasjön. The compact 18-hole course has attracted a number of celebrities over the years – former US president Bill Clinton, rock star Alice Cooper, and professional golfer Tiger Woods to name a few.Ullna Golf Club is completely cashless. It is a 30-minute drive north from Stockholm city. The golf restaurant serves breakfast, lunch, à la carte, and takeaway. Since August 2019, there is also a paddle club with two outdoor courts on the premises.

title: Upplandsleden
label: Activity
text: Hike the 500 kilometers from the bays of Mälardalen in the south all the way up to Dalälven archipelago in the north. Or, select one of the 31 sections or 14 circular routes. Upplandsleden is a hiking trail that cuts through the counties of Stockholm and Uppsala. Two popular spots along the trail are Kolarmoraån (Section 9), a river with great canoe trails, and Färnebofjärden National Park (Section 18-20), with its islands and shores. There are wind shelters along most sections and even a number of cabins that are free to use and available on a first-come basis. Some sections also have birdwatching towers.For those who have hiked Upplandsleden already and can't get enough, a tip is to try out Vikingaleden (the Viking trail), which is part of S:t Olavleden and connects Upplandsleden with Roslagsleden, another popular hiking trail close to Stockholm.More information in English about hiking The Uppland Trail can be found here.

title: Yasuragi
label: Activity
text: Japanese baths, rejuvenating activities, different treatments, and a very pleasant restaurant are offered here. Yasuragi is not only a spa - it's a holistic experience in an environment inspired by the best from Japan.

title: ABBA The Museum
label: Museum
text: ABBA The Museum is more than just a museum. Sure, the permanent exhibition is chock full of ABBA memorabilia like stage outfits, instruments, gold records, awards, and much more. But it’s also an interactive experience that invites you to sing, dance, mix music and become the fifth member of ABBA on their big stage.

title: Accelerator
label: Museum
text: Science and art meet at Accelerator, an exhibition hall for contemporary art. The venue, located at Stockholm University, highlights cutting-edge artists and features collaborations with the University's different faculties.

title: An open invitation to Stockholm
text:
We invite people from all around the world to visit Stockholm. People we admire, those we can’t understand, the friendly, the noisy, and the well-behaved. Lovers, haters, and hesitators.
 
Welcome to Stockholm, whoever you are!

title: ArkDes
label: Museum
text: ArkDes on Skeppsholmen is a place for architecture and design. Explore inspiring exhibitions, creative activities, a café, and a unique library with rare collections. Admission is free all summer, and there’s something for all ages to enjoy.

title: Army Museum
label: Museum
text: Follow men, women, and children through Sweden's history of war and peace. Roam from the 16th century to the present day among dramatic, full-scale scenes and original artifacts in temporary and permanent exhibitions. Don't miss the Trophy Chamber with its unique spoils of war and trophies. Learn more about Raoul Wallenberg and his deeds during World War II. Audioguide in English. Free entry for all visitors on Tuesdays 5 - 8 pm. Artilleriet, the museum restaurant next door, is also worth visiting.

title: Baltic Sea Science Center
label: Attraction
text: Discover what lurks beneath the surface in the waters of Stockholm. The Baltic Sea Science Center at Skansen is both an aquarium and an exhibition about the challenges facing the efforts of preserving the wildlife of the Baltic Sea. Admission is included in the ticket for Skansen.

title: Bergius Botanic Garden
label: Attraction
text: A botanical garden beautifully situated at lake Brunnsviken. A paradise for plant-enthusiasts with thousands of trees, shrubs, and herbs from around the world. The famous Victoria House (open May-September) has the world’s largest water lily. Exotic plants thrive in the Victoria House and Edvard Anderson Conservatory. Café, shop, and restaurant. The outdoor parts of the garden are admission free.

title: Berwaldhallen
label: Attraction
text: Berwaldhallen, one of the two major concert venues in Stockholm, is home to both the Swedish Radio Symphony Orchestra and the Swedish Radio Choir. The two ensembles are among the best in the country within their respective fields, reaching far beyond the borders of Sweden. The hall was opened in 1979 and the building itself is unique in both architecture and setting.

title: Boat to Drottningholm Palace
label: Activity
text: Board a century-old steamer and sail to world heritage site Drottningholm, the private residence of the Swedish Royal Family. Travel time 60 min on Lake Mälaren offering beautiful scenery. Café and restaurant.

contact.address: Stromma - Ticket shop Klara Mälarstrand, Stockholm, Sweden,
contact.label: stromma.com

title: Bonniers Konsthall
label: Museum
text: Bonniers Konsthall is a contemporary art venue in central Stockholm, known for spotlighting new voices and unexpected perspectives. Housed in a distinctive triangular glass building designed by Johan Celsing Arkitektkontor, it presents leading Swedish art—with a particular focus on emerging artists—alongside significant international exhibitions.The venue is rooted in the Maria Bonnier Dahlin Foundation, founded in 1985 by Jeanette Bonnier in memory of her daughter Maria. The foundation awards annual grants to young artists. There’s also a shop and a café on site.Free admission for visitors under 26 and job seekers, and for everyone on Fridays.

title: Brunkebergs tunnel
label: Attraction
text: Brunkebergs tunnel is a 231 meters long shortcut for cyclists and pedestrians through a ridge in the city center. It is located between David Bagares gata and Tunnelgatan and turned out to be a difficult task for the engineers back in 1884. Two years later it was ready to welcome the Stockholmers. A classic Instagram spot in Stockholm.

title: Brunnsviken
label: Park
text: The park areas around Brunnsviken lake are part of Nationalstadsparken, the National City Park. They’re popular for picnics, swimming, and recreation.The area features a beautiful rolling park setting, a botanical garden, cafes, palaces and several buildings of historic interest. Haga Park, on the western shore, was laid out between 1771 and 1793 on the initiative of Gustav III. The park has promenade streets along the shores and beautiful avenues. Many buildings of historic interest are located here: Gustav III’s pavilion, the Copper Tents, Haga Castle and the Butterfly House Haga Ocean. The Haga Park is one of the leading examples of English parks in Sweden.As its name implies, Bellevueparken on the southern shore is situated high above the parks and Brunnsviken lake, with a view over these features. The studio and museum of the sculptor Carl Eldh are also located here. Attractions on the eastern shore include the Bergius Botanic Garden and several boat clubs, as well as the Swedish Museum of Natural History.

title: Bryggartäppan
label: Park
text: The Bryggartäppan public playground is a reminder of how Södermalm looked during the late 19th -and early 20th-century. Replicating a Stockholm workers-neighborhood, the small wooden houses (including a workshop, a smithy, and a factory building) create a unique and exciting environment for children to discover. There's also a cute café during the summer serving waffles, coffee, and ice cream.

title: Bus sightseeing with Strömma
label: Activity
text: A bus is a relaxing way of getting around Stockholm in comfort while your guide talks you through the highlights. Stay seated all the way or hop on and off as you fancy.

title: Carl Eldh's Studio Museum
label: Museum
text: Visit the unique wooden building from 1919 and enjoy a sheltering environment with a panoramic view of Brunnsviken and the Haga Park. Carl Eldh's Studio Museum houses several hundred sculptures by one of Sweden's most prominent sculptors. Also temporary exhibitions. Carl Eldh's Studio Museum is mainly open during summertime and offers guided tours in English once a day.

title: Children's library at Kulturhuset
label: Activity
text: On the fourth floor of Kulturhuset at Sergels Torg, you can spend many hours together with the kids. The imaginatively decorated area - a second living room for many Stockholm kids - includes a large library full of books in 50 different languages and for all ages. Find a comfy corner to read your favorite book or discover brand new worlds of literature.

title: Drottningholm Court Theatre
label: Attraction
text: One of Europe’s most well-preserved 18th-century theatres. A unique attraction with its original scenery, 200-year old stage machinery, and interior decoration virtually untouched by the passage of time. Guided tours in various languages several times a day.

title: Färgfabriken
label: Museum
text: Färgfabriken has been a platform for contemporary art, architecture, urban planning, and design since 1995. The name, meaning 'the color factory', refers to the history of the building. During the late 1800s and early 1900s paint, soap, and other artistic materials were produced within the same walls. Färgfabrikens Kafé serves fika, lunch, and brunch. Located on Liljeholmen.

title: Fjällgatan
label: Attraction
text: Historic environment located high up on the edge of a cliff with a fantastic view of the city. Fjällgatan’s Kaffestuga café is charming and popular.The blocks around Fjällgatan, Stigbergsgatan, Mäster Mikaels Gata, Fiskargatan, and Södra Teatern are lined with well-preserved wooden buildings from the 1700s on one side and a magnificent view of the other.

title: Folkoperan
label: Activity
text: With constant innovation and much-discussed performances, Folkoperan has established itself as one of Stockholm’s most exciting venues, and new visitors are regularly drawn to the opera house. The ensemble offers artistic fashion, high quality and moving productions. The beautiful space was originally a premiere cinema in the 1920s and it shares a wall with cozy Folkbaren, where you can enjoy a glass of cava, little delicacies, or the full Opera menu. Don’t miss the balconies offering views of the lobby and mingling opera attendees.

title: Fotografiska
label: Museum
text: Fotografiska is an international meeting place for photography. In addition to ever-changing exhibitions, the premises also host a souvenir shop and an award-winning restaurant. Photography courses are also organized here. From the café on the top floor, you can enjoy excellent coffee and one of Stockholm's absolute best panoramic views.The museum is a favorite among visitors and Stockholmers, much thanks to its accessibility – Fotografiska is open late every day of the year!

title: Gripsholm Castle
label: Attraction
text: Located in Mariefred, a picturesque town on Lake Mälaren, this renaissance castle offers romantic grounds, a fallow deer nature reserve and collections of furniture, handicrafts, and interiors from four centuries. Including Gustav III´s theatre and the Swedish National Portrait collection.

title: Gröna Lund's Amusement Park
label: Activity
text: Experience the joyful and magical world of Gröna Lund, Stockholm's amusement park. A day spent at Gröna Lund is a memorable one, whether you dine in one of the restaurants, compete in the mini-games, enjoy a live concert, or go on one of the 30 exciting rides. Gröna Lund is open from late spring to September. The park is also open during the Swedish Autumn break and Halloween.

title: Gustav III's Museum of Antiquities
label: Museum
text: NOTE: The Museum of Antiquities is open to pre-booked groups only from May through September, and is closed for the rest of the year. The museum holds the collection of classical sculptures purchased by King Gustav III during his journey to Italy (1783–84).This is Sweden’s oldest public art museum, recently renovated and housed in its original location in the Royal Palace.

title: Gustav III's Pavilion
label: Attraction
text: One of the finest examples of late 18th century Swedish Gustavian style located in beautiful Hagaparken park surroundings. The Pavilion was built as a home for King Gustav III and with an interior decoration completed 1792, the year of the king's death. A major part of the pavilion´s original furniture is still in situ. Guided tours only.

title: Haga Park
label: Park
text: Part of the Royal National City Park, the lush Haga Park (or just Haga) is situated just north of Stockholm in the suburb of Solna. Founded by the monarch Gustav III in 1780-1797, Haga is Sweden's foremost example of an English landscape park, and one of Sweden's most popular recreational areas. It's also the site of many historical landmarks. The Chinese Temple, The Turkish Kiosk, and The Royal Burial Ground are all found in the park. Within the park is also Haga Palace, the residence of Crown Princess Victoria and her family.

title: Hornsgatspuckeln
label: Attraction
text: The advent of the car posed a problem for city planners in Stockholm in the early 20th century. Many of the city’s streets were narrow and ill-suited for motorized transport, Hornsgatan being one of them. Consequently, the buildings along the southern parts of Hornsgatan had to be demolished and their lots paved over with tarmac, to accommodate a wider two-way street for cars and city trams. The raised part of southern Hornsgatan – Hornsgatspuckeln - is what’s left of buildings closest to old street.Today Hornsgatspuckeln (“The Horngatan hump”) is known for its many art galleries and historically important buildings. It’s also a great place to start your Sunday walk, with its close proximity to the scenic Monteliusvägen.

title: Humlegården
label: Park
text: Humlegården is a green oasis a stone's throw from nightclub mecca Stureplan, in the middle of the exclusive Östermalm district.Here you can see businessmen in suits eating brown-bag lunches on the grass when it's warm and sunny, but also lots of young families and dog owners. In the beginning, the park was a royal garden established by Johan III, who grew fruit, spices, and hops. "Humlan" has been a public park and a popular spot to relax since 1869.The park includes a large playground area, a skateboard ramp, Surfer's summer restaurant, and Omnipollos Flora, a summer biergarten. A statue of the flower king Carl Linnaeus stands in the middle of the park, and the National Library of Sweden is right next to Stureplan.

title: Ice hockey
label: Activity
text: Of all team sports, ice hockey is probably the one most closely associated with Sweden. With multiple World Cup and Olympic-medals in their cabinet, both Sweden’s women's –and men’s national team is a force to be reckoned with out on the ice. And SHL (Swedish Hockey League, the top-tier league in hockey) is consistently ranked as one of the greatest in the world. The most prominent clubs in Stockholm are Djurgården and AIK. For more info on the teams and current season visit SDHL.se.The hockey season starts in September and lasts to march. Tickets can be bought either at the arena on game day, through the different clubs’ web pages or (depending on the team and arena) through Ticketmaster, Stockholm Live and Friends Arena. International games and tournaments are almost always played at Avicii Arena.

title: Ivar Lo's Park
label: Park
text: Ivar Lo's Park is one of Stockholm's most beloved public parks, yet a hidden gem. Overlooking the northern shore's of Södermalm, along scenic Monteliusvägen on Mariaberget, Ivar Lo's is also a great viewpoint and perfect spot for a summer picnic.

title: Junibacken
label: Attraction
text: The Story Train takes you on an amazing journey through the magical fairy tale world of Astrid Lindgren. Meet Mardie, Emil, Karlsson on the Roof and many others. Experience a treasure trove of Swedish children’s books through playful exhibits and a well-stocked children’s bookstore. Restaurant with a great view.

title: K. A. Almgren Silk Weaving & Museum
label: Museum
text: K. A. Almgren silk weaving is the only still active silk weaving mill left in the Nordic region. Here, silk fabrics and ribbons are woven on original machines in their original factory environment from the 1860s. The museum gives an insight into the history of the company, silk production in Sweden and the place of women in our industrialization - all seen through Almgren's micro perspective.The history of the silk weaving industry reflects the rise and fall of the Swedish textile industry, from the 19th century to today. Here, present day and history meet through textile craftsmanship.

title: Kulturhuset Stadsteatern
label: Attraction
text: Kulturhuset Stadsteatern is Stockholm's arts and culture center. The imposing multistory building has something for everyone: live theater, exhibitions, libraries, seminars, events, and a cinema. It's a popular hangout during the day (especially among moms and dads on parental leave) and has several restaurants and cafés that are great for lunch, fika or dinner before a show.

title: Långholmen
label: Park
text: This idyllic island is a popular spot for picnics, swimming, and recreation for Stockholmers and visitors alike, but this wasn’t always the case. From the eighteenth century until 1974, Långholmen was a dreaded prison island. The old prison has become a popular hostel with a prison museum. There are also beaches, open-air stages, charming buildings and a nice allotment garden area on Långholmen. The island is also home to Mälarvarvet (The Mälaren Yard), one of Stockholm’s oldest shipyards, and a small Bellman museum with a café. There is a wonderful view from the east side of the island over Riddarfjärden and Gamla Stan.

title: LGBT+ Day Tours
label: Activity
text: With StandOut Travel Day Tours you will explore Stockholm and learn about Sweden’s LGBT History in a unique way. Choose from various tours designed for your interests. Are you a Viking or an ABBA lover? Meet new friends and explore yourself!

title: Liljevalchs Konsthall
label: Museum
text: One of Stockholm's most attractive exhibition settings, showing art and design. A recurring feature is the popular Vårsalongen (Spring Salon). There is a shop where you will find Liljevalch's own products. A restaurant/café with a garden is located in conjunction with the museum.

title: Marabouparken
label: Park
text: Marabouparken is one of Sweden’s best-preserved functionalist settings. In the park, there is a collection of sculptures as well as a gallery with exhibitions of contemporary art. Their restaurant alone is worth the trip.

title: Millesgården
label: Museum
text: Here, art, history and nature meet. Millesgården was created by sculptor Carl Milles and his wife, artist Olga Milles. It offers a unique environment that includes a large sculpture park, the artists' home, and a museum with rotating exhibitions. Visitors can walk through lavish terraces adorned with sculptures and fountains created by Carl Milles, and enjoy the view of Stockholm’s inlet. In the artist’s home, you can see the studios, and on one of the lower terraces is Anne’s House, furnished by Estrid Ericson and Josef Frank from Svenskt Tenn. Millesgården also has a restaurant and café.

title: Monteliusvägen
label: Attraction
text: A 500-meter long (quarter-mile) walking path with a magnificent view of Lake Mälaren, Stockholm City Hall, and Riddarholmen, especially at sunrise and sunset. The path is lined with charming houses on one side and a beautiful view on the other. There is, of course, a safety rail on the path, but be careful in the wintertime when parts of the path might be a bit slippery.

title: Mulle Meck Park
label: Park
text: Based on the beloved children's books, the Mulle Meck (Gary Gadget in English) park is an exciting and inventive public playground for kids of all ages. Visit Gary's garage, take a ride in his rocket or play in any of the unique jungle gyms. And who knows, maybe Gary and Buffa will stop by while you're there?

title: Museum of Ethnography
label: Museum
text: At the Museum of Ethnography, you will encounter museum objects and voices from different places and times, providing perspective on what it means to be human. Personal stories and social issues take center stage as conversations flow freely between inside and outside – from thought-provoking exhibitions to activities in the lush museum park. There's room for play and seriousness, personal creation and reflection. Free admission for everyone younger than 19 years!

title: Museum Tre Kronor
label: Museum
text: In this museum, in the cellars of the Royal Palace, remnants of the Tre Kronor Castle, destroyed by fire in 1697, are exhibited. See sections of defense walls raised in the 1200s along with artifacts rescued from the flames and hear the whole story of Tre Kronor.

title: Musikaliska Kvarteret
label: Activity
text: Musikaliska Kvarteret, the musical palace built in 1878 by the Nybrokajen quay was previously home to Blåsarsymfonikerna, the brass symphony orchestra, and Länsmusiken, Stockholm County orchestra. Today it's a place with various venues, among them the beautiful concert hall, and bars for music, art, and genre-crossing happenings in both expected and unexpected forms.

title: Nordiska museet
label: Museum
text: Learn about life in the Nordics for the past 500 years at Nordiska museet (The Nordic Museum), Sweden's largest museum of cultural history. Discover a variety of exhibitions on fashion and textiles, furniture and interiors, china and table settings, folk art, jewelry, photography, trends, and traditions. In 2024 Nordiska opened its new permanent exhibition 'Nordic Life' where many of these objects are exhibited for the first time.Audio guides are free of charge and can be downloaded to your smartphone.

title: Observatorielunden
label: Park
text: The noise of the city seems infinitely far away in the grove on the hill. Observatorielunden is a green oasis only a stone’s throw from the throbbing pulse of Drottninggatan. Exactly as the name implies, there’s an observatory in the park that goes back to the 1700s. One wing, from the end of the nineteenth century, contains Kafé Himlavalvet, known for its delicious waffles and toppings from a special waffle menu. The café and its outdoor seating area are open all year except for January.

title: Ocean Bus
label: Activity
text: Ocean Bus is a unique sightseeing tour, where you get the chance to experience Stockholm onboard an amphibious bus, that runs on land as well as on water. The tour is 60 minutes, passes by many of the city´s most well-known attractions, and is guided in English. The starting point in Strömgatan by the Royal Opera. Children are allowed from 3 years old.

title: Open Top Tours
label: Activity
text: Hop on and off as many times as you like. The ticket is valid 24h and takes you to the city’s most famous sights. Comfortably seated in an open top double deck bus you are guided by headphones. Buy the ticket on board or online.

title: The Parliament House
label: Attraction
text: A prime example of Sweden's openness is that Riksdagshuset – the Parliament House – is open to anyone wishing to attend a debate, public hearing, or a study visit. You can visit Riksdagshuset to learn how Sweden is actually run and Swedish political history. Tours are free of charge but can only be booked on-site.

title: Postmuseum
label: Museum
text: The only museum in Sweden showing the postal and philatelic history, and how the Swedish Post works today. In Stockholm, the museum has become a favorite among children, much thanks to the interaktive Postis (where children can play post office) and the Treasury.After major renovations, the museum reopened in the fall of 2024 with new exhibitions and the AVI restaurant.  The shop carries – obviously – Sweden's largest selection of stamps. Free admission for everyone under 18 years.

title: Prästgatan
label: Attraction
text: Prästgatan is a picturesque street with beautiful houses in the Old Town. The street is mentioned as early as 1586. The name (Priest Street) comes from this being where many priests from the Stockholm Cathedral and the German Church lived. In the corner of Prästgatan/ Kåkbrinken, there's an actual rune stone from 1100 in the wall. For obvious reasons - a favorite spot for Instagrammers.

title: Prince Eugen's Waldemarsudde
label: Museum
text: Prince Eugene's former home is one of Sweden's most popular art museums. Visit the prince's reception rooms and see his collection of early 20th Century Nordic art as well as temporary exhibitions. A flower and sculpture garden surrounds the museum.

title: Rålambshovsparken
label: Park
text: Rålambshovsparken on Kungsholmen is a popular park for activities during the summer. The park is located between two popular residential areas, with a great view over Riddarfjärden, City Hall, and Gamla Stan. People come here to play soccer, boule, beach volleyball, softball or visit the skate park. During the summer you can also take part in an aerobics session, or take a swim in the waters of Lake Mälaren.

title: Red Sightseeing: by bus and boat
label: Activity
text: Discover Stockholm by bus or boat with Red Sightseeing. The travel pass gives you 24 hours of fun allowing you to make your own itinerary and getting the most out of your Hop-on Hop-Off experience. The tours are entertaining and informative with digitally recorded commentaries in 14 languages. Red Sightseeing also offers an hour-long boat tour around Djurgården "The Royal Bridges & Canal Tour" .

title: Rosendal Palace
label: Attraction
text: This royal residence on the island of Djurgården, built for King Karl XIV Johan, is an outstanding example of the Swedish Empire style. Furniture, textiles, and fixtures create an impressive overall effect, designed and manufactured by Swedish artists and artisans.

contact_text.text: Rosendal Palace is open between June and August each summer.

title: Rosersberg Palace
label: Attraction
text: Rosersberg Palace is a royal residence with furnishings intact from the reigns of Karl XIII and Karl XIV Johan.The Oxenstierna family built the palace in the 1630s and it has been at the disposal of the royal family since 1762. Today it has a wealth of well-preserved, unique textiles from the late Gustavian 1700s to the Empire style of the 1800s. The vast palace grounds in their Lake Mälaren setting add to Rosersberg's charm.

title: Royal Canal Tour
label: Activity
text: Through city and nature. The tour takes you through the picturesque Djurgården canal, along the shores of Saltsjön, and past historic buildings and sights. Audio guides in eleven languages.

title: Royal National City Park
label: Park
text: The world's first national urban park is a green lung forming an arc more than six miles long, stretching around and through the city.The park abuts the adjoining forests around the city, ensuring an exceptional wealth of species. You can encounter deer and hares, even foxes and moose, and spot rare birds, butterflies, and insects, right inside the city. You can walk for days through the Ekoparken, discovering ever new lovely spots.There's an abundance of things to see: museums, an amusement park, theaters and entertainment, castles, inns and hotels, sports facilities, numerous residences from different historical periods, hills with centuries-old oak trees, lakes, streams, bays, marshes, and canals.The meadows with grazing cows, horses, and sheep, secluded swimming spots, rocky hilltops, and areas with wild, virgin nature make it hard to take in that you're in the middle of a big city.

title: Skansen Open-Air Museum
label: Attraction
text: Skansen is a favorite both among Stockholmers and visitors passing through, and it’s a perfect family outing. This is the oldest open-air museum in the world and also the Stockholm zoo, with animals native to Scandinavia, a children's petting zoo, and two indoor aquariums; Skansen's Aquarium and the Baltic Sea Science Center.Skansen is beautifully located on Royal Djurgården and offers spectacular views over all of Stockholm. This is also Sweden in miniature. 150 farms and dwellings from different parts of the country were disassembled and transported here. Swedish traditions such as Midsummer, Walpurgis Night, and Lucia are celebrated at Skansen.

title: Skansen's Aquarium
label: Attraction
text: Meet Saki monkeys, giant iguanas, and yellow-beaked toucans in the misty rain forests. Find everything from big crocs to pygmy marmosets. Meet them all at Skansen's Aquarium.

title: Skinnarviksberget
label: Park
text: The highest natural point in central Stockholm is a favorite place among the locals for picnics and parties under the open sky. The views are stunning – across Kungsholmen, Gamla Stan (Old Town), the Stockholm City Hall, and other points of interest. The park beneath the hill has a small playground and an open-air café where you can enjoy a light lunch or an ice cream in one of the hammocks.

title: Skokloster Castle
label: Attraction
text: One of the world's greatest baroque castles in a beautiful natural setting by Mälaren's shore near Arlanda. The castle is from the Swedish Empire of the 17th century; it is Sweden's biggest private palace. Visit the castle's staterooms on your own, or take a guided tour through the beautiful rooms and halls filled with original furniture from various centuries.

title: Skyview
label: Activity
text: Skyview is the world-class attraction that takes you to the top of the world’s largest spherical building, the Avicii Arena, a Stockholm landmark. From the apex 130 meters (425 feet) above sea level, you get a fantastic view encompassing all of Stockholm. The two SkyView gondolas depart every 10 minutes, and the entire visit takes about 30 minutes.

title: Kulturkvarter Snösätra
label: Attraction
text: Situated in the suburb of Rågsved the open-air (and all year round) exhibition in Snösätra Kulturkvarter is certainly off the beaten path, but well worth a visit for anyone with even a passing interest in street art. Swedish and international artists bring their signature style each year, and there’s also an open wall where anyone who respects the rules is welcome to showcase their artistry. There’s an annual festival every spring with music, DJs, and live painting to unveil new murals and a handful of official vernissages and parties all through the summer.

title: Snus and Match Museum
label: Museum
text: The Snus and Match Museum on the Skansen Open-Air Museum grounds, which takes you on a cultural-historical journey through two products that have had a major impact on Swedish history.Here, you can follow the development of snus and matches from the 17th century to the present day, discover magnificent rococo boxes, carved snus dogs and colorful match labels, and learn more about historical Swedish tobacco cultivation. The museum houses both permanent exhibitions and temporary exhibitions that delve into the stories of industrial history, design, trade and the people behind the products. In the creative workshop, both children and adults can explore their creativity through activities inspired by matches.

title: Solvalla
label: Activity
text: Sweden’s biggest harness-racing track, with about 80 race-days per year.The highlight of the year is an elite race in May. V86 betting takes place every Wednesday. Exceptions can occur. The elite race on the last Sunday in May is harness racing’s annual highlight. Several restaurants in the area.

title: Spritmuseum – Museum of Swedish drinking culture
label: Museum
text: Located between a shipwreck and an amusement park, this museum will take you on an unforgettable historical journey through the Swedish drinking culture. From the 15th century until today, through joy and despair, cocktail parties and park benches, rarely does an afternoon dedicated to alcohol have so many wise insights. Shop, restaurant and bar.

title: Stockholm – My inspiration
text:
We have spoken to six Stockholm locals about what inspires them about their home town. Meet rapper and entrepreneur Silvana Imam, singer and producer Beatrice Eli, artist and art activist Saadia Hussain, fashion designer Naim Josefi, Lina Thomsgård, Director of Stockholm Museum of Women's History, and Albin Flinkas, creative director of The Park Theatre, and find out what inspires them about Stockholm.
Click here to watch.

title: Stockholm Cathedral
label: Attraction
text: Stockholm’s medieval Cathedral, built in 1279, houses unique objects such as the St George and the Dragon sculpture (1489), the legendary Vädersoltavlan (1535) and Lena Lervik’s sculpture ”Joseph and Mary” (2002).Since 1527, the Cathedral has been a Lutheran church. A wide range of religious services and concerts are held. The wedding of T.R.H. Crown Princess Victoria and Prince Daniel took place on Saturday, June 19, 2010, in Stockholm Cathedral.

title: Konserthuset Stockholm
label: Activity
text: Konserthuset (The Stockholm Concert Hall) at Hötorget is home to the Swedish Royal Philharmonic Orchestra, and world-famous for hosting the Nobel Prize ceremony. The house was built in 1926, and overflows with music all year round (you can also attend guided tours and exhibitions on the premises).The iconic blue building is one of Stockholm's prime examples of neoclassicism; The architect Ivar Tengbom aimed to erect a classical temple to the glory of music. Many leading artists, including Carl Milles and Isaac Grünewald, have contributed to the decoration, inspired by ancient mythology.

title: Stockholm Panorama
label: Activity
text: A great way of getting to know Stockholm. This 75-minute bus trip allows you to get to know famous sites and buildings and to enjoy fantastic views. Buy your ticket in the kiosk on Gustav Adolfs torg.

title: Stockholm Photo Tour
label: Activity
text: A guided tour of Stockholm and a photography course in one! City Photo Tours take you to Stockholm's best photo spots and along the way you get to hear anecdotes and stories about the places you are passing. You will get tips and tricks on shooting, so you can take your own postcard-like images.

title: Stockholm Toy Museum – CLOSED until September
label: Museum
text: NOTE: Closed for renovations until September 2026 Previously housed at Tidö castle, Stockholm Toy Museum is the largest collection of its kind in Scandinavia. Since 2017 the exhibit has a new home; Bergrummet, the caverns under Skeppsholmen. Get lost in nostalgia and explore the vast collection of boxcars, teddy bears, comic books, action figures, collectibles and dolls in a unique setting that brings kids, parents, and grandparents together!

title: Stockholm Transport Museum
label: Museum
text: The Stockholm Transport Museum showcases a vast number of objects and activities that illustrate how public transport has affected the lives of Stockholmers for more than 150 years, and what its future might entail. The collections feature nearly 70 vehicles, 20,000 drawings, 10,000 other objects, and 500,000 photos of which 30,000 have been digitized. Since May 2022 the museum has relocated to Hjorthagen, north of Östermalm. The easiest way to reach it is by taking the metro's red line north, to the station of Ropsten.

title: Stortorget
label: Attraction
text: Stortorget is not only the main square in Stockholm's old town, but also the oldest square in the city! It was mentioned as early as 1420. This must-visit is home to several highlights such as the Nobel Prize Museum, the popular café Chokladkoppen, the bakery Grillska Huset and the bar and restaurant Pharmarium. The colorful facades on the west side of the square are probably the most photographed in the city!

title: Streetcar Djurgården Line
label: Attraction
text: Take the well-preserved museum piece streetcar Djurgården Line (Streetcar no. 7N) roundtrip from Norrmalm Square to Royal Djurgården with all its sights. Runs on weekends during spring and fall and Tuesday-Sunday during peak season in the summer. Among the streetcars, there is a mobile café, which runs on the weekends during spring, fall, and winter.

title: Strömkajen
label: Attraction
text: So you want to book a trip to the Stockholm Archipelago. Sure, you can do that online. But why not go down to the terminal at Strömkajen, and experience some award-winning architecture in the process? Opened in 2013, these brass covered buildings have won several awards and been nominated as the most beautiful buildings in Stockholm.

title: Strömma: sightseeing by bus and boat
label: Activity
text: Built where the Baltic Sea meets with Lake Mälaren, with stunning vistas and sparkling blue water wherever you turn, Stockholm has to be one of the world’s top cities for sightseeing. Strömma gives you the opportunity to experience Stockholm from every angle. Whether you want to go for a cruise in the archipelago or under the bridges of Stockholm or on a classical bus tour Strömma has the sightseeing tour for you.

title: Sven-Harry's art museum
label: Museum
text: This shiny six-storied building with a brass facade houses an art gallery, museum, restaurant, and roof terrace. Probably the most unique feature of the museum is the copy of Sven-Harry’s former home, an 18th-century manor house, reconstructed on its premises. Visitors will be able to cross the threshold of Sven-Harry’s “home” and enjoy the art collection he has lovingly built up over the last 35 years. In the large bright art gallery, diverse, multifaceted exhibitions are shown, primarily by Swedish contemporary artists. There are regular tours and programs related to the ongoing exhibitions.

title: Swedish Museum of Natural History and Cosmonova
label: Museum
text: Exhibitions about nature (dinosaurs!) and the development of mankind. Learn about the universe and the earth, animals, and plants. Also, step right into a film adventure under Cosmonova's huge dome screen (8,000+ sq. ft.) !

title: Swedish Museum of Performing Arts
label: Museum
text: Scenkonstmuseet, or the Swedish Museum of Performing Arts, is devoted to theatre, dance, and music. Besides offering insights into the history and future of the performing arts, its interactive exhibitions let you be a part of the experience. Take place in a virtual dance troupe, try on theatre masks or create your own piece of music from a multitude of instrument samples.

title: Tantolunden
label: Park
text: Tantolunden is a large park by Årstaviken on the island of Södermalm. Its location close to the restaurants and cafés of Hornstull, Mariatorget, and SoFo has made the area a popular meeting place for young Stockholmers. People of all ages meet here for swimming and picnics in the summer and for sledding in the winter. There's a playground, beach volleyball court, minigolf, a frisbee golf course, and an open-air theater. Don't miss the chance to take a stroll up the hill and enjoy the more than 100 allotment gardens and garden sheds. Creative carpentry and gardening have been blooming behind the fences since 1915.

title: Tensta Konsthall
label: Museum
text: Tensta Konsthall is the result of a grassroots initiative to bring art to the suburbs of Stockholm. Opened in 1998, the museum has hosted exhibitions by some of the world's leading contemporary artists like Tris Vinna-Michell, Marie Louise Ekman, and Iman Issa.

title: The bridge to Skeppsholmen
label: Attraction
text: The bridge over to Skeppsholmen. Stop by the golden crown at the middle of the bridge to get that stunning view over the Royal Palace.

title: The Butterfly House Haga Ocean
label: Attraction
text: Step into a lush, tropical environment and meet hundreds of exotic butterflies, frogs, parrots and other animals. 1,2 million liters big sea aquarium with sharks and reef fish. Shop and greenhouse café.

title: The Chinese Pavilion
label: Attraction
text: Located on the Drottningholm Palace grounds and built in the 1750s. This fairytale palace is a remarkable treasure, featuring one of Europe´s best examples of rococo furnishings with chinoiserie, painting a picture of relations between Asia and Europe 300 years ago. Drottningholm with the Chinese Pavilion is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.The Chinese Pavilion is open during the summer season May-September.

title: The City Hall
label: Attraction
text: Stockholm City Hall, with its spire featuring the golden Three Crowns, is one of the most famous silhouettes in Stockholm. It is one of the country’s leading examples of national romanticism in architecture. The City Hall was designed by architect Ragnar Östberg and is built from eight million bricks. The 106-meter tall tower has three crowns, which is the Swedish national coat of arms, at its apex. Behind the magnificent facades are offices and session halls for politicians and officials, as well as splendid assembly rooms and unique works of art. Stockholm’s municipal council meets in Rådssalen, the Council Chamber.The great Nobel banquet is also held at City Hall. After dinner in Blå Hallen, the Blue Hall, Nobel Prize laureates, royalties, and guests dance in Gyllene Salen, the Golden Hall, with its 18 million gold mosaic tiles.The City Hall shop features specially designed souvenirs and presents that commemorate City Hall and Stockholm. The City Hall is open to the public through guided tours only. Guided tours are held daily in Swedish and English at certain hours and can be canceled with short notice due to events. The City Hall Tower is open during the summer months (May to August). During this period, you can climb up inside the tower and enjoy a fantastic view of the city.

title: The Stockholm Public Library
label: Attraction
text: The Stockholm Public Library in Stockholm was created by world-famous architect Gunnar Asplund and is a great example of the style called Swedish Grace. This library has been listed as one of the world's most beautiful libraries by the magazine Conde Nast Traveler. The facade is truly gorgeous, but make sure to enter the building for an even more amazing sight. Closed for renovations until 2027.
mass_info: The Stockholm Public Library is currently closed due to renovations and maintenance. Planned reopening is in early 2028. Read more about the project at Stockholm växer (page in Swedish).

title: Stockholm City Museum
label: Museum
text: A magnificent 17th-century palace filled to the brim with Stockholm's history. Trace the city's development from a little, medieval harbor town to today’s multicultural metropolis.

title: The Djurgården Ferry
label: Activity
text: The popular commuter ferry Djurgårdsfärjan takes both Stockholm locals and visitors between the central quay at Slussen and Djurgården island, via Skeppsholmen island. The beautiful journey only takes around 10 minutes. The ferry is a part of Stockholm’s public transport, meaning that all types of SL tickets are valid on board.

title: Avicii Arena
label: Attraction
text: Avicii Arena, formerly the Ericsson Globe, has since it's inauguration in 1989 been one of Stockholm’s most iconic buildings. With a volume of 605 000 cubic meters (approximately 2 136 540 cubic feet), this is the world’s largest spherical building. The arena serves as Sweden's national hockey arena but also hosts a variety of other events and concerts. Through the years some of the world's biggest artists have graced its main stage: The Rolling Stones, Metallica, Beyoncé, Madonna, and U2 to name a few. The vista from The Skyview, a gondola running along the outside of the structure's curved wall, offers a spectacular view of southern Stockholm.

title: The Gustavsberg Porcelain Museum
label: Museum
text: The Gustavsberg Porcelain Museum exhibits examples of the well-known porcelain factory’s production from 1825-1993, with over 45 000 objects. You will find unique artwork from different epochs and countless examples of household china, including classics created by the factory’s famous designers, but also many old beloved patterns of a more anonymous character.

title: The Hallwyl Collection
label: Museum
text: Step into a magnificent palace in the center of Stockholm that will take you 100 years back in time. Discover the von Hallwyl family’s fascinating history and experience the luxuries of the past in the sumptuous dining room, drawing room, smoking room, billiard room, and armory. Audio guide in Swedish and English. Shop.

title: The House of Nobility
label: Attraction
text: Commissioned in the 17th century by the Swedish nobility, to whom it still belongs, The House of Nobility remains one of the most exquisite works of architecture in northern Europe.The walls of the Session Hall are decorated with the 2.326 coats of arms of the Swedish aristocracy.

title: The Jewish Museum
label: Museum
text: The Jewish Museum can be found in Stockholm's oldest extant synagogue. The site itself, situated in the Old Town, tells the story of when the first Jews came to Sweden, how they formed a Jewish community and became part of Swedish society.

title: The Medieval Museum
label: Museum
text: The Medieval Museum's former facilities by the Riksdag are closed, but the museum still organizes various events: City walks, tours of historical rooms, and more! In the summer, you can also visit the museum's pop-up Medeltidsboden. The Museum is relocating, and is expected to open during the relocation,

title: The Museum of Far Eastern Antiquities
label: Museum
text: The Museum of Far Eastern Antiquities is beautifully located on Skeppsholmen in the middle of Stockholm. The rich collections from China, India, Southeast Asia, Japan, and Korea have few counterparts outside of Asia. The exhibitions "China before China" and "The Middle Kingdom – Imperial China" will walk you through 6,000 years of the fascinating history of China. Meet multifaceted Japan with glimpses of entertainment, religion, and tea ceremony performances. Café and museum shop.

title: The Museum of Mediterranean and Near Eastern Antiquities
label: Museum
text: With fascinating collections from Egypt, Cyprus, Greece, the Roman Empire, and the Middle East, the Museum of Mediterranean and Near Eastern Antiquities is Sweden´s main archaeological museum of Mediterranean cultures. Come on a journey through 7,000 years of Egyptian history, and meet the people who lived alongside the Nile. Stories, films, and digital technology will guide you through history and down into the burial chamber. Bagdad Café offers an amazing view of the Royal Palace. Museum shop.

title: The National Maritime Museum
label: Museum
text: Swedish vessels and warships from the 17th century and onwards. Learn more about the efforts to master the sea and the impact of merchant shipping on society, as well as pirates of the past and present and about life onboard. You will find a playroom and a creative workshop for children, as well as a restaurant with a fantastic view. Take the opportunity to discover the museum’s floating museum ships and boat collection near the Vasa Museum—open during the summer.

title: The National Sports Museum of Sweden
label: Museum
text: At the National Sports Museum (Riksidrottsmuseum) you can see exhibits on Swedish sports from ancient times until today, from the 1912 Olympic Games in Stockholm to today’s fixed stars and the fascination of sport, but also its downsides.Try different sports activities and challenge yourself or others in fun competitive activities. Don’t miss the films of sporting highlights and old reviews, listen to radio commentaries and relive the excitement.

title: The Nobel Prize Museum
label: Museum
text: The Nobel Prize Museum contains all essential information about the most prestigious prize in the world, Alfred Nobel, and the Nobel Laureates. Guided tours, films, and artefacts show you the ideas that changed our world. The bistro serves lunch and Nobel ice cream, and the shop has something for curious minds of all ages.!

title: The Per Albin Houses
label: Attraction
text: The 94 houses on Ålstensgatan in Bromma are a classic example of Swedish functionalism. They were designed by architect Paul Hedqvist and built in the 1930s. The street has become a symbol for the political term "folkhemmet" (the people's home), which aimed to build a society without class barriers and where everybody would be entitled to a decent home. The concept of "folkhemmet" was launched by Per Albin Hansson, who was the prime minister of Sweden from 1923 to 1946, except for a short period in 1936. He actually moved into one of the collective houses on the street, and the nickname The Per Albin Houses has stuck ever since. Per Albin Hansson lived on Ålstensgatan 40 until his death, and his house can be recognized by its half-round extension.

title: The Police Museum
label: Museum
text: The Police Museum is about police work and the role of police in society. The museum presents the historical development of the Swedish police and describes police work today. The exhibitions also explain forensic techniques and how the police are depicted in the media and popular culture. In the children’s exhibition, children can play in a police car, try on uniforms, and solve a tricky case. At the traffic playground, you can rent pedal cars.

title: The Riddarholmen Church
label: Attraction
text: Stockholm’s only remaining medieval abbey, built in the late 1200s.The church is the last resting place of the Swedish monarchs and aristocracy, including Gustav II Adolf, Karl XII, Gustav V, and their consorts. The Riddarholmen Church is open for visitors between May and September.The spire of Riddarholmskyrkan will be renovated between autumn 2025 and 2028. The church will remain open as usual during the summer, but the exterior will be affected.

title: The Royal Armoury
label: Museum
text: Experience Sweden’s royal history in the dark cellar of the Royal Palace. Splendid costumes and glittering carriages tell stories of magnificent royal coronations, weddings, and funerals. Learn about Streiff, the horse belonging to Gustav II Adolf. See Karl XII’s muddy blue uniform from 1718 and the clothing Gustav III wore to the masquerade ball of 1792. In the children’s room, you will find yourself in an enchanted world. Try on dresses and knight costumes, play, read and draw.

title: The Economy museum – Royal Coin Cabinet
label: Museum
text: The Economy Museum – Royal Coin Cabinet is a great place to learn about the economy and money, and how they affect you and the world around us, through exciting exhibitions and activities. The museum's restaurant, Restaurang Rosengården, serves lunch and fika during opening hours.

title: The Royal Dramatic Theatre
label: Activity
text: Sweden's national theatre is a beautiful Jugend building located on the waterfront at Nybroviken bay. The guided tours of Dramaten starts at the main entrance and moves through the elegant marble foyer and the main stage. A fascinating look behind the scenes, including a visit to the theatre’s extensive wardrobes. If you fancy a drink, the Marble Foyer (Marmorsalen) and its adjacent terraces are great places to hang out in beautiful and cultured atmosphere.

title: The Royal Stables
label: Attraction
text: This workplace museum is located in the heart of the city in a historic building dating back to 1890. The King's coachmen guide visitors around the unique stables with their horses, cars, decorative harnesses and a fine collection of 19th-century carriages. Guided tours only. Summertime the horses go to graze.
mass_info: Please note: The Royal Stables are only open for pre-booked groups, as well as certain public events.

title: The Royal Opera House
label: Activity
text: Kungliga Operan has been the Swedish national venue for opera and ballet since January 18, 1773. You can visit Kungliga Operan as a member of the audience at one of the performances or take a guided tour. On the tour, you will have the opportunity to look backstage, visit the royal rooms, and peer down into the orchestra pit. Learn about the fascinating history of Kungliga Operan and get a glimpse of what backstage life is like today.

title: The Royal Palace
label: Attraction
text: Welcome to one of the largest palaces in Europe! The Royal Palace is the official residence of His Majesty the King of Sweden, with over 600 rooms.The Palace is open to the public and offers no less than five museums. The Palace was largely built during the eighteenth century in the Italian Baroque style, on the spot where the “Tre Kronor” castle burned down in 1697. Visit the reception rooms with splendid interiors from the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, Rikssalen (the Hall of State) with Queen Kristina’s silver throne, and Ordenssalarna (Halls of the Orders of Chivalry). You can also see Gustav III’s Museum of Antiquities, the Tre Kronor Museum, and the Treasury.The Royal Palace also contains the Armory, with royal costumes and armor, as well as coronation carriages and magnificent coaches from the Royal Stable. Make sure not to miss the parade of soldiers and the daily changing of the guard.

title: The Strindberg Museum
label: Museum
text: Blå tornet - 'The Blue Tower' is the last residence of famous Swedish author, playwright, and artist August Strindberg (1849-1912). Visit this home, consisting of a bedroom, dining room, and workroom. Strindberg's library is open in conjunction with the exhibition. The exhibition 'Strindberg in the center' features books, photos, paintings, and artifacts.

title: The Swedish History Museum
label: Museum
text: The Swedish History Museum narrates Sweden’s history from the earliest times to the present. See gold and silver treasures and magnificent medieval art. The museum also has the world's largest collection of objects from the age of Vikings.

title: The Thiel Gallery
label: Museum
text: One of the finest art museums in Sweden, the Thiel Gallery exhibits a unique collection of Nordic late 19th and early 20th-century art. Painters such as Edvard Munch, Carl Larsson, Bruno Liljefors, and Anders Zorn form the basis of the banker Ernest Thiel's collection.

title: The Toy Museum
label: Museum
text: The Toy Museum, located by the seas in the suburb of Fisksätra, houses a large collection of toys, including dolls, dolls’ houses, cars, action figures, teddy bears and model railways.

title: The Treasury
label: Museum
text: The Swedish state regalia are used for royal weddings, christenings, and funerals. Among the priceless treasures are King Gustav Vasa’s sword of state, King Erik XIV’s crown, orb, and scepter, as well as a galaxy of princely crowns.

title: The Vasa Museum
label: Museum
text: The Vasa is the best-preserved seventeenth-century ship in the world and a unique art treasure. More than 98 percent of the ship is original, and it is decorated with hundreds of carved sculptures.The 69 meter-long warship Vasa sank on its maiden voyage in Stockholm harbor in 1628 and was salvaged 333 years later in 1961. For nearly half a century the ship has been slowly, deliberately, and painstakingly restored to a state approaching its original glory. The three masts on the roof of the tailor-made museum show the height of the ship's original masts.There are different exhibitions around the ship ranging from topics like life on board and its historical context. The film about the Vasa is shown in different languages. There is also an audio guide in different languages, to be used by visitors on their own mobile devices. The museum has free Wi-Fi. In addition, there is a well-stocked shop and a pleasant restaurant for lunch and fika. Free admission for children up to 18 years.

title: The Vasa Tour
label: Activity
text: The Vasa Tour combines water-bound Stockholm-sightseeing, with an exciting history tour. The 50-minute tour takes you along the infamous Vasa-ship's maiden voyage, to the spot where the ill-fated war cruiser sank in 1628. Departure is from either Nybrokajen or the Vasa Museum jetty and the tour is in English and Swedish.

title: The Vaxholm Fortress Museum
label: Museum
text: The history of the fortress and coastal defense is shown in models, exhibits and recreated milieus.

title: The Viking Museum
label: Museum
text: The Viking Museum on Djurgården offers an immersive journey into the Viking Age. Explore interactive exhibitions, authentic artefacts and meet knowledgeable guides in historical attire. Experience the adventure ride Ragnfrid’s Saga, and discover stories of daily life, trade and mythology in Viking Age Scandinavia.

title: The Wave Swinger at Gröna Lund
label: Activity
text: The old-fashioned wave swinger at amusement park Gröna Lund makes for a great photo, especially at nighttime.

contact.address: Gröna Lund, Lilla Allmänna Gänd 9,  Stockholm

title: Tom Tit's Experiment
label: Attraction
text: A world without limits. Tom Tits Experiment opens the door to a world where you can choose whether to dive deep into a mixture of creativity and knowledge or simply draw your finger across the surface.Experiments and lots of fun for all ages – both inside and outdoors (garden open May-September). Café, restaurant, picnic room, shop. Program and shows on weekends and school holidays. Tom Tit's Experiment is located in the suburb of Södertälje and is easily reached by Stockholm's public transportation.

title: Tour: Old Town & Riddarholmen
label: Activity
text: Welcome to a walking tour in the historical heart of Stockholm. See the most famous sights such as the Royal Palace, the narrowest alley and St George and the Dragon. The tour includes a visit to the island of Riddarholmen, with a stunning view of Lake Mälaren and the lakeside of the city.

title: Tullgarn Palace
label: Attraction
text: The summer residence and favorite palace of Gustav V, built in Vagnhärad south of Stockholm in around 1720.Prince Fredrik Adolf’s State Apartment is particularly well preserved, and the English park dates from the early 19th century.

title: Ulriksdal Palace
label: Attraction
text: Ulriksdal Palace is situated on the banks of Edsviken Lake in the National City Park in Stockholm. The palace was built in the 1600s and visitors to the palace will find traces from many different epochs. Several Swedish regents have left their mark on Ulriksdal. Queen Kristina built a pleasure garden in front of the palace and Hedvig Elenora built an Orangery in the park. In the palace grounds, you´ll find the Orangery, with its collection of Swedish sculptures, a café, a nice park, and fresh breezes from the sea. Guided tours are included in the entrance fee.

title: Vita Bergen
label: Park
text: Vita Bergen, commonly known as Vitabergsparken, is a popular picnic hangout located on Southern Södermalm. The park’s high elevation makes it a great viewpoint of Södermalm on a sunny summer’s day. Built in 1897 to give the factory workers a place for rest and relaxation, the park still features many typical 19th century buildings.

title: Walking Tour Old Town in Russian
label: Activity
text: A walking tour in the heart of the medieval Stockholm. Discover the narrow streets of the Old Town, the Royal Palace and the beautiful city views from the island of Riddarholmen. The tour includes stories of the Swedish-Russian relations during the past centuries. Limited seats. Language: Russian.

title: Arholma
label: Excursion
text: Arholma is the Stockholm archipelago’s most northerly island. Its landscape is exciting and varied—from craggy rocks to old farmland. Most of the island is a nature preserve. There are two year-round hostels. Open-air dance floor with tavern and café in the summer.

title: Blidö
label: Excursion
text: Its location near the mainland with the open sea to the east makes this island a popular vacation paradise. Summer guests have come here since the late 1800s. Visitors can have lunch or dinner at Blidö hamnkrog, or stay the night at the island's hostel.

title: Bullerö
label: Excursion
text: Bullerö lies in the outer archipelago but it is well worth the trip. There is a regular boat, Bullerölinjen (timetables at www.battaxi.se). The island is a nature and bird preserve with many nice bays and rocks to swim from. The island belonged to Swedish artist Bruno Liljefors for many years, and his old guest cottage and studio have been preserved. Many other artists, such as Anders Zorn and Albert Engström, often visited Bullerö. There are is a hostel and a sauna on the island but no restaurant or grocery store.

title: Fejan
label: Excursion
text: A small, historic island in the northern archipelago on the edge of the open sea. In the late 1800s, there was a quarantine station here to stop cholera that was ravaging Europe. Fejan now has a popular tavern and hostel open in the summer. Kayaks and rowboats are available for rent in the large guest harbor.

title: Mariefred
label: Excursion
text: A sweet, picturesque small town with plenty of history, just over an hour by car from Stockholm, built around the majestic Gripsholm Castle. Gripsholm was a fortress in the 14th century and took its present form in the 1530s under King Gustav Vasa. The castle houses the Swedish State’s portrait collection In the warm months, you can reach the town on the historic steamship Mariefred. Launched in 1903, it has trafficked this route ever since. You can eat lunch on board in the beautiful dining saloon.Mariefred also has a narrow-gauge historical railway where you can enjoy a historic ride through the surrounding area. The charming town center has numerous quaint restaurants, cafés, and shops.

title: Nacka
label: Excursion
text: Nacka is where big city and island meet. It is easy to get here by boat, car, bus, bicycle or the suburban Saltsjöbanan train, and the trip usually takes between 10 and 20 minutes from Stockholm proper.History buffs get their fill either at the Battlefield Museum HAMN, or have a fika at the 18th-century country estates Svindersvik and Stora Nyckelviken. If you're into architecture, the designer hotel J at Nacka beach and the beautiful historic homes from the 20th century in Saltsjöbaden are sure make an impression. For art and culture, Dieselverkstaden is a creative space and exhibition hall well worth exploring, as are 20 newly-painted murals in the area that will make your jaw drop.For the outdoor types, Hellasgården and Velamsund’s nature reserves are classics that never go out of style.

title: Nynäshamn
label: Excursion
text: It is said that Nynäshamn is the only place in Stockholm County where you can see the sea horizon from the mainland. The beautiful barren nature along the 1,000-km-long stretch of coast has also inspired many of Sweden’s best-known authors. Take a walk along the coastal Strandvägen, visit the Iron Age house in Körunda or the popular island of Landsort/Öja. Take a boat trip to the islands Nåttarö, Rånö and Ålö or try your hand at surfing, wakeboarding, jet-skiing, diving, sailing, paddling, climbing, hiking or golfing.

title: Runriket (Vallentuna/Täby)
label: Attraction
text: Ornate runestones, in effect ancient billboards with important messages written in runic alphabets, were a preferred mode of communication of the Vikings. Of the world's 7500+ recorded rune stones over 2000 are located in Sweden, and they can be found in the woods all around the Stockholm area. But the biggest concentration of preserved runestones in the world can be found in Runriket just north of Stockholm. Runriket is located in the woods around Vallentunasjön and free for everyone to visit. But to make the best out of your Viking hike, start at the official park entrance at Jarlbankes bridge and work your way around the trail! You can also book a guided tour of the area with a personal guide.

title: Sigtuna
label: Excursion
text: Sweden’s first town, founded in the 10th century. Small-scale and pedestrian friendly, with charming wooden buildings by Lake Mälaren, less than an hour outside of Stockholm. Good selection of stores, cafés, restaurants and hotels, plus an interesting museum. The district is rich in rune stones, to fascinate history buffs. Sigtuna can be reached by train, bus, or boat from the center of Stockholm. Nearby is Skokloster Castle, a first-class attraction. Skokloster was the residence of one of Gustav II Adolf’s generals when Sweden was a superpower, and the castle interior from the mid 17th century has been kept completely intact. Steninge Palace and Rosersberg Palace is also situated close to Sigtuna.

title: Svartsö
label: Excursion
text: Svartsö is of the largest of the mid-archipelago islands. There is a country store at Ahlsvik’s jetty and nearby Svartsö Krog has its own jetty. Rent a bike or walk and then cool down at one of the island’s inland lakes. The inhabitants of Svartsö get their drinking water from Storträsk, the largest of these lakes. In Skälvik you will find Svartsö Herrgårdspensionat, a summer villa from the early 1900s that is now a guesthouse and restaurant that has rooms available during the summer season (April to October). There are also cottages for rent.

title: Trosa
label: Excursion
text: The picturesque town of Trosa, with its narrow alleys and charming shops, is a popular tourist destination. The low wooden building along Trosån to the outer pier contributes to this fact.The guest harbor (Gästhamnen) is a lively meeting place during the summer months. Visitors also come to Trosa to kayak, visit SPA, visit Tullgarn and Nynäs castles, see the Middle Age churches from the 1100s and 1200s, and to hike along the 900-km-long Sörmland footpath.

title: Uppsala
label: Excursion
text: Uppsala is Sweden’s fourth largest city and an important university town just north of Stockholm. Visit the three Iron Age royal burial mounds in Old Uppsala, the cathedral (Scandinavia’s largest) or Uppsala Castle. Uppsala is also home to a plethora of charming shops and cafés, as well as the home and gardens of nobleman and famous botanist Carl von Linné.

title: 2 Little Spoons
label: Shop
text: 2 Little Spoons models itself after small neighborhood stores of old. Located in the heart of trendy Midsommarkransen, the store offers a little bit of everything. Both from local designers and from around the globe. Lightbulbs, cutlery, toys, towels, cooking books, posters, blankets and more. Everything on-sale is carefully selected to be made from sustainable and natural materials.

label: Shop
text: A cozy lifestyle boutique in the trendy neighborhood of SoFo. Shop everything from surfboards and clothes to table books and tents, or have a seat in the café and enjoy an organic espresso or an açai bowl. If you’re not an outdoor person before visiting 6/5/4, you will definitely want to become one afterward.

title: Acne Archive
label: Shop
text: Love the Swedish fashion house Acne but think it’s a bit too pricey? Then this is the store for you! Acne Archive offers a handpicked selection of Acne Studio classics, showpieces, accessories, shoes, and items from previous collections at up to 75 percent off.

title: Åhléns City
label: Shop
text: Sweden’s largest department store, with competitive prices for clothing, design, media, beauty and much more. Large, diverse grocery store in the basement.

title: And the revolution
label: Shop
text: And the revolution designs builds and sells custom bicycles for two-wheeled travelers that want to get around town on a more personalized vehicle. You'll also find an assortment of handy bike accessories like helmets, baskets, clothes, and bags.

title: Anna Holtblad
label: Shop
text: A pioneer in contemporary Swedish fashion, timelessly elegant and simultaneously up-to-date collections, with a loyal clientele in Sweden and abroad. Signature knitwear garments.

title: Aplace
label: Shop
text: A fashion store and magazine with a wide range of the latest in Scandinavian and international men’s and women’s fashion. You will find several Swedish success stories here including Dagmar, Whyred, and Rodebjer. Aplace also has a second-hand program that lets you both buy pre-used clothes, but also turn in your own clothes that you don't use anymore.

title: Arkivet secondhand
label: Shop
text: Arkivet secondhand specializes in, not necessarily retro-chic and antiques, but on current fashion trends and seasons. Primarily selling women's fashion, Arkivet also has a selection of beautiful accessories and shoes. From high street to high-end fashion, the items are carefully selected and none of them are more than two-three years old.Arkivet has stores on Nybrogatan 44 in Östermalm and Sergels Torg 18 in the City center.

title: Asplund
label: Shop
text: Nordic light colors and Scandinavian simple design at its best. The prominent Swedish designers are collected here. There is a large selection of high-quality Scandinavian furniture, rugs, lamps and other retail items. A must for the visitor with an interest in minimalism.

title: Bågar & Glas
label: Shop
text: Trendy yet classic boutique offering handpicked spectacles and sunglasses. At Bågar & Glas, you'll find spectacles from Swedish designer Oscar Magnuson along with other exclusive and smaller brands. If you are looking for unique and high-quality (sun)glasses, this is the place to go.Bågar & Glas has another store on Norrlandsgatan in the city center.

title: Beyond Retro
label: Shop
text: London’s leading supplier of vintage clothes has a big store on Södermalm. Colorful, festive vintage clothes in a delightful mix of inexpensive and not-so-inexpensive. There is also a store on Drottninggatan 77.

title: Blås & Knåda
label: Shop
text: Blås & Knåda has the country’s largest selection of contemporary Swedish studio pottery and studio glass, both studio and unique art objects. 45 working members operate the store and gallery together. Since it was started in 1975, Blås & Knåda has become a concept in handicraft circles and today it functions as a center for those interested in glass and pottery.

title: Bokslukaren
label: Shop
text: Children´s bookstore for both kids and their parents, with books for all ages and in several different languages, as well as gifts and toys. There's a small café in the back which serves great coffee along with miniature cakes, cookies and scones.

title: Bookbinders Design
label: Shop
text: A Swedish chain with high-quality paper goods created with the environment in mind. They have colorful and timeless notebooks, photo albums, journals and storage boxes in beautiful materials, made to preserve life's memorable moments.

title: Brandstationen
label: Shop
text: Brandstationen (The Fire Station) focuses on furnishings and antiques. From the same people behind the Herr Judit clothing stores, Brandstationen shares the concept of high-quality vintage and second hand. All of the items and jewelry are carefully selected with a trendy and style-conscious target group in mind. The store name comes from it previously being located in – that's right – a fire station.

title: Bruno Götgatsbacken
label: Shop
text: Trendy mall with stores like APLACE, Hope, Arket, and & Other Stories. If you’re in need of a coffee, there’s a cafe with the vibrant Götgatan just outside the window. Even though the mall is small, there’s a lot to discover.

title: Bye Buy
label: Shop
text: This secondhand shop in Kungsholmen makes it fun and easy to buy stuff that someone else has said goodbye to. Bye Buy offers carefully selected clothes, shoes, and toys suitable for children up to six years old. Good for the climate – and good for your wallet!

title: Byredo
label: Shop
text: Exclusive Swedish perfume house whose products are as beautiful to look at as they are fragrant. What makes Byredo unique is its simplicity and the relatively few ingredients they use. All the fragrances are unisex. In addition to perfume, the line includes soaps, skincare products, and scented candles.

title: Cajsa Warg
label: Shop
text: This grocery and delicatessen in the Vasastan district offers a wide selection of high-quality, locally produced and organic products. The store was named after Cajsa Warg, a famous Swedish cookbook author who lived in the 1700s.

title: Caramella
label: Shop
text: Do like a Swede and mix your own bag of candy at Caramella. The small candy shop at Hötorget is crammed with hundreds of varieties och hard and soft candy; Swedish fish, jelly beans, gummy bears, peaches, jelly frogs, cola bottles, chocolate coins and more.

title: Carl Malmsten
label: Shop
text: Tradition and modern furniture are mixed here, with Swedish folk tradition as the starting point. Handicrafts, genuine materials, colors from nature, sustainability and functionality are the watchwords.In addition to furniture designer Carl Malmsten’s classics, some of which have been given new clothing, the company is also investing in a complementary more modern look. Visitors to The City Hall can also see Carl Malmsten's Stadhusstolen which won first prize in a furniture competition for the City Hall in 1916.

title: Caroline Hjerpe
label: Shop
text: Self-taught jeweler and rising star Caroline Hjerpe designs and crafts jewelry in her charming studio and shop on Södermalm. Caroline's credo is to create playful jewelry that can be enjoyed by everyone - from inventive bracelets to stunning diamond engagement rings. And since all her pieces are handmade, no two objects are identical!

title: Chokladfabriken
label: Shop
text: This is the place for chocolate in almost every imaginable variety: chocolates, petits fours, wedding cakes, drinking chocolate, and muffins. Everything is made by hand. Chokladfabriken is run by Martin and Ellinor Isaksson. Martin is a pastry chef who has competed on the Swedish National Culinary Team.

title: Christoffers Blommor
text: Every morning, six days a week, the narrow alley Kåkbrinken is transformed into a lush oasis as Christoffer Broman opens the doors to his shop and starts arranging all the flowers and plants for sale outside. Christoffers Blommor is a small and personal flower shop in Stockholm's Old Town (Gamla Stan) with many regulars who firmly claim it to be the best in town.

title: Coctail deluxe
label: Shop
text: Coctail deluxe is like an inferno of kitsch. They sell plastic odds and ends in every color and shape, and newly manufactured nostalgia items, primarily from the 1950s. If you believe that Sweden is only about minimalism, this place will you convince you otherwise.

title: Cos
label: Shop
text: Modern, urban and chic fashion for both women and men. Quality clothing for work and evenings. Cos is a Swedish brand and part of H&M.

title: Dagmar
label: Shop
text: Behind this interesting label are three sisters, Kristina, Karin, and Sofia. The name comes from their great source of inspiration – their grandmother Dagmar, who was a seamstress herself. Their style can best be described as “arty chic,” and it is inspired by the Art Deco period of the twenties and thirties. High quality, feminine tailoring, and comfortable knitwear garments are Dagmar’s signatures. Sold at stores including Awesome Rags, Kungsgatan 47.

title: Deadwood
label: Shop
text: Everybody knows that leather jackets simply look better when worn and aged. It’s a design philosophy Swedish brand Deadwood has taken to heart. Deadwood uses recycled leather from vintage garments to make new jackets with a timeless feel.

title: Design House Stockholm
label: Shop
text: Discover contemporary Scandinavian design at Design House Stockholm’s Flagship Store in Södermalm, next to Slussen. A curated space for furniture, lighting and design objects by more than 60 independent designers, where craftsmanship, materials and ideas take center stage.See new collections first and explore icons like Block Lamp, Step Stepladder or the vibrant collection of wooden birds in Birds 1967 – always supported by personal guidance from our knowledgeable team.Design House Stockholm is a publishing house for design with retailers worldwide, and we ship across Europe – but everything begins here, at our home in Stockholm.Whether you’re a design enthusiast or curious traveler, this is a must-see stop on Stockholm’s design route – where form and fantasy meets everyday life.

title: Designtorget
label: Shop
text: Designtorget is a shop for people who like form, function and freshening up their lives, combined with unique design. You’ll find a carefully selected assortment of items such as home furnishings, kitchenware, postcards, books, toys and jewelry from well-known and unknown Swedish designers.

title: Eataly
label: Shop
text: Eataly's philosophy is simple; all the Italian delicacies you can imagine, in one place. Eat Italian cheese, salami, and cured meat, fresh pasta and pizza at their large indoor piazza, or pick and choose from the many food stalls and create your own meal at home.

title: EcoSTHLM
label: Shop
text: EcoSTHLM specializes in sustainable and environmentally friendly products for children and toddlers; toys, clothes, furniture, cutlery, bottles, cups and glasses and much more. The items are carefully selected and the store carries both Swedish and international brands.

title: Efva Attling & Attling Man
label: Shop
text: Efva Attling's jewelry collections are distinguished by words and phrases on jewelry in simple basic designs executed in silver. In addition to rings and necklaces for both men and women, you’ll find her designs for glasses and glass. The third store, which is the Efva Attling Flagship store, is located at Birger Jarlsgatan 9.
