title: Artikel2 Stockholm
label: Shop
text: Humanitarian organization and second-hand shop. Artikel2 is a popular spot for the trendy and fashionable of Södermalm to go on a classic thrift store treasure hunt.

title: Filippa K
label: Shop
text: Filippa K founded her successful company in 1993. Today she has more than 500 retailers around the world. Filippa K is where you will find the very essence of Swedish fashion. The collections are characterized by simple, stylistically pure, timeless design of high quality that also stays on the cutting edge!

title: Gallerian
label: Shop
text: Downtown Stockholm’s first and largest galleria. Over 80 stores under one roof offer a broad selection of young and affordable fashion, cafés and restaurants.

title: Gamla Amsterdam
label: Shop
text: Nobody in Stockholm knows Dutch cheese culture better than Gamla Amsterdam. Their cheese shop has a wide selection of the best Gouda, Edamer, Chévre, and Leiden varieties as well as an assortment of delicious cheeses from all over Europe. If you’d rather eat something right away, Gamla Amsterdam also has a cheese bar serving cheese platters, sandwiches, wine, and beer. Obviously, a cheese sandwich here isn’t just a cheese sandwich.

title: Gamla Stans Bokhandel
label: Shop
text: Located on Stockholm’s oldest boulevard, Stora Nygatan, Gamla Stans Bokhandel is a bookshop with a wide selection of literary best sellers in Swedish and English, popular science reads and handy maps. Just a stone’s throw from all of the biggest attractions in Old Town, it’s the perfect place to get more in-depth knowledge about Swedish history after an exciting visit to the Royal Castle.

title: Gamla Stans Polkagriskokeri
label: Shop
text: Gamla Stans Polkagriskokeri makes polkagrisar, a traditional Swedish peppermint-tasting candy, the tried and tested way: by hand. Located in the Old Town, the shop is a great spot to grab a bag of colorful sweets and get a taste of one of the staples of Swedish candy bowls.

title: Goodstore
label: Shop
text: A food boutique in SoFo that prides itself on its one hundred percent vegetarian, ninety-five percent eco-friendly wares, many of which bear Fair Trade labels. It has everything a regular food store provides, from fresh fruit, vegetables, baby food and delicacies to detergents and hygiene products. Ready-prepared food to take away is available during the summer season and catering is available all year round.

title: Grandpa
label: Shop
text: Charming, personal mix of clothes, shoes, accessories, jewelry, vintage items, design, and knickknacks. Frequent DJs and live music. Stores can be found on Södermannagatan, Södermalm and Gamla Brogatan in the city center.

title: Granit
label: Shop
text: Furnishing shop focusing on functional and creative storage options. Here you will find smart storage solutions made of paper, porcelain, plastic and wicker for both home and office. The base colors are black, white, grey and natural. The store also provides lighting solutions, games, baskets, boxes and other fun gift ideas. Granit stores can be found on Götgatan, St. Eriksgatan, Kungsgatan, Humlegårdsgatan and Långholmsgatan.

title: H&M
label: Shop
text: The Swedish fashion chain H&M is a huge global player. Much of its success is attributed to its wide selection of affordable fashion and ability to quickly pick up the latest trends. In central Stockholm, you’ll find the biggest selection in the stores at the intersection of Drottningatan and Mäster Samuelsgatan. Here you will also find H&M's head office.

title: Happy Food Store
label: Shop
text: Happy Food Store sells ecological, local and fresh foods in the city center. You'll find everything from smoothies to beauty creams. The shop is located at Sveavägen 22, just a stone's throw from the Stockholm Concert Hall.

title: Happy Socks
label: Shop
text: Happy Socks has infused sock drawers around the world with a much-needed splash of color. The company was founded in 2008 and today their socks and underwear can be found all around the world.

title: Herr Judit
label: Shop
text: Herr Judit is considered to be one of the best shops for vintage men's clothing in Sweden. The recipe for success is due to carefully selecting the stylish garments and accessories, and the collection is full of high quality and brand name clothing. The shop on Hornsgatan is Herr Judit's main store, while there is an additional store on Sibyllegatan in Östermalm. Brandstationen (The Fire Station), a sister store focusing on indoor furnishings, is also on Hornsgatan.

title: Hestra
label: Shop
text: Famous for its high-quality alpine-gloves, Hestra started out in 1936 by making robust leather gloves for the lumber mill-workers in the village of Hestra in southern Sweden. The company's flagship store is located in central Stockholm where you'll find their latest collection of both durable and water resistant gloves for outdoor activities, and stylish casual gloves.

title: Hope
label: Shop
text: The collections from the Hope design duo are pure in style, timeless and androgynous, inspired by uniforms and vintage. Hope has become famous for well-tailored outerwear and has also received praise for its shoes and handbags. In 2017 the Swedish label decided to change up things and to challenge fashion norms and conventions; all clothes are unisex and come in sizes for both men and women. Except for the flagship store on Smålandsgatan, there is one on  Klarabergsgatan and one on Götgatan.

title: Hornstulls marknad
label: Activity
text: Hornstulls marknad is an outdoor street market situated in the western part of Södermalm. The market stretches along the waterfront and has become one of Stockholms favorite Sunday activities. Expect to find a variety of vintage, second-hand, art, food trucks and everything else that comes with a proper street market. Open every Saturday and Sunday 11:00-17:00, April through October.

title: Hötorget flea market
label: Shop
text: The Hötorget flea market has been a staple of weekend shopping since the mid-'90s. Every Sunday the food and vegetable stands are replaced by tables of old vinyl records, kitchenware, and other knick-knacks, for thrift store hunters to rummage through.

title: Ikea of Sweden
label: Shop
text: A phenomenon that has changed the entire world's view of home furnishing. Kungens Kurva in Skärholmen, south of Stockholm, is the home of the largest Ikea store in Sweden, which opened in 1965. The area is also home to numerous other megastores and shopping centers with affordable shopping.

title: Illums Bolighus
label: Shop
text: The first store in Stockholm from the Danish furniture and interior design chain. Exquisite furniture, glass, ceramics, and lighting fixtures by famous Scandinavian designers.

title: Iris Hantverk Gamla Stan
label: Shop
text: At the end of the nineteenth century, a small brush factory was started in Stockholm. It was a successful operation, so successful that it’s still in existence today. Today, just as in the past, every brush is made by hand by the visually disabled. In addition to brushes, there are numerous other handicraft products, textiles, and interior décor items. There is also a store on Kungsgatan in central Stockholm.

title: J. Lindeberg
label: Shop
text: J. Lindeberg has been combining fashion and sportswear since its inception in 1996. The label emphasizes well-tailored suits, attractive everyday clothing and – golf. J. Lindeberg has truly renewed golf fashion, and today they provide clothing for a series of golf stars.

title: Judits second hand
label: Shop
text: The store at Hornsgatan 75 has one section with used clothes and shoes and another with new clothes, bags, and accessories. Vintage garments are carefully selected styles from the 50s, 60s, and 70s.

title: Jus
label: Shop
text: Jus is a multi-brand store carrying brands such as Ann Demeulemeester, Dries van Noten, Rick Owens, Comme des Garçons, Maison Martin Margiela but also shoes from Guidi, jewelry from Werkstatt München, hats from Horisaki and many other things.

title: Kasthall
label: Shop
text: This Swedish company is a leader in the design and manufacture of contemporary rugs in natural materials. The company takes active responsibility for the environment and is environmentally certified. The store has hand-tufted and woven rugs with its own label, and you can also design your own rug by combining patterns, colors, and accents the way you want.

title: Konsthantverkarna
label: Shop
text: Stockholm’s oldest and largest handicraft cooperative has evolved over the course of 50 years from a “shop for high-quality products” to a modern handicraft gallery on an international scale. The store and exhibit operation is managed by the approximately 90 members. They have traditional handicrafts in pottery, glass, wood, silver, iron, leather and textiles.

title: Konst-ig
label: Shop
text: On Åsögatan 124 you’ll find the largest independent art bookstore in Scandinavia. Konst-ig specializes in most visual art forms, from graffiti to brutalist architecture. You’ll find books, magazines, and journals on such ranging topics as knitting, classic fonts, European street art, cubism, Mapplethorpe, album covers, beer can design and more.

title: Lakritsroten Sveavägen
label: Shop
text: A stylish specialist shop that has all kinds of licorice from around the world. Great for souvenir and gift shopping. The original shop is on Sveavägen and there are four more scattered around town.

title: Lisa Larsson
label: Shop
text: One of Stockholm’s most well-known second-hand stores and a favorite of fashion experts. Vintage clothes for women and men from the 30s through the 70s.

title: Maria Nilsdotter
label: Shop
text: Maria Nilsdotter has created quite a buzz with her 90's inspired designs, taking cues from rave -and punk culture. You can find her jewelry at several locations, and her flagship store is located on Sturegatan in central Stockholm.

title: Maruschka de Margó
label: Shop
text: Maruschka de Margó is a high-end fashion boutique established in central Stockholm three decades ago. Here you'll find exclusive niche brands like Camilla, With Love, Etro, Dea Kudibal, Odabash, Missoni, and Robert Clergeri.In addition to a hand-picked selection from some more unusual fashion houses, Maruschka de Margó also features its line of Tweed Jackets.

title: Mickes
label: Shop
text: Mickes has become an institution among crate diggers and record collectors in Stockholm. The shop – catering to your vinyl, cd and comic book needs – is a vintage rummager's dream with both great bargains and rare collector's items on sale. The shops' irregular opening hours – every day of the year and open to at least 10 in the evening during weekdays – has also made it a popular pit stop for evening shoppers. Adding to its uniqueness, the store is split up in two separate locations facing each other across the street Långholmsgatan.

title: Mini Rodini
label: Shop
text: Mini Rodini was founded 2006 in Sweden and since then has opened up shops all across Scandinavia. The idea is simple; to make stylish clothes for kids that can take the wear-and-tear of hide-and-seek. All the items on shelve are also made from eco-friendly or recycled materials.

title: Modern Retro
label: Shop
text: A jumble of new and second-hand clothes, accessories, shoes, furniture, china, and curios filling 200 square meters (2,000 square feet). Perfect for treasure hunters.

title: Modernity
label: Shop
text: High-end store specializing in vintage design and 20th-century antiques – furniture, lighting, and objets d’art. Emphasis is on Scandinavian design, including luminaries lie Alvar Aalto and Arne Jacobsen.

title: Monkey Beach
label: Shop
text: While many movie stores in Stockholm have, unfortunately, closed down or taken their business online, the digitally shy Monkey Beach has stayed open without as much as an email address. Though small, the store is filled from floor to ceiling with cinematic oddities, hard-to-find cult classics, Arrow Blu-rays and VHS tapes.

title: Mood Stockholm
label: Shop
text: New and stylish mall with a focus on fashion and design. When you are ready for a shopping break, you can enjoy a delicious meal in one of the popular restaurants (Boqueria, Vigårda, E.A.T.) or take in the modern art that adorns the walls. Mood Stockholm is on Regeringsgatan on the block that connects the Hamngatan and Bibliotekstan shopping districts.

title: Myrorna Götgatan
label: Shop
text: For some 100 years, Myrorna has been synonymous with thrift store bargains. The chain of second-hand shops – run by the Swedish arm of The Salvation Army – opened its first store in 1917 in Gothenburg. Today you’ll find Myrorna in every major city in Sweden, and there are several shops in Stockholm.

title: Naturkompaniet Kungsgatan
label: Shop
text: Heading out into the wild, but forgot to pack your favorite pair of long johns or gloves? Naturkompaniet is a Swedish chain of stores specializing in durable clothes for all seasons, and handy outdoor equipment. You'll find everything from warm jackets, backpacks and wool caps to portable kitchens, mushroom knives and sleeping bags. There are several stores in the Stockholm area of which the two on Kungsgatan are the most central.

title: NK - Nordiska Kompaniet
label: Shop
text: Steeped in tradition, NK is Stockholm's most luxurious department store, established in 1915. Swedish and international fashion, cosmetics, jewelry, crystal, ceramics, design, fine foods and much more.

title: NK Market Hall
label: Shop
text: A perfect way to either start of or finish your day of shopping at the venerable NK department store. The market hall, located on the department store’s basement floor has several shops and food stalls with fresh produce, local delicacies and imported treats. Grab a coffe, have a lunch or buy what you need for a great dinner at home.

title: Nordiska Galleriet
label: Shop
text: One of Europe's leading stores when it comes to contemporary classic furniture, with a large selection of décor, lighting and gift items from well known international designers and suppliers.

title: Norrgavel
label: Shop
text: Swedish designer Nirvan Richter is inspired by a combination of Scandinavian minimalism and American Shaker. The award-winning designer runs his company with a humanistic and ecological mindset that takes the eco-cycle into account.

title: Nudie
label: Shop
text: Yet another success story for a Swedish jeans label. Nudie takes great pride in making every piece of clothing from sustainable materials, from the fabric and threads to the smallest buttons. The store has room for the entire Nudie collection and offers free repairs on every pair of Nudie Jeans, no matter when or where you got them. An extremely wide-ranging product line with something every style and age group.

title: Old Touch
label: Shop
text: Large selection of dresses, jewelry, hats and odds and ends from the 1900s to the 1960s, with an especially good eye for the 1920s. Also has clothes and accessories to rent as costumes.

title: Oyyo
label: Shop
text: Oyyo is a design studio producing unique textile interior products. They integrate traditional weaving techniques with a sustainable production process to create beautiful carpets and rugs. Oyyo has a showroom and shop in Stockholm, but open by appointment only.

title: Papercut
label: Shop
text: Papercut is a store that offers both international and Swedish newspapers, books, films, music and printed matter. The collection is carefully selected with the focus on art, design, and fashion. If you share these interests, you will want to spend several hours here. If you need to buy a present for anyone, you will likely find it here.

title: Pärlans konfektyr
label: Shop
text: Looking for a candy shop on Söder? Head to Pärlans Konfektyr. The atmosphere and interior will transport you to the glamorous days of the 1930s. Here, caramels and other sweets are made year-round using traditional craftsmanship in their own factory just outside Stockholm.

title: Pen Store
label: Shop
text: Need a ballpoint pen? A felt-marker? Or a good-old pencil? Pen Store has got you covered. As the name implies it’s a haven for anyone who takes their longhand-writing seriously. The store, located along Hornsgatan on Söder, has colorful writing –and drawing utensils in all shapes and sizes.

title: Polarn O. Pyret
label: Shop
text: The childrenswear brand Polar O. Pyret is as ubiquitous to Swedish parents as IKEA in Swedish living rooms. The company remade itself in the 70’s – from being a pharmacy – and since then their striped unisex children's clothes have become a design classic. Stores can be found all over Sweden and in many shopping malls.

title: Rodebjer
label: Shop
text: Swedish star designer Carin Rodebjer has two stores in Stockholm. She has received numerous awards over the years, including Elle’s Fashion Designer of the Year three times. Rodebjer’s collections are practical, elegant and feminine, with a touch of crudity and avant-garde. Recurring sources of inspiration are Swedish folk costumes, French bohemians of the 1920s, and the Finnish trash rock band Hanoi Rocks. Talk about contrasts! There is a second store on Regeringsgatan 50.

title: Rodebjer Revisited
label: Shop
text: Rodebjer, a Swedish fashion house founded in New York in 1999, is well-known for its timeless design and sustainable style. At Rodebjer Revisited, the brand takes it one step further, offering samples, unique pieces, and previous collections at reduced prices.

title: Rönnells Antikvariat
label: Shop
text: Rönnells has been a staple of Stockholm's literary scene since 1929. The store has a huge collection of used books, oddities and out-of-print rarities. The three floors host over 100 000 books, main in fiction, art, and academic literature. Here, the shop regularly hosts concerts and author talks, and has occasionally auctioned the private collections of famous authors.

title: Skultuna
label: Shop
text: Founded in 1607 just outside Västerås, Skultuna has produced accessories, candle holders, pots and other fine metal objects for over 400 years. The venerable company's older objects have become highly-sought after antiques and in the flagship store on Östermalm you'll find an assortment of their latest collections.

title: Söderbokhandeln Hansson & Bruce
label: Shop
text: Since 1927, Stockholm’s Söderbokhandeln Hansson & Bruce has been on Götgatsbacken. What it lacks in physical space it makes for up in inventory and overall cozy atmosphere. Söderbokhandeln also regularly hosts popular seminars and author talks.

title: Sound Pollution
label: Shop
text: Brutal sounds and distorted guitars; Sound Pollution is an oasis for fans of the heavier side of Rock. Heavy Metal, Thrash, Punk, Hardcore, Grind, Experimental Rock, Goth, Black Metal and more. If you’re not keen on heavy music; move along.

title: Sprall
label: Shop
text: Sprall’s award-winning children books have sold at museums all over the world. They also offer clothes, toys, furniture, and other quality products of their own design as well as foreign brands. Many of the products are fairtrade labeled and/or organic.

title: Stadshandel
label: Shop
text: Inspired by the old general stores of rural Sweden, Standshandel on Södermalm sells socially and environmentally sustainable household items and food items. Buy everything from toothbrushes and skin cream to yogurt and bread.

title: Sturegallerian
label: Shop
text: An exclusive mall in the middle of Stureplan square, with fashion boutiques, restaurants, cafés and the historic Sturebad spa, which opened in 1885.

title: Svenskt Tenn
label: Shop
text: The classic interior design company Svenskt Tenn has its flagship store on the beautiful shoreline boulevard of Strandvägen. The company originated with a fortuitous meeting between two courageous people with fresh ideas: the stylist and businesswoman Estrid Ericsson and the designer Josef Frank. The timeless, amazingly-patterned, and brilliantly colored creations are cause for a pilgrimage for anyone with an interest in design and interior furnishings. The store has modern classics, a lovely gift department with glass, pottery, and objects by younger established designers.

title: Tambur
label: Shop
text: Sustainability is the keyword when Tambur chooses its assortment of Swedish design. Everything in the small shop, no bigger than a one-room apartment, is picked with great care to be free from chemicals, locally produced and of the highest quality. And it doesn’t hurt if the products are beautiful to look at, as well.

title: Tid Watches
label: Shop
text: Stockholm based Tid designs uniquely stylish wrist watches. Fittingly, Tid is the Swedish word for time, and their goal is to create iconic products with a genuine value over time. You’ll find their main office and brand store on Torsgatan in Vasastan

title: Totême
label: Shop
text: Totême is a Swedish fashion brand founded by style journalist Elin Kling and her partner Karl Lindman in 2014. From their Stockholm studio, they design ready-to-wear, shoes, and accessories, with clear Scandinavian aesthetics. Totême has established personal relationships with the suppliers and factories they work with in order to secure fair products and circumstances in every step of the manufacturing chain. In 2020, they won 'Designer of the year' at the Swedish ELLE gala. The flagship store is located in the fashionable shopping street Biblioteksgatan in central Stockholm, and Totême is also represented with a shop in the luxury department store Nordiska Kompaniet in the city.

title: Triwa
label: Shop
text: More than a watch boutique, Triwa wants to bring change to the watch industry. Instead of making draconian status symbols the company wants their wristwatches to be stylish accessories with a more relaxed aura around them.

title: Uniforms for the Dedicated
label: Shop
text: Innovative, cutting-edge fashion for men. New purchases are brought home in “The Rag Bag,” which can be turned inside out and used to send in your used clothing for recycling at the same store.

title: Urban Bike Wear & the Mechanics
label: Shop
text: This complete cycling paradise is situated by Björns Trädgård on Södermalm. The staff is passionate about cycling culture and can answer just about any question on the topic. Want to buy a bike or just a frame? Maybe some rain gear? Whether you’re cycling to work or heading into the woods on your mountain bike, you’ll find what you need here with a focus on high-quality brands. The store also has a webshop and an adjacent bike workshop.

title: Växjö Elektriska
label: Shop
text: Family-owned Växjö Elektriska was founded in 1944, in southern Sweden. In 2017 the company opened a second store on Tegnérgatan in Stockholm. The boutique specializes in lamps, fixtures, and armatures. Besides some of the world’s leading manufacturers, you’ll find a large assortment of Swedish and Scandinavian brands as well.

title: Vintageaffischer
label: Shop
text: Vintageaffischer is the perfect place to find that retro poster you didn’t know you wanted to spruce up your apartment. While the store deals mainly in Swedish posters from the 60’s and 70’s – music, politics, art, movies, exhibition posters, public announcements, theater, fantasy motifs and ads – they occasionally carry international posters by famed artists.

title: Weekday
label: Shop
text: Weekday is a modern and mindful fashion and denim brand offering current international fashion influenced by Scandinavian style. Founded in Sweden in 2002, Weekday carries in-house brands as well as a selected offering of external designers. Stores at Götgatan 21, Södermalm and Drottninggatan 63 in the city center.

title: Westfield Mall of Scandinavia
label: Shop
text: Experience shopping, food, and entertainment in grand style at Stockholm's and Scandinavia's largest shopping center – Westfield Mall of Scandinavia. Here you will find 224 stores and restaurants offering the very best from Swedish and international brands, gastronomic experiences from all over the world, as well as Sweden’s only commercial IMAX® cinema. This popular shopping center is only a 7-minute ride from Stockholm’s Central Station.

title: Wos
label: Shop
text: If you are at all into accessories, Wos is your nirvana. Everything in the store is carefully selected or handmade by artists and designers. This is also the place to discover upcoming brands or find one-of-a-kind pieces!

title: Lökholmen
text: Lökholmen is a small island of breathtaking beauty, just north of Sandön, with one imposing feature; a 20th-century fortification with canons overlooking the guest harbor. Built by coal magnate Kurt Heinecke, the fortification and its adjacent mansion today serve as the clubhouse for the Royal Swedish Yacht Club and as a hostel for members and non-members alike. Lökholmen can be reached by taxi boat from Sandhamn.

title: Östersjöns Drottning
label: Excursion
text: Viveca Steen might be the queen of Swedish crime literature, but the lighthouse on the small island of Grönskär is the queen of the archipelago. The 26-meter-tall building (just over 86 feet) – named Östersjöns Drottning, literally “Queen of the Baltic sea” – has helped seafarers navigate through the eastern inlet of the archipelago since 1770. To visit Grönskär you can rent a taxi boat from Sandhamn on Sandön as there are no regular ferry lines to the island.

title: Svenska Högarna
label: Excursion
text: On the eastern reaches of the archipelago, just before islands and skerries give way to the open sea, you’ll find Svenska Högarna. To get to this remote small group of islands you’ll have to arrange transport through the island supervisor, but it’s sure worth a visit.The largest island, Storön, has one of the archipelago’s few lighthouses that is manned all year. It also houses a weather station and a handful of residents. The locals are friendly and will happily give you a tour of the islands. Svenska Högarna is a popular pit-stop for migrating birds and during winter time you can spot grey seals and long-tailed ducks in the surrounding waters.

title: The Secret Garden
label: Restaurant
text: The Secret Garden is an honest and open-minded bar, restaurant and nightclub in the heart of Stockholm - Gamla Stan. Have a quiet dinner in their hidden garden, a glass or two with a view, a fun night of dancing, or all of it. They're open every day from 12 to 03, and their DJ's are playing beats Wednesdays through Saturdays from 10 p.m.

title: Bellmansgatan 1
label: Attraction
text: Mikael Blomkvist’s home address. The apartment is located on the hills of the historic Söder district. Several key scenes in the Millennium adventure are set here.

title: Fiskargatan 9
label: Sevärdhet
text: At this upscale address on Södermalm with a view of Djurgården and Gamla Stan, Lisbeth Salander buys an apartment with 21 rooms, of which she occupies only three. The name on the door is “V. Kulla”, in a nod to “Villa Villekulla”, home of the children’s book character Pippi Longstocking.

title: Kaffebar
label: Coffee Shop / Café
text: Kaffebar, formerly known as Mellqvists Kaffebar, is a cozy coffee shop on Södermalm known for its excellent coffee and great atmosphere. It's was also for being Stieg Larsson's real-life hangout and is prominently featured in the Millenium books. Perhaps this is the very place where he sat and developed the plots of the novels?

title: Rigoletto
label: Activity
text: A classic theatre and the main premiere cinema in Stockholm opened in 1939. Located in the city center, at Kungsgatan. The largest auditorium has 756 seats, and the venue includes a VIP balcony and lounge with a bar.

title: Bio Skandia
label: Activity
text: The classic single-screen cinema Bio Skandia has presented movies in Stockholm since the early twentieth century. Since 2024, its managed by the Stockholm International Film Festival and screens niche films as well as mainstream movies.It is undoubtedly one of Stockholm’s most beautiful theaters, originally designed by world-renowned architect Gunnar Asplund and is adorned with works by many major artists of the twentieth century. The auditorium is designed to produce a sense of being outside.

title: Bagarmossen subway station
label: Attraction
text: Bagarmossen’s former subway station is to date the first and only to have been closed down and taken out of service. Where it once was situated at surface-level there now are residential buildings.The old station opened in 1958 and was the terminus for the green line no. 17 until 1994 when the subway was extended to Skarpnäck to the south. To accommodate the underground extension, the old Bagarmossen station had to be taken out of use, and a new one was built underground. And with the new station came new beautiful art; Gert Marcus screen painted glass-plates adorning the walls."The art doesn’t represent anything particularly", says art guide Marie Andersson. "But it is typical of Marcus’s oeuvre to work with color denominations in almost seamless transitions".

contact_text.text: Bagarmossen is on the subway's green line no. 17.

title: Citybanan – Odenplan
label: Attraction
text: Citybanan, a new track for Stockholm’s commuter trains that connects T-Centralen directly with Odenplan, was completed in 2017 with new platforms and new art by 14 artists on the stations.Hanging down from the ceiling of Odenplan’s western entrance hallway, “Life Line” is one of Citybanan's most eye-catching pieces. The piece by David Svensson consists of jagged white lines of fluorescent light, shining brightly in the tunnels. Obviously, the 400 meters of LED-lighting serves a practical purpose, but they’re also of a personal nature explains art guide, Marie Andersson:"The shape of the lights was inspired by the heartbeats of the artist’s son, as shown on the CTG-monitor during the childbirth".

contact_text.text: Odenplan is on the subway's green line. You can reach it by taking the no. 17, 18 or 19 train.

title: Hallonbergen subway station
label: Attraction
text: The first tenants of Hallonbergen’s typical Swedish “Millon Program”-apartment blocks moved into the suburb in 1969, but construction continued until the mid-’70s when Hallonbergen also got its own metro station.With Hallonbergen's relatively young age in mind, it’s probably no coincidence that the artists Elis Eriksson and Gösta Wallmark were inspired by their own childhoods when decorating the subway station. Looking at the artwork can best be described as peeking into the vivid imagination of a child, with colorful drawings of fantastical beasts and imaginative contraptions.­"Eriksson and Wallmark actually used their childhood drawings and drawings made by their own children", says art guide Marie Andersson. "The station’s name itself [Hallonbergen literally means “Raspberry Mountains”] sounds almost like something plucked from a fairytale".

contact_text.text: Hallonbergen is on the subway's blue line no. 11.

title: Hötorget subway station
label: Attraction
text: In 1952, Hötorget was built as the southern terminus of Stockholm’s second subway line, going northwest to the then newly built suburb of Vällingby.As with all below-surface stations from the early 1950s (other examples being Slussen, Medborgarplatsen, Skanstull, Odenplan, and Rådmansgatan), Hötorget’s walls are covered in square bathroom tiles, and when it opened up for traffic, that was pretty much it.In fact, none of the early metro stations had any public art at the time of their opening. Stockholm’s politicians were simply put indifferent to the idea of stations being anything else than functional pit-stops. They were content with having billboard ads on the walls. It wasn’t until after a decade’s worth of discussions, debates, and op-eds by the Swedish art community that art got its place in the subway. The artists pointed to Sweden’s long history of public art displays as their most important argument, explains art guide Marie Andersson."Public art is considered to be democratic art because it gives everyone the opportunity to experience good quality art in their everyday lives. And not only people who can afford to buy art or visit galleries and museums".And when T-Centralen and Gamla Stan were being planned – two new stations that would connect the southern and northern lines to one single stretch of subway tracks – a contest was organized to determine the artwork.Since then, public art has become an integral part of Stockholm’s subway. Over time all the early stations have been either redecorated or had artworks installed. And in 1998, Gun Gordillo's bright neon-lights were installed in the ceiling of Hötorget. By that time the original interior had become classic and was left virtually untouched. The tile work, platform signs, benches – even wastebaskets – were preserved to keep the 50’s atmosphere.

contact_text.text: Hötorget is on the subway's green line. You can reach it by taking the no. 17, 18 or 19 train.

title: Kungsträdgården subway station
label: Attraction
text: One of Stockholm’s most stunning stations is unsurprisingly also one of its most photographed: Kungsträdgården. Located in the middle of downtown Stockholm, it’s the terminus of the blue line, or at least until its southward extension opens in 2025.Kungsträdgården is one of Stockholm’s oldest public parks. The name, roughly meaning “The King’s Garden”, is derived from the area’s royal history. Between 1643 and 1825 it was the site of the majestic Makalös Palace, and a beautiful French garden. After Makalös burned down, the site was used for military exercises. Finally, in 1875, the park landed in the care of the Stockholm City Council, which in turn opened it for the public."Almost everything on the station tells the story of the site above ground", says Marie Andersson, subway art guide. "The color scheme – red, white and green – is a reference to the old French formal garden and statues around the station are actually replicas of Makalös Palace’s exterior art".Another unique feature of Kungsträdgården is its fauna. The station is the only place in Northern Europe where the cave-dwelling Lessertia dentichelis-spider can be found. Presumably, the species hitched a ride on equipment and machines traveling from Southern Europe when the station was being built."Nobody knows exactly how they ended up here", continues Marie Andersson. "But they seem to be thriving. I saw one just yesterday, as a matter of fact. In 2016 scientists also discovered a previously unknown fungus on the station walls with a unique DNA-structure".

contact_text.text: Kungsträdgården is on the subway's blue line. It can be reached by taking the no. 10 and 11 trains.

title: Mörby Centrum subway station
label: Attraction
text: At first glance, Mörby Centrum’s station art might seem unassuming. Except for the colorful tilework embedded in the bedrock, the color scheme is light and almost subdued. But as art guide Marie Andersson explains it, the color is actually an optical illusion."The walls actually change color depending on where you stand on the platform. From one end the room appears white with a light shade of pink, and from the other white and grayish-green". The effect was achieved by first lighting the wall and painting its shadows from one side, and then from the other. The artists, Gösta Wessel and Karin Ek wanted to emphasize the changing landscape on a journey, not only on the platform itself but more importantly from your starting point to your destination.

contact_text.text: Mörby Centrum is on the subway's red line no. 14

title: Östermalmstorg subway station
label: Attraction
text: Situated approximately 23 meters below sea level (roughly 75 feet), Östermalmstorg is the third deepest subway station in Stockholm’s metro system. The station, completed in 1965, lies in the heart of the city’s poshest and most expensive boroughs; Östermalm.Although the station displays several works of art by different artists, the centerpiece is Siri Derkert’s sketches adorning the station walls. The pictures blasted into pitch-black rock walls covered in white concrete, are both playful and personal. Derkert was 77 years old when the station opened and the station’s art was in a sense a summary of her extraordinary body of work."The central themes in her art are all represented on the walls", says art guide Marie Andersson. "When walking around the station you will see the word “peace” written in different languages, you will see portraits of people that had been working for the environment and with women’s rights issues".Derkert’s involvement in the women’s rights movement is evident in the historical figures depicted on the walls. Many are women from the Fogelstad group, a women’s art collective which Derkert was a member of.

contact_text.text: Östermalmstorg is on the subway's red line. It can be reached by taking the no. 13 and 14 trains.

title: Solna Centrum subway station
label: Attraction
text: The station of Solna Centrum opened with the first arm of the blue line in 1975. The bright green and red landscape - the green being the forest and the red an evening sun setting behind the treetops - is both timeless in its beauty, but also something that few other stations artwork is; political.After completing the walls artists Karl-Olov Björk and Anders Åberg felt they were lacking. So they continued adding various details and scenes to the forest."Originally the walls were supposed to be only green and red", explains art guide Marie Andersson. "So the rest of the paintings were pretty much improvised. This resulted in pictures that illustrated some of the most debated societal topics in 70’s era Sweden; the environment, deforestation, and the depopulation of rural areas".

contact_text.text: Solna Centrum is on the subway's blue line no. 11.

title: Solna Strand subway station
label: Attraction
text: The contrast between the heavenly cubes – jutting out from the ceiling and platform at Solna Strand – and the dark cave, is characteristic of Takashi Naraha’s art. The Japanese artist often uses a yin-and-yang-theme in his work, explains art guide Marie Andersson."It’s the foundation of his pieces, there’s often a balance between light and darkness. And in the way that the platform’s cubes mirror the open sky above ground, the black cube just outside the station entrance relates to the dark cave below ground".

contact_text.text: Solna Strand is on the subway's blue line no. 10.

title: Stadion subway station
label: Attraction
text: Each year Östermalms IP serves as the main festival area for the Stockholm Pride festival. By coincidence, the nearby subway station (Stadion) happens to have a beautiful rainbow in vivid colors painted against the bright blue of the station's cave walls to welcome festival-goers. The station is one of Stockholm’s first cave stations, a controversial subject when it was built in 1973, explains art guide Marie Andersson. "There were actual fears that people would associate these cave stations with the netherworld and other nasty places. So the bright blue and the rainbow serves as a reminder that there is a sky not far above".The station’s artists, Åke Pallarp and Enno Hallek, not only wanted to bring the sky underground but also remind passengers of Stadion’s significance in sports history. Close by is The Stockholm Olympic Stadium, the site for the 1912 Olympics, and each year between 1913 and 1965 the Swedish bandy finals. Today, Stadion is still one of Stockholm’s great arenas and regularly hosts sports events and concerts.

contact_text.text: Stadion is on the subway's red line no. 14

title: T-Centralen subway station
label: Attraction
text: T-Centralen, the nexus of Stockholm’s subway system, opened up for traffic in 1957 and was the first station to feature artwork. The blue line-platform, quite literally “the blue platform” is hands down one of the public transport system’s most recognizable places. But it didn’t open until 1975 when the blue line to Hjulsta was completed.Painting a platform on the subway’s blue line almost entirely in, well… blue might seem a little on the nose. Art guide Marie Andersson theorizes that the artist Per Olof Ultvedt not only chose the blue shades based on their aesthetic values but also their relaxing effect."­I think Per Olof Ultvedt wanted to create a calming atmosphere because this is a station where people are in a hurry. They are changing trains to another metro line or another commuter train. I suppose the idea was that the blue color together with the simple motifs – stylized flowers and leaf creepers – gives passengers pause and a chance to clear their mind".

contact_text.text: T-Centralen can be reached by all subway trains in Stockholm.

title: Tekniska Högskolan subway station
label: Attraction
text: Kungliga Tekniska Högskolan (KTH Royal Institute of Technology) was founded in 1827 and has since then had famous alumni like Christer Fuglesang, Dolph Lundgren, and Anette Scheibe pass its exams. In 1973 Tekniska Högskolan finally got its own subway station, to help students and professors get to their classes.Unsurprisingly, the award-winning station (with art by Lennart Mörk) is a celebration of scientific advances and discoveries. The most eye-catching are probably the five regular polyhedra located on the platform, each one representing one of Plato’s five elements: fire, water, air, earth, and ether.– You’ll also find representations of Copernican heliocentrism, Polhem’s mechanical alphabet, Newton’s three laws of motion, and da Vinci’s attempts at creating a flying machine, explains art guide, Marie Andersson.

contact_text.text: Tekniska högskolan is on the subway's red line no. 14

title: Tensta subway station
label: Attraction
text: The Suburb of Tensta was built between 1966 and 1972 to accommodate a Stockholm that was growing and in need of more residential housing. Although it was part of the building plans from the beginning, the station of Tensta wasn’t ready until 1975.Artist Helga Henschen, together with Arne Sedell and her brother Lars, spent over a year decorating the station’s platform with a colorful display of animal sculptures and stylized leaves against a bright white wall. Since Tensta has always had a majority of residents who immigrated to Sweden, the artists wanted the station to feel welcoming no matter where your roots are, explains art guide Marie Andersson."The various pieces are called “A rose for the immigrants”, “Solidarity”, “Kinship”. The words written around the station are a celebration of all the people from different cultures living in Tensta".

contact_text.text: Tensta is on the subway's blue line no. 10.

title: Thorildsplan subway station
label: Attraction
text: Thorildsplan is one of only three street-level surface stations in downtown Stockholm. The station was built in 1952, but the pixelated artwork by Lars Arrhenius is a more recent addition. Arrhenius was commissioned to create new art in 2008, the caveat being that it had to be tile work. Otherwise, he had total creative freedom, but considering his background the material was a perfect fit.While planning his work, he drew inspiration from Thorildplan’s surroundings. The street crossings, rondos, elevated sidewalks, elevators, and stairs reminded him of intricate video game levels. Clearly, this also resulted in a work that borrows from 8-bit aesthetics - a source of inspiration that runs through his whole body of work - with pixelated clouds, mushroom power-ups, and projectiles."SL and Konstrådet [Stockholm Public Transport and the Stockholm Art Council; the two governing bodies over the subway and public art of Stockholm respectively] only chose art based on the artist’s submissions", explains art guide Marie Andersson. "They never bring suggestions to the table beforehand. And besides, there’s no rule that says that subway art must have a literal connection to a station. Sure, Kungsträdgården’s station art is a mirror of the station’s name. But the maritime-themed Fridhemsplan on the other hand obviously doesn’t depict what’s above ground".

contact_text.text: Thorildsplan is on the subway's green line. You can reach it by taking the no. 17, 18 or 19 train.

title: Magasinet i Vaxholm
label: Restaurant
text: Magasinet, located on the waterfront in idyllic Vaxholm, is more than a restaurant serving hungry archipelago-visitors. The old smithy has been turned into a yoga studio, design shop, and bistro, serving lunch every day and brunch on weekends.
mass_info: Some restaurants and cafés in the Stockholm archipelago are closed during fall and winter. Be sure to check their webpage if you're planning a visit outside of the spring and summer season!

title: Remedy
label: Activity
text: A boutique studio on Östermalm where physical wellness, contemporary workout forms, and spiritual well-being meet. Take a class in Pilates, Garuda, or Barre or enjoy sound healing and the infrared sauna.

title: Release Co.
label: Activity
text: Release Co., the first vitamin therapy-clinic in Sweden, specializing in intravenous and intramuscular treatment. Treated by trained medical professionals you'll receive either vitamin-IVs' or drink vitamin shots to boost your body and spirit.

title: Santosh Clothing
label: Shop
text: Santosh Clothing opened its doors in 2011 on Östermalm, specializing in garments made from highly durable cashmere. The fabric is sourced from herders on the Mongolian tundra, and the garments are made in Santosh’s factory in Ulaanbaatar under ethical and sustainable standards.

title: Galleri Sebastian Schildt
label: Shop
text: Sebastian Schildt is one of the most renowned jewelers and silversmiths in Sweden. The gallery bearing his name, on Östermalm, not only showcases his latest creations but also organizes exhibitions by some of Sweden's leading contemporary artists.

title: Märta Larsson
label: Shop
text: Märta Larsson got into jewelry design during her time as vocalist for The Don’t Fucking Cares. Basically, she wanted custom-made rings and necklaces to wear during the band’s live shows. Today she has branched out into clothes and accessories, but with the same punk-rock ruggedness that makes her jewelry so unique.

contact_text.text: At the moment, Märta Larsson hasn't got a flagship store. But you can either find the latest collections online, or at Svenskt Tenn and her showroom at JUS.

title: Café Uddvillan
label: Coffee Shop / Café
text: Finish (or start) a lovely walk in Vinterviken, with some coffee and raspberry pie at Café Uddvillan. The café is located in an old mansion overlooking lake Mälaren, offering some rustic charm in the suburb of Hägersten.

title: Järvafältet
label: Park
text: Järvafältet is a large forested area, connecting several of Stockholm's northern suburbs, like Kista, Akalla, Solna, and Sundbyberg. A popular place for outdoor activities, you'll find hiking trails, meadows, ponds, and several nature reserves like Hansta nature reserve and Järvafältets nature reserve.

title: Enskedeparkens Bageri
label: Coffee Shop / Café
text: Enskedeparkens Bageri lies in the suburbian villa idyll of Enskede, next to a riding school and allotment gardens. The café is small, with only a few tables, but the patio is open all-year-round and their famous cinnamon buns are worth a trip alone, no matter the weather.

title: Chelas
label: Restaurant
text: Chelas is Mexican slang for beer, and that gives you a hint of what this trendy restaurant is all about: Mexican food and drinks. The beer-battered fish tacos are a favorite among Hornstull locals who have made Chelas their go-to restaurant. Dogs are also welcome!

title: Sibyllans Kaffe & Tehandel
label: Shop
text: Small and personal teashop and coffee roastery in Östermalm. Sibyllan's was founded in 1916 and most of the décor has remained intact ever since. Drop by for a tea tasting, and you'll probably find yourself walking out with their immensely popular tea blend Sir William's, named after the founder Hilmer Hansson's brother.

title: Brasserie Astoria
label: Restaurant
text: Brasserie Astoria on Nybrogatan is Michelin-starred chef Björn Frantzén’s latest Stockholm endeavor. Housed in a former cinema, Astoria is opts for a more relaxed dinner experience than the inventive kitchen wizardy at three starred Frantzén. You’ll be treated to classic dishes from the French and Italian culinary traditions – pasta carbonara, Moules frites and Cesar salad to name a few ­– served in a casual atmosphere.

title: Spotify
label: Company
text: Spotify is a Swedish audio streaming and media services provider, launched in October 2008. Today, Spotify is the world’s most popular audio streaming subscription service with 320 million users, including 144 million subscribers, across 92 markets.

title: TrueCaller
label: Company
text: Truecaller is a Swedish company founded in 2009 in Stockholm, Sweden by Nami Zarringhalam and Alan Mamedi. Today, Truecaller is loved by over 150 million daily active users around the world, and is the go-to app for Caller ID, spam blocking and payments.

title: Karma
label: Company
text: Karma is a food rescue app that allows retailers to sell their surplus food to consumers at a lower price instead of having great food go to waste. Karma was founded in Stockholm in November 2016 by Hjalmar Ståhlberg Nordegren, Elsa Bernadotte, Ludvig Berling and Mattis Larsson.

title: Klarna
label: Company
text: Klarna was founded in Stockholm, Sweden and is Europe’s highest valued private fintech company. It offers products and services to consumers and retailers within payments, social shopping, and personal finances.

title: Ericsson
label: Company
text: Ericsson is a Swedish multinational networking and telecommunications company headquartered in Stockholm. It was founded 140 years ago on the premise that access to communications is a basic human need.

title: Furhat Robotics
label: Company
text: Furhat Robotics is a Stockholm-based startup building the world’s most advanced social robotics and conversational AI platform. With roots in 20+ years of research, the vision is to build a human-like computer interface that enables people to interact with machines in the same way that humans interact with each other – by speaking, listening and showing emotions.

title: King
label: Company
text: Founded in Stockholm in 2003, King is a leading interactive entertainment company for the mobile world. It has developed more than 200 fun titles, offering games that are enjoyed all around the world.

title: Nyföretagarcentrum
label: Advisory service
text: NyföretagarCentrum provides free support for people who are considering setting up, or have recently set up, their own company.

title: Antler
label: Venture Capital
text: Global early-stage VC that enables and invests in the defining companies of tomorrow.

title: iZettle
label: Company
text: iZettle is a Swedish financial technology company, now owned by PayPal. It was one of the first companies to develop a chip-card reader and mobile payments app that complies with international security requirements.

title: Telia
label: Company
text: Telia is a Swedish multinational telecommunications company and mobile network operator present in Sweden, Finland, Norway, Denmark, Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia. Its approximately 20,800 employees serve millions of customers every day in one of the world’s most connected regions.

title: The Local Europe
label: Company
text: The Local is a Stockholm-founded English-language digital news publisher with local editions in nine European countries. Coverage is purely domestic in each country, and includes current events, politics, business, sports and culture, as well as analysis and opinion.

title: Climeon
label: Company
text: Climeon is a public company, listed on the Stockholm Nasdaq Stock Exchange. The company is located in Stockholm, Sweden and has 90+ employees. Climeon has customers and partners all over the world and in various industries.

title: Heatpower
label: Company
text: Heatpower.com was started thanks to the support of initial funding from clean tech company Climeon. The mission is to raise awareness about heat power, and make sure it is considered alongside other renewable energies.

title: Kognity
label: Company
text: Founded in Sweden, Kognity was designed to redefine the traditional textbook and supercharge the learning process as we know it. Today, Kognity is loved by thousands of students, in hundreds of schools, in over 100 countries.

title: Trustly
label: Company
text: Trustly is a Fintech company that develops and sells online payment solutions. Its mission is to make online bank payments convenient for everyone by connecting consumers and merchants through the bank account - the hub of people’s financial life.

title: Tieto
label: Company
text: Tieto is a leading digital services and software company with local presence and global capabilities. Headquartered in Finland, Tieto employs around 24 000 experts globally.

title: Bemz
label: Company
text: Bemz creates custom sewn design covers in hundreds of high-end fabrics so that you can update your IKEA sofa, armchairs, chairs and more to reflect your own personal style. It was founded over 13 years ago when Lesley Pennington adopted the Swedish dream lifestyle and bought a summer house by the sea.

title: Instabridge
label: Company
text: Instabridge is a Swedish-founded app that lets you easily access thousands of free WiFi hotspots around the world as well as share all the free hotspots you find with your friends.

title: Fishbrain
label: Company
text: Fishbrain is a tech startup with a global user base of over 10 million anglers. Fishbrain works with the latest tech, from AR to machine learning and is backed by the investors behind some of the most successful social networks and apps.

title: Globhe
label: Company
text: Globhe collects data for the purpose of predicting or preventing disasters and outbreaks. The drones are used to collect data via images, for example malaria outbreaks or natural disasters. Globhe is connected to nearly 4000 drone-pilots in 77 countres, a number that is growing every week.

title: THING Stockholm
label: Company
text: THINGS is the #1 industry focused deep tech and innovation hub in Sweden, located on the KTH (The Royal Institute of Technology) campus. It is a 2,000m2 co-working space for startups, connected to an extended community of close corporate partners, including some of the most successful and innovative export companies in Sweden.

contact.address: Drottning Kristinas väg 53, Stockholm, Sweden, 11428 Stockholm

title: Detectify
label: Company
text: Detectify was founded in 2013 and quickly became one of the most talked about startups in the field of web security. It has since received worldwide recognition for its security research, won several awards and nominations and attracted customers from a wide range of industries and company sizes.

title: Bontouch
label: Company
text: Bontouch is a software-as-a-service company serving clients in North America, Europe and Asia from five innovation studios in Sweden, London and New York.

title: Watty
label: Company

title: Stockholm Olympic Stadium
label: Attraction
text: The Stockholm Olympic Stadium, commonly referred to as just "Stadion", was built as the main venue for the 1912 Olympiad in Stockholm. Initially, Torben Grut, the stadium's architect, planned for a provisional arena made of wooden boards painted white. But when it was decided that it was to become a permanent landmark Grut opted for a majestic brick construction instead, inspired by Ragnar Östberg's constructions and the Visby City Wall, in a typical Swedish National Romantic style. The arena is also decorated with small patterns and reliefs embedded in the brickwork, and you'll also find statues by Carl Eldh and Carl Fagerberg.Stadion is not just a beloved historical landmark but also a cherished cultural hub. Before modern arenas like Tele2 and Friends were built in the 21st century, Stadion was the obvious concert venue for international superstars visiting Stockholm during the summer. In fact, the arena is still used to this day for concerts and sports events, which makes it the world's oldest Olympic arena still in use. It's also open to the public every day, for anyone who wants a morning jog or practice some soccer out on the field.

label: Coffee Shop / Café
text: At the edge of Grimsta nature reserve, just a stone's throw from the Kanaan public beach, you'll find Kanaans trädgårdscafé overlooking Lake Mälaren. The indoor café is open all-year round but in the spring and summer the café opens up its outdoor area and garden bar, as well as its petanque-courses.

title: Get Out Kayak
label: Activity
text: Get Out Kayak helps explorers that want to go out on a self-guided Archipelago adventure. Starting from one of their bases – Stavsnäs, Bullandö, or Sollenkroka – you can rent kayaks and outdoor equipment (like tents and portable stoves) for either a short paddle, a weekend adventure, or a whole week of exploration. If you're unsure of where to start, they've also prepared a kayaking trail split into three stages offering various kinds of challenges and sights.

title: Botkyrka Konsthall
label: Museum
text: Botkyrka Konsthall is an art hall exhibiting modern art by both international and local artists. The space, housed in the same building as Fittja bibliotek, regularly hosts various workshops and art events. The arthall also runs the Xetmuseum in Tumba, showcasing art by Sven Xet Erixon.

title: Konsthall C
label: Museum
text: Konsthall C in the southern suburb of Hökarängen is one of a kind. Housed in a former industrial laundry building, it started as an art experiment but is now both a permanent exhibition hall and place of work for artists, authors, researchers, and more. The area of Hökarängen itself is worth a trip, especially if you're interested in Swedish post-war architecture. Besides Konsthall C, you'll find several culturally significant buildings and areas, like the Skönstaholm townhouses and the "zig-zag"-building on Fagersjövägen.

title: Pontonen
label: Restaurant
text: Pontonen is a centrally located summerbar att Norr Mälarstrand on Kungsholmen. Have a fresh cocktail and modern Swedish food while enjoying the view of Lake Mälaren and Södermalm.

title: Öppet Hav
label: Activity
text: Öppet Hav has various exciting ways to explore the archipelago. Either from a helicopter, a R.I.B, sailbot or seaplane. Öppet hav also offers a variety of activities in the city, like segway sightseeing, escape rooms and archery.

title: Chili Masala
label: Restaurant
text: Chili Masala in the suburb of Solna specializes in punjabi-cuisine from the region of the same name in India and Pakistan. Well-seasoned Karai, Tikka and Tawa-dishes cooked the traditional way in a degh-pan.

title: Blidösundsbolaget
label: Activity
text: Blindösundbolaget organizes both day trips and evening trips, as well as tours that combine the scenic sights of the archipelago with live music on board.On the ships S/S Storskär and S/S Norrskär, you can book lunch and dinner cruises during spring, summer, and autumn.During the summer, S/S Blidösund offers Blidösund Live – music cruises featuring live performances on board, where you can enjoy the concert alongside a meal in the restaurant.

title: Ekhagens strandbad
label: Activity
text: Ekhagens strandbad, commonly refered to as "Lappis beach" is a public beack at Lilla Värtan on Norra Djurgården. There's no parking, changing rooms, or café on-site. You can reach Lappis Beach by taking bus no. 50 to Lektorstigen and then take a short walk.

title: Ängbybadet
label: Activity
text: Ängbybadet in Bromma, one of northern Stockholm's most beloved beaches, is widely known for it's excellent water quality. The area was turned into a public beach in 1936, has changing room and a small coffee -and ice cream shop, and has been modernized for people with accessibility needs . The easiest way to find it is by taking a 10 minute walk from Ängbyplan's metro station.

title: Mångkulturellt Centrum
label: Attraction
text: Mångkulturellt Centrum is an exhibition hall and culture hub in Fittja, working towards a society where diversity and migration are an integral part of Sweden's cultural heritage. You'll also find the restaurant Tavernan here, serving climate-friendly and vegetarian dishes with inspiration from Jamaica.

title: Amida
label: Restaurant
text: Popular street-food joint Amida has been serving Turkish barbecue staples like döner, falafel, köfte, and iskender since 2002. The original restaurant is on Folkungagatan on Södermalm but you'll also find them in Kungens Kurva, Sollentuna and Sundbyberg.

title: Minh Mat
label: Restaurant
text: Minh Mat serves typical Vietnamese dishes – frogs legs, autumn rolls, and deep-fried tofu – in the traditional "ăn chơi"-style. The restaurant is located on Odengatan just by Vasaparkan, just a short walk from S:t Eriksplan metro station.

title: Eatnam
label: Restaurant
text: Eatnam serves Vietnamese-cuisine, with ingredients and spices inspired by the everyday food in Saigon. Pho-soup, banh mi-sandwiches, fresh spring rolls and noodle salad. The restaurant originally opened on Odengatan but also has locations on Östermalm and Södermalm.

title: Sweden History Tours
label: Activity
text: Sweden History Tours organizes guided tours perfect for history buffs. Get to know the infamous Vikings, get in-depth knowledge about Scandinavian folklore or learn about the royal castles in the Stockholm area. You can either join a guided tour or book a personal guide, and the tours are available in Swedish, English, and German.

title: Storholmen Viking Village
label: Attraction
text: Storholmen is a summertime open-air museum, wholly devoted to the fascinating history of Vikings. The museum is located in Norrtälje, roughly an hour's drive north of Stockholm, by the Iron Age burial mounds at lake Erken. Take a guided tour through the village, try your hand at Viking crafts or take part in the Viking games!

title: Hammarby Sjöstad
label: Attraction
text: Hammarby Sjöstad is one of the most recent additions to Stockholm's cityscape and was built between 1994-2020. Most of the buildings are located around Lake Hammarby, an area that had previously been known as the "Lugnet" industrial park. But a portion of the new neighborhood is located across the canal on Södermalm. Initially, the idea was for "Sjöstaden" to act as the Olympic Village during the 2004 Olympic Summer Games in Stockholm, before being turned into a permanent residential area. Although Stockholm lost the bid for the games the construction went ahead. When it was completed it was comprised of 12 700 apartments, many restaurants, and shops, and had four stops along the newly constructed Tvärbanan-tram. During the expansion on the Stockholm metro, one of the new stations will be built in Hammarby Sjöstad. The architecture is an excellent example of the urban supermodernism that was in vogue during the '90s. Simple and clean shapes and materials, that put function before form. Its central location made open spaces and daylight something of a commodity, which was compensated by large windows, balconies, and higher ceilings. Since the project took over 15 years to complete, small differences can be found when comparing the first buildings with the more recent ones. Uniform for the whole area though is its high environmental profile. Already in its planning stages, Hammarby Sjöstad was meant to spearhead sustainable city-planing. For example, Lake Hammarby and its surrounding area were restored having been polluted by the industries in "Lugnet", and eco-friendly materials were used during the construction.

title: ShareKayak
label: Activity
text: ShareKayak is a self-service kayak rental, that lets users rent a kayak at one of their stations with the help of a dedicated app.

title: Sandhamnsguiderna
label: Activity
text: Sandhamnsguiderna offers various exciting activities in and around the popular island of Sandhamn. Guided tours of the village, seal safari, kayak rental, guided fishing tours, and much more. The various tours are available in Swedish, English, and German.

title: Stavsudda Kajakdepå
label: Activity
text: At Stavsudda Kajakdepå, on the island of Norra Stavsudda you can rent kayaks to explore the surronding islands at your own pace. Norra Stavsudda. Located in the central archipelago it's a great starting point for a day full of beautiful vistas and exploration.

title: Själbottna och Östra Lagnö naturreservat
label: Excursion
text: Själbottna and Östra Lagnö are two adjacent nature reserves, located on opposite sides of the Storfladen bay I the area of the Stockholm archipelago known as Rosslagen.Själbottna can be reached by taking Waxholmbolagets summer ferries or by boat taxi, while a bus from Danderyd will take just a two-kilometer walk from Östra Lagnö. Both offer serene nature with thick pine forests, old oak trees, lovely forest paths, and great spots for a swim in the ocean.

title: Saigon Baguette Gamla Brogatan
label: Restaurant
text: Popular Saigon Baguette in central Stockholm specializes in spicy bánh mi-sandwiches: crispy baguettes filled with vegetables, fresh herbs and chili, and marinated meat or tofu. The menu also offers various rice and noodle-dishes, Pho-soup, bubble tea, ice coffee, and Vietnamese beer, rice vodka and rice wine.

title: Esperia
label: Restaurant
text: Esperia on Sankt Paulsgatan serves genuine Greek cuisine in a relaxed environment. Either order several small dishes (mezatas) to share with your company, or order a larger dish. You'll find staples like souvláki, saganáki, orzo and deep-fried calamari on the menu.

title: Nostimo
label: Coffee Shop / Café
text: Greek cafés are a rarity in Stockholm, but Nostimo on Sveavägen is just that. The menu offer both lunches – gyros and spanakopita (spinach and feta cheese pie) – and bougatsa pastries with either Fred espresso or regular coffee.

title: Restaurang Cypern
label: Restaurant
text: Cypriot cuisine is heavily influenced by both Greek and Turkish food, something you'll be able to experience first-hand at Restaurang Cypern on Valhallavägen. Moussaka, bifteki, halloumi, or a fresh salad as a main, followed by a baklava or yoghurt mastiha for dessert.

title: Wäng Izakaya
label: Restaurant
text: Pan-Asian restaurant Wäng Izakaya is all about the beloved classics of Asian cuisine. Japanese sushi and sashimi, Korean bibimbap-bowls, spicy fried rice from Singapore, Pad Thai from Thailand, or Vietnamese Pho-soup. You can have them all, in one place.

title: Machi Machi
label: Coffee Shop / Café
text: Machi Machi is a tea house catering to sweet-tooths. Choose between Créme Brulee, Strawberry with cream cheese, or a zesty tea with fresh fruits. They also have a large selection of Taiwanese "boba teas"; flavored teas with sweet and chewy tapioca bubbles.

title: Bodyflight
label: Activity
text: Who has not dreamed of flying? In bodyflight (or indoor skydiving) you get to feel what it is like to fly in free fall without actually jumping out of an airplane. You fly on an air jet in a glass chamber with a safety net below. Certified instructors accompany first-time pilots into the flight chamber.

title: Indio
label: Restaurant
text: Indio is Sweden's first Nikkei-restaurant; a fusion between Japanese and Peruvian culinary traditions that arose in the late 18th century when farmers from Japan emigrated across the Pacific to Peru. The menu features, among other delicacies, unique sushi and sashimi and Nikkei-style ceviche and tiradito.

title: Wira Bruk
label: Attraction
text: For 140 years, between 1635 and 1775, Wira Bruk was Sweden's most important smithy supplying the Swedish army with sharp blades. As time went on the smithy pivoted its production to farm tool, like axes and scythes, until it closed down in the 1960's. Today, Wira Bruk is a museum where visitors can get a glimpse of it's storied production and learn more about the lives of the people that lived and died here.

title: Ninecha Milk Tea
label: Coffee Shop / Café
text: Ninecha Milk Tea on Katarinagatan serves chilled tea drinks in various flavors. Refreshingly fruity, creamy or in different sweet bubble tea-variants.

title: Yi Fang
label: Coffee Shop / Café
text: The bubble tea-café Yi Fang serves fruity and refreshing drinks made from only natural ingredients. Fresh fruit, cane sugar, and their homemade tapioca pearls cooked every morning before opening hours,

title: Cha Talk
label: Coffee Shop / Café
text: Popular Cha Talk in Vasastan serves bubble tea, juice tea and flavored milk tea in various blends. For a lighter snack there are also egg waffles on the menu to go with your drink.

title: Prime Burgers & Smokehouse
label: Restaurant
text: Stockholm-based Prime Burger has several restaurants in inner-city Stockholm. Besides juicy burger (vegetarian or vegan options available, as well) they also serve smoked meats such as baby back ribs, beef brisket and pork belly.

title: Vasaparken
label: Park
text: Vasaparken is located in the middle of the Vasastan-district, close to both S:t Eriksplan's and Odenplan's subway stations. The park is a beloved oasis for inner-city Stockholmers and has a soccer pitch, jungle gym, and a green lush environment that received the Siena Prize in 2007; Architects Sweden's award for landscaping. In other words, there are lots of places for a picnic or an ice cream break. During winter there's an ice skating rink located here.At Vasaparken's northeastern end you'll find Astrid Lindgren's terrace, close to Dalagatan where she lived.  Dalagatan which, by the way, movie buffs probably recognize from the Swedish Noir classic The Man on the Roof. Adjacent to the park you'll also find Sven Harry's Art Museum.

title: Tegnérlunden
label: Park
text: Tegnérlunden was built in the 1940s and is a popular lunch spot for takeaway lunches during spring and summer. One of its defining traits is the large statue of playwright August Strindberg by Carl Eldh. But avid Astrid Lindgren-readers might also recognize the name since it's featured in several of her books. It's for example here that Bo Vilhelm Olsson lest out the genie that whisks him away to The Land of Far Away in Mio, My Son.

title: Skeppsholmen and Kastellholmen
label: Attraction
text: Skeppsholmen and Kastellholmen are two beautiful islands in the middle of Stockholm, joined together by a bridge. The easiest way to get here is just by taking a walk along Skeppsholmsbron or taking the public transport ferry from Slussen or Nybrokajen. The islands are probably best known for their museums and attractions; Moderna Musset, The Museum of Far Eastern Antiquities, and Stockholm Toy Museum are all found here. They're also great for a seaside walk, with a panoramic view of Östermalm, Djurgården, Södermalm, and Gamla Stan. And if you want to chill out for a bit, maybe enjoy a takeaway lunch from any of the cafés or restaurants here, Sveskuddsparken or Kastellparken offer a green oasis.

title: Glassverkstan
label: Coffee Shop / Café
text: Glassverkstan crafts its own artisan gelato in a former barn, now transformed into an ice cream bar. It was previously located at Skeppsholmen.

title: Victoria
label: Activity
text: Victoria on Götgatan had its premier screening in 1936, something that is evident in the cinema's well-preserved and beautiful interior by Ernst Grönwall. The movie theater has been renovated and modernized several times since opening night. The once one-screen cinema is today a multiplex with 8 screens and modern surround sound systems.

title: Grand
label: Activity
text: Grand on Sveavägen belonged to the Pentecostal Church in Stockholm, before being bought and turned into a movie theater by cinema magnate Anders Sandrew in 1933. Although it's been modernized several times in the following years, some of the cinema's design details have been left untouched. Like the ornate intarsia doors leading into the main auditorium. Grand is also infamous as the cinema where prime minister Olof Palme watched The Mozart Brothers, before being murdered on February 26 in 1986.

title: Pang Pang Taproom
label: Bar
text: Pang Pang has been making IPA, stout, and lager since 2010 and was one of the first microbreweries to gain traction during the Swedish beer renaissance of the 2010s. In the summer of 2021, Pang Pang opened a small taproom in its Hökarängen brewery, serving beer and ice slush to drink and dumplings to chow. The bar is open Friday-Sunday during the spring and summer seasons. Pang Pang also runs a restaurant in Hornstull that is open all-year round!

title: Upplevelsemuseet – Museum of Experiences
label: Museum
text: The Museum of Experiences has collected odd and unique objects from around the world. In this interactive exhibition you'll be able to taste, touch and smell them! Experience the animal kingdom's most notorious smell, get a taste of the food of tomorrow and feel the pricks of hundreds of small nails of an Indian nail mat.

title: Aryam
label: Coffee Shop / Café
text: Award-winning ice cream parlor Aryam was founded by Hosanna Amanuel, a pastry chef and baker by trade, in 2020. Since then it has served tasty Italian-style gelato, made from fresh ingredients.

title: Ascaro Padel & Social Club
label: Activity
text: Ascaro Padel is located in central Stockholm, on the rooftop of the NK department store’s parking complex. The experience offers more than just padel. You can start your visit with a workout in the outdoor gym, run a few laps on the track, and wrap up with a drink at the rooftop bar. You can also enjoy the new sauna and cold plunge, or simply relax with a drink in hand while taking in the view

title: We Are Padel Täby
label: Activity
text: At We Are Padel (WAP) in Täby, north of Stockholm, you can book a court to play a match with your friends, or a training session with a professional padel coach to get better at your game.

contact.address: We Are Padel Täby, Galoppvägen, Täby, Sweden,  Täby
contact.label: wearepadel.com

title: Chiôi
label: Restaurant
text: Chiôi is a popular Vietnamese expression that roughly means “hey, sister!”. Its menu consists of traditional and homey Vietnamese cuisine ­– like Pho-soup and Bánh Xèo-crêpes – and many of the recipes have been passed down through generations, from grandmothers to mothers.

title: Le Petit Cochon
label: Restaurant
text: Le Petit Cochon is a bistro in the french mold, located on Norrtullsgatan in Vasastan. The menu strives to be playful, unexpected and features delicacies from not only France but southern Europe in general.

title: Kajen Padelcenter
label: Activity
text: Kajen Padel is an open-air padel facility, open during the summer months. The courts are located by the shores of Nacka Strand and offer exercise with a great view of Lake Mälaren. Nacka Strand can be reached by taking the bus from Slussen or a commuter ferry from Nybrokajen.

title: PDL Center Frihamnen
label: Activity
text: PDL Center Frihamnen is one of Stockholm's largest padel facilities, with 22 indoor and 6 open-air courts. The facility also offers various group training sessions, junior padel courses and regularly hosts professional matches.

title: Man in the Moon
label: Bar
text: Popular gastropub Man in the Moon has one of Stockholm's largest selections of beer; 650 different kinds of which 30 are on tap. There's also a large selection of whiskey with around 110 single malts to chose from. Hungry guests can expect a menu that mixes Swedish classics – like Beef Rydberg and potato pancake – with international favorites.

title: Skepparholmen Nacka
label: Activity
text: Skepparholmen was built in its current functionalist form in 1964, as a corporate conference center for the Swedish Savings Bank Association. Nowadays it’s a hotel with spa and fitness areas. Chose from a range of fitness sessions, either with an instructor or by yourself, or enjoy a refreshing treatment or calming bath.

contact.address: Franckes väg, Saltsjö-boo, Sweden, S-132 39 Saltsjö Boo
contact.label: skepparholmen.se

title: Smådalarö Gård Hotell & Spa
label: Activity
text: Smådalarö Gård is a hotel and spa, just 50 minutes south of central Stockholm. There are several relaxing treatments to enjoy, a pool area and sauna, yoga, and fitness classes. Smådalarö Gård also has two open-air padel courts, tennis courts, and a nine-hole golf course open during the summer months.

title: Fågelbrohus
label: Activity
text: Fågelbrohus is located on Värmdö, in the inner archipelago, and offers rest and relaxation in serene surroundings. Besides a pool, sauna, various treatments, and classes, Fågelbro also has an open-air padel court and is just a short walk away from the Fågelbro golf course.

title: Hotell Havsbaden
label: Activity
text: Located just a stone's throw from the sea, Hotell Havsbaden is a spacious hotel and spa in the northern Stockholm archipelago. The spa has 13 pools - both indoor and open-air pools – several saunas, a gym, and offers various treatments, classes, and spa experiences.

title: Blå+
label: Restaurant
text: When Liljevalchs opened its new annex in 2021, the art hall also inaugurated its new museum restaurant Blå+. Blå+ is a branch of the classic Djurgården eatery Blå Porten. Unlike its older sibling, Blå+ is a wholly vegetarian experience though, with a new menu of green and organic dishes every week.

title: Vinterviken padel
label: Activity
text: Just a short walk from Vinterviken's garden café you'll find three open-air padel courts, maintained by the city of Stockholm. The courts are free to use but have no booking system. In other words, players take turns on the courts and make sure everybody gets to play.

title: VREX Bromma
label: Activity
text: VREX in the northern suburb of Bromma is a state-of-the-art experience center. Bring three friends and venture out on either action-packed romps or adventurous dungeon treks with the latest in VR technology. A 400 sqm room, equipped with motion trackers, lets you move about freely for a truly immersive game experience.

title: Kappa Bar
label: Bar
text: Kappa Bar is an e-sport bar, regularly showing games and tournaments in the most popular e-sport games – like CS: GO, Dota2, and League of Legends – on big screens TVs. If you'd rather play than watch they also have several gaming PCs and a VIP corner with Playstation and Xbox consoles. Kappa also hosts regular pub quizzes about games, film, and tv-shows.

title: DIS Inredning
label: Shop
text: After many years in the design -and fashion industry, Gabrielle Jangeby started her own boutique at Sturdeplan; DIS Inredning. DIS Inredning stocks its own collection of furniture, carpets, lamps, and accessories as well as handpicked items from some of the world's most innovative designers and brands.

title: Svensk Hemslöjd
label: Shop
text: The association Svensk Hemslöjd ("Swedish handicrafts") was founded in 1899 to preserve and document traditional handicrafts from all over Sweden. At their boutique on Norrlandsgatan, you'll find many beautiful examples of traditional craftsmanship and unique items made from traditional materials.

title: Yellow Korner
label: Shop
text: Art boutique specializes in high-quality prints of beautiful photographs to decorate your home with. At their Stockholm location, as well as a web shop, you'll find pictures by both legendary photographers and contemporary talents.

title: Bobergs Matsal
label: Restaurant
text: Classic Bobergs Matsal was architect Ferdinand Boberg's last project before his retirement.
